## H. HAND-OFF — READ THIS FIRST (what to do, in order, how to test, how to read the results, when to promote)

**Reading budget (the whole file is ~150k tokens; do not read it end to end):** read section H (this, ~12k tokens) and S5.16–S5.24 (the last ~9k tokens, the current state). Everything else is the record — open a section only when H cites it for the work at hand (`grep -n "^### S" LEDGER_SANDBOX_v2.md` lists them). The old/ files are for citations, not reading.

### H.0 Standing rules (owner's, all binding; break one and the work is wasted)
1. **Quota stop:** all work stops at 98 % of the WEEKLY quota (not the session's). All test results must land before that. Only the owner overrules. Ask the owner for the figure at every status point.
2. **The owner's eyes decide, not metrics.** No artifact class exists for a decision until the owner has SEEN it rendered in colour, zoomed, with and without the change. Send renders first (SendUserFile), numbers after. Never luma-only renders; every eye check = colour render + amplified |decode − source| per plane + per-row error profile (`harness/eye_flat.py`, `eye_diff.py`, `rowphase.py`).
3. **Consult the ledger before every tool, build, arm or claim:** `grep -n -i "<terms>" Codec/Current/LEDGER_*.md` and `ls .work/sandbox/harness`; cite the sections you rely on BEFORE the work. Never answer "why is X still there" from memory; run the ledger's method and quote it. Never answer "it's rate" without the evidence (S3.34 shows how that is proven, and S3.10/S3.19 how the owner reacts to the bare claim).
4. **Smudge detection = the owner's method:** level map (mean signed error per LL-support block) minus the source's, dense red/blue groupings = smudges (`harness/smudgegroups.py --thr 6 --dens 0.4`), plus `artifactmap.py` (sect.50.7) and `strongmap.py --ref` (classes WASH / SMUDGE / BOTH / RATE). Never blotch counts alone.
5. **No opt-in trade-offs:** broadcast has no switch-flipper; graphics and camera share a screen; adaptivity must be automatic per slice. Env levers are for PROBES; a promoted change is default-on with no switch.
6. **FPGA first:** integer math, sub-1 ms including conversion, memory incl. DDR jitter; account every change in those terms (S2.8 style).
7. **Structural work in a sandbox tree** (`.work/sandbox/sbx_*`), never in the current tree (`.work/v54tree`); promotion only through a train script with gates (H.4).
8. **Owner bar (2026-09-02):** zero flat textured blocks at ≥ 0.5 bpp up to 4K (≥ 1.0 above 4K), every cell/plane; measured by `flatplane.py` (FLAT column).
9. **Normative (decoder) changes must be reported to the owner as such** with a minor bump; **kept-as-fallback engines get [LEGACY-REPAIR] markers + inventory**.
10. **Deferred formats:** 16-bit / 4:0:0 / 4:4:4:4 measurement deferred until after Task G (owner 2026-09-01).
11. **Plain-English status to the owner;** details in the ledger. Report faithfully: failures with the output, skipped steps as skipped.
12. Two-sided probes: in-loop levers (freeze table sect.11.5c: OMC_FILLDIV, FILLREACH, ANTSGATE, XSL_*) are decoder-frozen; probe them via the `_X` aliases read after the freeze (sbx_probe8 / sbx_tctx). **Declare env levers near the top of codec.c** (declaration-order build failures cost three relaunches today). **Never launch arms before a successful build** (`make …; echo $?`, then `strings omc_enc | grep LEVER`).
13. `pkill` patterns: bracket the first letter (`"[h]_foo.sh"`) AND make them specific — a loose pattern today killed the owner's own `watch_resumes.sh` (§H.9) and, twice, the monitor shell.

### H.4 How to test (the exact commands; every result line format is what the ledger tables quote)
- Build a tree: `cd .work/sandbox/<tree> && make -j8 omc_enc omc_dec test_unit test_tf > build.log 2>&1; echo $?` — run `./test_unit` (RCT bijective, config validator, DWT) and `./test_tf`; verify a lever is in the binary with `strings omc_enc | grep OMC_LEVER`.
- Encode/decode: `omc_enc -i src.yuv -o x.omc -w W -h H --fmt 422|444 --depth 8|10|12 --bpp R -n 12 [--refresh none|N] [--refresh-req f:s[-s2]] [--lossless] [--gamut-strict 0]` (`OMC_GM_LATT=1` in the scripts is now redundant in sbx_dcbias/sbx_mv — default ON since S5.23 — but still needed for `sbx_temporal_c` and the probe trees); `omc_dec -i x.omc -o y.yuv [--lose f:s[-s2]] [--cdr]`.
- The standard cell line: `bash harness/cell_measure.sh TAG SRC DEC W H FMT DEPTH NF OMC` → `SCELL … NEG= BLOTCH[…] FLATF2[…] AM[…] LEVEL[…] TEXLOSS_F2[…] STRONG_F2[…] … LVLGRP_F2[…]`.
- NEG only: `bash harness/negscore.sh SRC DEC W H FMT DEPTH NF | tail -1`. Per frame: `harness/negframes.sh`.
- Colour cast / signed bias (3 lines): per plane `mean(decode − source)` in codes; the snippet is in `h_dc_gamut.sh` (`bias()`); any |mean| > 0.2 code on a plane is a cast (S5.18).
- Generation chains: `h_dc_chains.sh` pattern (CDR: `--cdr-in --display-w/h`, decode `--cdr`; baseband: plain decode re-encoded; PASS = gen g pixels byte-equal to gen g−1 from gen 2 on).
- Task C recovery: `h_dc_recover.sh TAG CLIP BPP "3:30-31" "5:29-35"` → per-frame differing slices; PASS = "none" from the request frame on (RC2 form). The RC1 form (request only the lost slices) leaves the chain wrong forever — that is the documented behaviour, not a failure of the tree.
- Closed loop: `omc_loop -i src -w -h --bpp -n 16 --lose "3:30-31,8:5-20" --refresh none --rtt 2` (S4.5).
- Eye renders: `h_dc_render.sh` pattern (BT.709 from YCbCr, source / A / B side by side, most-chromatic crop ×2, error map ×40 on mid-grey); Read the PNG yourself before sending; then SendUserFile.
- Owner's smudge method: `python3 harness/smudgegroups.py SRC DEC W H FRAME OUTDIR --sh SH --fmt FMT --thr 6 --dens 0.4` (groups/blocks/largest per plane) and `harness/amsum.sh` (artifact map areas).

### H.5 How to read the results (the traps that cost hours today)
- **VMAF-NEG saturates at 100 on soft/blurred sources** (soccer inter frames) → use PSNR there (S5.3). **NEG does not see a 2 dB per-plane deficit** (S5.16: OMC 4:4:4 vs XS equal NEG, −2 dB on every plane) → always report per-plane PSNR beside NEG.
- **A NEG gain bought by trading planes is not a gain** (S5.12 chroma rung +2: +1.8 NEG, −1.5 dB Cb/Cr).
- **"No difference" arms**: `omc_enc --no-fill` is inert in T5 (use `OMC_FILLTHR=9999`); decoder-frozen levers (sect.11.5c) silently do nothing when set from the encoder side — use `_X` aliases.
- **A metric can move while the eye sees nothing** (black class: owner 16:50 "there is no difference. leave as-is" on the 0.5 and 1.0 bpp renders — ruling text after S3.36 in the old S3 file ~line 241; numbers S3.28) and the eye can see what the metric hides (colour cast +1 code, S5.18). Both directions happened today.
- **Frozen clips overstate static cameras** (identical noise each frame, S5.20).
- **Level-group counts (owner's smudge measure) and STRONG classes** go DOWN with a real fix even when NEG dips (cf_gfx in S5.18) — read them together.
- Timestamps: write the machine clock (`date`), not an estimate (several corrections today).
- **Generation exactness (S5.32):** a grain-fill change is safe only as a change of UNITS; caps/clamps/floors on the derived gain break the T5 prefix-budget induction at any placement. Gate every fill-amplitude change on the CDR chain (baseband can pass while CDR fails) and run the early detector: per-slice payload bits gen 1 vs gen 2 — any slice spending more at gen 2 is a failure in waiting.
- **Harness (S5.34/S5.35):** check exit codes and file sizes before any `cmp`; a failed run must never become a number; normative probe levers must be set on the DECODER too in chain scripts; check plan churn between the two arms compared (plan-freeze); cross-validate anything trained; reconcile modelled totals against the real stream size.
- **Generation invariance (S5.36):** a per-slice encoder choice that changes the reconstruction must be reproducible from data the NEXT generation sees; transmitting it is not sufficient. Run the gen1-vs-gen2 bits detector WITH the shipped arm as control.
- **Mechanism claims (S5.32):** "X causes Y" needs the probe that separates the paths, never one switch that removes the symptom.

### H.6 Falsified register (what did NOT work, why; full text in `old/OLD_LEDGER_SANDBOX_S3_falsified_full_text.md` and the cited sections)
| lever | what was tried | result | why it failed / what it taught | where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| calm-kill texture gate | kill the calm rule where texture is high | no smudge change, NEG loss | the median was zero (edge LL cells never receive positions) → count only receiving cells; the class was not calm's | S3.7 |
| global chroma fill divisor 2 (chroma only) | halve chroma fill everywhere | removes speckle but re-opens chroma flatness on smooth cells | fill-vs-flatness conflict is per region → luma-gated chroma fill instead (S3.20, post-C) | S3.18 |

## S0. Why this track exists — the structural findings from the full read of LEDGER_v5_3

Recorded 2026-09-01 after reading all 56,598 lines of `LEDGER_v5_3.md` (notes:
`.work/notes_disk/LEDGER_v5_3_READ_NOTES.md`). These are the things in how OMC is built
that look structural rather than incidental, worst first, each with the record that
supports it. They are the candidates for replacement; none is a decision yet.

| # | what | evidence in the v5.3 record |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Picture legality by iteration.** The in-gamut repair codes a slice, tests every pixel for legal range, shrinks coefficients, and re-codes the WHOLE slice — up to 12 passes, plus a converging restart, plus an unbounded redo. | §51 (the wash mechanism is the repair's LL edits), §51.18.6 (basis table: LL is the only non-zero-mean basis), §74 (repair = 65–72 % of encode time; re-runs all 30 bands after touching ~10; v5 is 59 % slower than v4.14 with fill off), §67.6 (repair's fill veto = the flatness), §78.9/78.10 (veto is a convergence device), §45.9/45.10 ("the binding constraint is the replan"), B3.7f (repair OFF + decoder clip is exact by design on the coded-domain path). |
| 2 | **Exactness by hand-mirrored search.** Generation exactness rests on a candidate-plan search plus a verifier that must mirror every live decision rule by hand. | TEMPORAL_T5 5.5.4/5.5.6, §62, §67.11, §68.8, v5.4 B5.5 — four breaks of the same class, each found only by a chain failing downstream; §75.5 rule 2. |
| 3 | **The grain fill invents texture that must then survive re-encoding byte-exactly.** | §78.11 (crawl is 100 % the fill by elimination; constant amplitude fails A4 three ways at G-T5-CALM2a/b; position churn is bounded by the A5 refresh), §67 (veto ↔ flatness), §55.7 (one knob moves four artifacts in opposite directions), §67.3 (the metric rewards removing it). |
| 4 | **Slice geometry bakes in the seam and the smudge shape.** 16-row slices × two vertical wavelet levels → 4-row level blocks (a wash reads as a bar); the vertical 5/3's last pair degenerates at the slice bottom (row replication = the chroma seam); the 720p 8-row rung is consistently worst; several shipped rules key on slice height to compensate; the boundary blend cannot be widened without paying in wash. | §55.2, §55.7, §55.8d, §59.1, §80.4, §51.18.6 point 4. |
| 5 | Smaller: the entropy context never looks at the previous frame though both ends hold it (§77, §81 — but §81's measured ceiling is small); the slice header is exactly full at 352 bits (§64.7); refresh slices sit at their hard budget so one byte starves them (§B5.5); motion is derived from committed frames only, which protects exactness but limits high motion (§48.3). | as cited |

**Decision taken with the owner (2026-09-01):** the baseline track lands its in-flight
exactness fix and its instrument work, then PAUSES its remaining knob-tuning items (kept as
the documented fallback queue in LEDGER_v5_3_5). This track proceeds in the order:
step 0 (read), step 1 (legality by construction, replacing the repair loop), step 2 (the
texture engine, re-judged once the repair is gone), step 3 (exactness by construction,
expected to fall out of step 1), slice geometry last and only if the seam cannot be closed
otherwise. **Constraints that apply in full to any replacement:** unlimited generation
byte-exactness on baseband AND coded-domain paths; sub-1 ms including resolution
conversion, measured on the FPGA model never in C; exact CBR; one default for all footage;
royalty-free vintage only; C1–C8 and A1–A5 of PROJECT_CONSTRAINTS.

**Standing rule added 2026-09-02 (owner):** think FPGA at every step — the math must be
hardware-realisable, latency including resolution conversion stays under 1 ms, memory
including external DDR jitter is managed. Every S2 entry therefore states arithmetic class,
worst-case work as a COUNT, added reach/buffers, and memory before any quality number.

**Why this is the finding-1 answer and not another knob:** nothing in the step is a property
of the iteration — no shape, no factor, no escalation schedule, no fallback ladder, no
content classifier, no per-slice adaptation. The only numbers are geometry-derived (the
allowance scales with the LL block height) or hard limits (move cap). The exactness argument
is unchanged: the emitted values are lattice points, the reconstruction is `q<<s` (+ prediction),
the trigger is false at generation 2, and the gate suite passes with the step on (97 ok).

### S2.11a — The exactness argument for the step, stated once

1. **What is emitted is an ordinary lattice point.** Every move sets a coefficient's source
   value to `dequant(q') (+ prediction)` with `q' = q ± 1`; the ordinary quantiser maps that
   value back to `q'` exactly (the deadzone test `16·|c| < 9·2^s` is false at `|c| = 2^s`, and
   the calm kill's strict `|c| < 2^s` is false there too), so the emitted symbol is `q'` and the
   decoder reconstructs `q' << s` (+ prediction) — the same rule as for any other coefficient.
   Both `coef` and `dcoef` are written consistently (`dcoef = value − pcoef`), so the band
   reconstructs the same value whichever mode the emission picks.
2. **The fill is never contradicted.** A move to `q' = 0` inside a band whose fill bit is set is
   not a candidate, so no position the search assumed to be zero is later painted by the fill;
   a move from `q = 0` to `±1` replaces a fill value by a lattice value, which the decoder does
   identically (fill applies only at `q = 0`).
3. **Generation 2 is a no-op by construction.** The trigger is "the committed picture leaves the
   legal range". A generation-2 encoder's input is a committed picture the step (or the repair)
   already placed inside the range, so the count is zero, the step does not run, and the
   lock reproduces the slice. This is the §12.22.3e rule ("a correction must be a no-op at
   generation 2") satisfied by the trigger, exactly as the shipped repair satisfies it — the
   step adds nothing generation-dependent. The gates that assert it (G-T5-GAMUT2b, CUT3,
   CALM2a/2b, the RESTORE and SPEND gates) pass with the step on (97 ok).
4. **Determinism.** Fixed candidate order, integer ranking (cross-multiplied gains and costs in
   64-bit), integer estimate table measured once per geometry through the codec's own inverse,
   no wall-clock, no randomness. G-T5-GAMUT5b/5c/5e (same-process re-encode, byte-identical,
   identical internal path) pass with the step on.
5. **The declared CDR input stands the step down** (`!e->cdr_input`), the same declaration the
   repair uses (§12.22.4).
6. **What it does not promise:** closure of every slice. A slice the step cannot close (7 of
   211 at 720p, 2 of 130 on the graphics clip, none on either 1080p cell in run 7) falls
   through to the unchanged shipped repair, whose convergence guarantee is untouched. So
   `oob = 0` at the end of every slice is exactly as guaranteed as before, and the picture is
   never worse than the shipped path on the slices the step does not touch — only the causal
   bit bank those slices see differs, which the full train measures.

### S2.14 (parts 4–5) — What the final-build train found, and the three mechanisms behind it (2026-09-02 08:42)

Final-build train (form-4 guard + row-0 margin 2×cap): battery 52 cells identical bytes — NEG up on
11, down ≤0.03 on 3; 1080p 4:2:2 @0.5 worst block **+19 / 0 / 0 / 0** (shipped −71 / 30 / 3 / 4),
4K @0.5 **+22 / 5 / 0 / 1** (−47 / 67 / 2 / 3), 720p @0.5 **−59 / 284 / 13 / 5** (−117 / 600 / 105 / 20),
cf_gfx **+173 / 422 / 35 / 13** (+233 / 605 / 126 / 12); crawl within 0.11 on every plane; gates 97 ok.
**One cell regressed:** 4:4:4 10-bit @0.5, worst −144 / 33 / 13 / 16 against the shipped −72 / 31 / 7 / 5,
all from one slice (f0 s62). Three things were learned on it, each measured:

1. **The margin reserve fires on closed slices at barriers.** The 2×cap row-0 margin (part 2) made
   s62 need more moves than the cap; reverting to cap and instead disarming v5.1's margin reserve
   (`omc_gm_loopneed`) for a slice the step closed (`latt_closed`) fixes the 4K frame-0 case just
   as well (worst +19.8, no blocks past 20) and is the principled form: the barrier blend is
   display-only and the in-loop edit is off, so a blended sample inside the cap has no downstream
   consequence. `[S2-STEP]` gate added at the reserve's condition.
2. **A bounded lowpass last resort is FALSIFIED on this slice class.** s62 is a dense, deep excursion
   (221 samples, up to 206 codes past the rail, at the coarsest plan Q9/ns0). Single-step detail
   moves reach a dead end under every guard form (445 moves over three rungs). A fourth rung with
   LL moves bounded to 8 codes does not close it; sized by the measured need it closes with 1,284
   moves and washes WORSE than the shipped fallback (−179 / 68 / 34 / 47 against −144 / 33 / 13 / 16).
   Kept as `OMC_GM_LATT_LLMAX` (default 0 = off).
3. **The real cause of s62's plan: the step's two-direction moves on EARLIER slices cost bits.** The
   shipped arm codes s62 at Q8/ns1 (1,945 bytes); the step arm's earlier slices spent 1,056 bits
   more (moves from q = 0 to ±1 add symbols), which at the causal prefix bound pushed s62 over a
   plan-rung cliff to Q9/ns0 (1,169 bytes) — and at that rung the overshoot is 206 codes deep
   and nothing gentle can close it. This is the rung-granularity floor the record already names
   (HALF-RUNG, v5.3 §38.4) seen from a new side. **Change: the first rung is reduction-only** (moves
   toward zero never add a symbol and so never starve a later slice); two-direction moves are
   the second rung. Re-measuring four cells at 12 frames before the train is re-run.

### S2.14 (part 6) — The hard slice explained, and the build frozen for the final train (2026-09-02 08:43)

Reduction-only first rung: no change on s62 (still Q9/ns0 at pass 0). The direct comparison
settles it: in the SHIPPED arm s62 starts at Q8/ns1 with 69 samples out, 78 codes deep; in the
step arm it starts at Q9/ns0 with 221 out, 206 deep. The step arm's slices 0–61 spent 1,056 bits
more, because the shipped repair's harsh cuts on THOSE slices (39 of them fell back to the harsh
rule in the shipped arm) removed energy and bytes, and the causal bank handed the savings to
s62 — enough to lift it over a plan rung. The step keeps the earlier slices' picture, so s62
lands one rung coarser, its overshoot triples, and nothing gentle can close a 206-code
excursion at that rung; the shipped fallback then washes it (−144). Net for the cell: NEG +0.16,
47 slices better, one slice worse. **This is the plan-granularity floor (HALF-RUNG, v5.3 §38.4)
and the rail-aware planning idea (S1.9) seen from a new side; it is a plan-level item, not a
legality-step item, and is the next structural candidate after step 1 lands.**

**Build frozen for the final train:** four-rung ladder (reduction-only form 4 → two-direction
form 4 → form 3 → no guard), margin = the encoder's own gm_need window, the margin reserve
disarmed after a constructive closure, lowpass rung present but off, cap 128 per rung, exact
per-band impulse table, integer ranking. Byte-identical to v5.3 with the step off. Full train
running (battery, crawl, chains, gates) on exactly this build.

### S2.18 — Accounting and the promotion recommendation

Work per firing slice (12 frames @0.5, all planes): median 8–16 plane inverses, p90 19–108,
p99 43–318, max 78–638 (the ladder's retries multiply the tail; the 8-bit cell has the most
wrong estimates, 2,938, because the Q12 table rounds small 8-bit steps to zero — a Q16 table
is the obvious fix and is queued). Every move is an integer lattice step; every verify is one
inverse of one plane; memory is one coefficient buffer and three pixel buffers per plane of one
slice; no lookahead, no new DDR traffic, no latency term. The tail must be bounded in hardware
by an inverse cap (`OMC_GM_LATT_INVMAX`, built, unmeasured) — measured in the promotion cycle.

**Recommendation: PROMOTE.** The step improves or holds every measured column on 51 of 52 cells
at identical bytes, removes the deep-smudge class on every 1080p format and on 4K at 0.5 bpp,
cuts it 8× at 720p and 4× on graphics, leaves chroma, flatness, pitch and crawl unchanged, passes
every exactness gate and chain, and reduces the legacy repair to a labelled fallback that runs on
a small fraction of slices. The one regression (4:4:4 10-bit @0.5, one slice: −144 / 13 / 16
against −72 / 7 / 5) is the plan-granularity floor and is the first item of the next structural
step. Promotion runs as its own baseline cycle (`h_latt_promote_train.sh`), default ON, restore
incantation += `OMC_GM_LATT=0`, legacy code labelled and inventoried.

## S3 — STEP 2: TEXTURE AND FILL AT THE SURVIVAL DECISION (flatness and crawl)

Opened 2026-09-02 11:48, while step 1's promotion cycle runs in the current tree.
Working copy: the step-1 frozen build (`sbx_legality`) as the encoder; step-2 outputs in
`sandbox/sbx_texture/out/`. Reading order before any idea: S1.2 (§12.23 — fill measured a net
loss on the T5 corpus; calm kill pinned at |q| = 1; the refresh pulse is half the ants level),
S1.7 (v5.2: flatness was never a bit limit; NEG rewards flattening; the fill amplitude must key
on an invariant; the repair's fill veto), S1.12 (HVBC: the survival decision is the mechanism;
hard gates cliff; synthesis was the wax), the v5.3 ledger's fill record (100 % fill by
elimination; constant amplitude fails A4 three ways; position churn bounded by refresh).

### S3.1 — Measurement 1 (launched): the fill switched OFF entirely, on today's full gamut

The record's first question (S1.2): is the grain fill, as the codec stands today with the
legality step in front of the repair, still worth its cost? Arm F0 = step-1 build with
`OMC_FILL=0` (no fill anywhere, nothing else changed) against the same build with the fill on
(the S2.15 `latt` arm), 52 battery cells × 12 frames at identical bytes: NEG, per-plane blotch,
per-plane flatness at frames 2 and 11, pitch; plus crawl on the four frozen masters at three
rates, all planes. Driver `sandbox/h_step2_run1.sh`, log `sbx_texture/out/run1.log`, marker
`RUN1.done`. Whatever the answer, the next design (texture at the survival decision — what is
quantised to zero and how that decision is coupled across positions, per S1.12) is built only
after this table exists.

### S3.1 — Result: the fill switched off entirely (2026-09-02 12:34; `sbx_texture/out/run1.log`; 52 cells × 12 frames + 12 crawl cells, identical bytes)

| luma flat blocks @0.5 bpp (dng 1080p 4:2:2) | 0.07 % | **57.2 %** |
| Cb / Cr flat blocks @0.5 bpp (same cell) | 0 % / 0 % | **82 % / 85 %** |

This reproduces the record in one table (S1.2 §12.23.8: fill off is better on NEG and on the
ants tail; S1.7 v5.2: NEG rewards flattening; the fill is what keeps textured blocks from going
flat). Today, with the legality step in front of the repair, the grain fill is the ONLY thing
standing between the codec and a waxy picture at 0.5–1.0 bpp: without it more than half of the
textured luma blocks and nearly all textured chroma blocks are rendered flat, the score goes UP
by a tenth of a point while it happens, and crawl halves — because the crawl is the fill's
synthetic grain moving. Both halves of the crawl/flatness pair therefore live in one place:
the detail coefficients that do not survive quantisation at these rates, and the synthetic
texture painted where they were. The HVBC record (S1.12) says the same from the other side —
they never solved it and went waxy. Step 2's design must keep REAL texture alive at the
survival decision rather than repaint it.

**Measurement 2 (launched): attribute the flatness to the survival decisions.** At identical
bytes, fill ON, on five half-rate/1.0 cells: (a) deadzone off, (b) calm kill off, (c) both —
per-plane flatness, blotch, NEG, and crawl on the frozen masters. If the decisions (not the
quantiser step itself) account for a large share of the flat blocks, the design lever is
there; if not, the lever is the plan (which coefficients get the finer rung), which is the
same plan-level item as the hard slice of S2.14.

**Conclusion (falsifies the step-2 premise as I framed it):** the two zeroing decisions account
for 2–3 points of the 57 % flatness at 0.5 bpp and ~11 points at 1.0 bpp; the rest is the
quantiser step itself at the plan rung these slices get. The real detail of grainy footage does
not survive quantisation at half a bit per pixel in this transform at these rungs, so
"keep real texture alive at the survival decision" has almost nothing to work with; the
decisions are net positive as shipped (score, smudge, crawl) and are not the lever.

**What this leaves for flatness and crawl, from the record (S1.2, S1.7, v5.3 §68/§78.11–78.12):**
1. Texture at these rates is the fill, and the fill stays. Its crawl is (a) amplitude churn
   because the quantiser shift moves with rate control (constant amplitude fails A4 three ways —
   falsified), and (b) position churn because the set {coded to zero} changes — 69 % of it forced
   by the A5 rolling refresh (immovable by any encoder rule; MODESTICK/LATCHMODE/FILLSTILL
   falsified). The record's one untried structural route: remove the SCHEDULED refresh —
   refresh on demand with drift detection (the owner's Task C item, with the owner's hard
   constraints: no frame-store growth, no extra DDR access, hash fused into the committed-state
   write pass, patches as stream syntax, return path in the control plane). §12.23.3 already
   bounds the prize: refresh period 8 → 64 halves the ants tail on every plane; the rolling
   refresh also costs quality, not bits, so removing it is picture at the same rate.
2. Flatness at 0.5 bpp is the plan rung, the same mechanism as the hard slice of S2.14 —
   the plan-level item (rung granularity near rails and for textured bands; HALF-RUNG,
   v5.3 §38.4, designed not built).

**Re-plan of step 2, stated for the owner:** the texture/fill step becomes two builds with
measured prizes — (A) refresh on demand (temporal engine change; crawl −50 % bound; quality)
and (B) the plan-granularity build (flatness and the coarse-rung slices). Order: A first
(largest measured prize, owner-specified constraints already on record), then B. Step 3
(exactness by construction) and the slice geometry remain after.

### S3.4 — Scoping refresh on demand from the code (read, not designed; 2026-09-02 12:54)

Where the scheduled refresh lives (sandbox `src/codec.c`): the encoder forces slice s intra on
frames with `fidx8 % R == s % R` (line ~4856, normative on the wrapped 8-bit frame index); the
XSL barrier rules (d)/(e) at `xsl_prep` (~2298), the barrier display blend (~2203) and the
un-blend (`omc_xsl_unblend`, ~2336) all derive the SAME schedule from `fidx8` and `refresh_r`
on both ends; the fill/texture ratchet relaxes on the schedule (~6658); the refresh boost
(sect.48, ~4753) budgets bits on it. `refresh_r` is a stream-header byte, validator range
0..64 (0 = 8, 1 = stateless). The decoder's concealment (MC + spatial, ~9031) fills a lost
slice from neighbours' motion and never affects a clean decode.

What "refresh on demand" changes, minimally: (1) the barrier rules must key on the slice's
ACTUAL coding (all bands intra in the header's mode mask, which both ends already hold) instead
of the schedule — a normative change (stream minor bump) that keeps "derivable from the stream
alone" (C7/C8); (2) the encoder's refresh decision becomes: scheduled only when configured for
multicast joins, otherwise on request from the control plane; (3) hash-verified concealment:
a per-slice hash of the COMMITTED state written in the slice header, computed in the same pass
that writes the reference rows (owner constraint: no new store, no extra DDR), so a decoder
can tell whether its concealed state equals the encoder's and ask for a patch only when it
does not; (4) block-level patches as stream syntax (attachment points: the Q5 block structure
and per-band intra). The return path is control-plane API, not bitstream. The A2 latency
model is untouched (no rows, no buffers); the A5 recovery bound becomes "one round trip +
one slice" on demand and stays R frames when scheduled.

Order of build, each measured before the next: (a) barrier rules keyed on the mode mask +
encoder refresh policy with a control-plane request API (measures the crawl/quality prize on
clean links and the unchanged behaviour when R is configured); (b) the state hash; (c) the
patch syntax and the decoder's request. Measurement 4 (running) bounds (a)'s prize.

Attribution — four mechanisms, each now with an owner:

- **M1 — the calm kill** (the "ants fix": in a locally flat LL neighbourhood every grain-scale

  is textured — a flat-LL neighbourhood with grain-scale coefficients IS fine texture on a
  smooth surface (water, walls, upscaled 8K), exactly what the flatness bar protects.  Build:
  a source-texture gate on class 3 (encoder-only; candidate-narrowing, so the 12.23.7 lattice
  argument and A4 are untouched).

  representational: the fill amplitude `1<<(s-2-div)` in 8-bit codes cannot express the
  half-code amplitudes the 10-bit fill uses at the same picture level, so a band's fill is
  either absent (flat) or a full code (over-loud, the NEG cost).  Build: sub-code fill
  amplitude by DENSITY (the tile's ±1 applied on a fixed fraction of positions) — normative,
  decoder synthesis; scoped after M1.

  the fill amplitude is the mechanism; the S3.5 (iv) suspect (the fill's LL gate has a two-row
  support at sh = 8) is next to probe.
- **M4 — the 8K remainder**: 11.5 % after the calm kill; probe after M1 lands.

Note also that the deadzone-off and calm-off arms make the 8-bit cells WORSE (6.0 → 11.4 /
8.7): spending bits on ±1 coefficients starves the fill's bands; the flatness bar cannot be met
by spending, only by not zeroing texture (M1) and by an expressible fill (M2).

## S4 — TASK C IN THE SANDBOX: REFRESH ON DEMAND (tree `sandbox/sbx_temporal`, from the step-1 tree; owner: "please start your sandbox task c", 2026-09-02 13:02)

### S4.1 — Build (a): the scheduled wave in one place, refresh on request, no stream change (2026-09-02 13:12)

What was found on reading (corrects S3.4 point 1): the cross-slice boundary term d[-1] feeds the
TRANSFORM (three call sites), not only the display edit, so rule (d) changes the lattice of a
refreshed slice.  Keying rule (d) on the mode mask would therefore have made the generation-2
encoder — which does not see generation 1's requests — transform a slice differently from
generation 1 and lose exactness.  Resolution: **an on-demand refresh is an ordinary all-intra
slice**.  It keeps the boundary term, nothing in the stream marks it, the decoder's normative
logic is untouched, and generation 2 re-emits the intra-coded lattice picture exactly whether
it codes the slice intra or inter (the T5 lock, S2.16).  Only the SCHEDULED wave suppresses the
term (rules d/e), as today.  Consequence for recovery: a requested refresh heals a slice fully
when its predecessor's committed rows are already clean, so a contaminated run is requested as
one contiguous block and heals top-down in one frame.

Code (`[S3-REFRESH]` tags): `refresh_due(cfg, fidx8, s)` is the single definition of the wave and
replaces the seven hand-written `fidx8 % R == s % R` sites (display blend, xsl_prep ×2, un-blend ×2,
can_inter, fill ratchet; the refresh-boost arithmetic is guarded); `refresh_r = 255
(OMC_REFRESH_NONE)` = no scheduled wave (validator, header byte, decoder all accept it — it is in
the stream header so both ends derive "never due"); `omc_enc_request_refresh(e, first, count)` and
`omc_enc_refresh_pending(e)` (control-plane API; per-slice pending byte, consumed at commit);
`omc_enc --refresh none` and the test stand-in `--refresh-req f:s[-s2],...`.

First cell (cf_gfx 448×256 @0.5, 12 frames): default period → **byte-identical** to the step-1
tree (md5 00ab1528); `--refresh none` NEG 78.80 → 80.94 (the whole prize on a clean link with no
loss over 12 frames); `none` + requests reproducing the wave 78.75 (≈ default: the retained
boundary term is worth nothing measurable); `none` + whole-frame refresh at frames 0 and 6
78.29.  CBR bytes identical in all arms.  Full battery + crawl with `--refresh none` launched
next (S4.2); the loss-injection/recovery test needs a decoder loss hook (S4.3).

### S4.3 — Recovery on demand, measured (2026-09-02 13:31; `sbx_temporal/out/recover.log`, `h_c_recover.sh`; decoder loss hook `omc_dec --lose f:s[-s2]` zeroes the slices' bytes → sync resync → concealment)

`--refresh none`, 1080p 4:2:2 10-bit @1.0, 12 frames; slices 30–31 lost at frame 3; the lossy decode
compared with the clean decode per slice and frame (luma rows exact-equal test, chroma sample count):

| test | clip | request at frame 5 | damaged at frames 3–4 | from frame 5 on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RC1 | frozen dng (static) | 30–31 (the lost slices only) | 31, 32, 33, 34, 35 (max \|d\| 68) | **still 31–35, forever** |
| RC2 | frozen dng | 30–35 (the chain) | 31–35 | **exact, every slice, every frame** |
| RC3 | cityalley (moving) | 30–35 | 29, 30, 31, 32, 33 (max \|d\| 34) | exact |
| RC4 | cityalley | 26–41 (motion margin) | same | exact |

Findings: (1) **a lost slice damages the slices BELOW it in the same frame** through the cross-slice
boundary term chain (the decoder's inverse transform of slice k reads its own, wrong, rows of k−1):
four slices on the static clip, two on the moving one; the slice ABOVE differs only through the
display blend (RC3's slice 29).  Without a scheduled wave the damage never heals by itself (RC1);
under today's wave it lasts until each damaged slice's own scheduled refresh — which is the A5 bound
as documented, but the damaged AREA is 2–5 slices per lost slice, not one.  (2) A request that covers
the lost slice and the chain below it heals **exactly** in one frame (RC2–RC4): the requested slices
are plain all-intra, the top one reads a clean predecessor, and each next one reads the freshly
healed rows — the top-down argument of S4.1 holds on the picture.  (3) Motion spread over the
two-frame round trip did not reach beyond the chain on this content (RC4 = RC3); it is content
dependent, and the chain length is too — so the decoder must tell the encoder WHICH slices are wrong
rather than the encoder guessing a margin: that is build (b), the per-slice state hash.  Until (b),
the control-plane rule is "request the lost slice through the bottom of its chain plus a margin".

### S4.4 — Build (b) **[SUPERSEDED by S5.13: the header re-cut keeps the four region vectors; the hash now takes 16 of the 30 bits freed by 3-bit table-group ids]**: the per-slice state hash, landed (2026-09-02 13:33; tree `sandbox/sbx_temporal_b`, `promotion/apply_state_hash.py`; minor 13 → 14)

Design: the slice header carries the 16-bit hash (CRC-32 of the row bytes, all planes, low 16 bits)
of THIS slice's committed rows in the PREVIOUS frame.  Both ends compute it when they commit the
rows (on hardware the reference-write pass; nslices × 2 bytes on chip; no new store, no extra DDR
traffic); the decoder compares the header value with what it computed last frame and flags the
slice on mismatch; a slice that failed to decode is flagged at once.  Wire: T5 derives ONE vector
per slice and the header's four region vectors were always equal, so regions 1..3 (39 bits) are
reclaimed — one vector, the 16-bit hash, 23 reserved-zero bits; header size and every other field
unchanged.  `omc_dec_state_report()` hands the flags to a control plane; `omc_dec -v` prints them.
Exactness: generation 2 reproduces the committed pictures, hence the same hashes.

Result (cf_gfx @0.5, `--refresh none`): clean decode — no flag on any slice of any frame; slices
10–11 lost at frame 3 (the resync takes 12 with them) — frame 3 flags 10 11 12 immediately, frame 4
flags 10 11 12 13 (13 damaged through the boundary-term chain, S4.3, detected one frame later), and
the flags persist until healed.  So the decoder now knows the exact set to request — the chain and
motion spread included — and the "margin" of S4.3 is not needed.  Note for the record: hashing the
encoder's reference right after its reconstruction step mis-flagged ~70 % of slices on a clean
decode while rt = 0 held (`--recon` vs `--cdr` identical); the reference rows are modified later in
the slice encoder (between the reconstruction step and the return), so the hash is taken at the
slice's final commit point — on hardware the pass that writes the reference, which is that point.

|---|---|---|---|

| cf_gfx sh 8 | 25.7 26.1 25.4 27.5 24.3 28.3 28.0 **32.1** | +8 % | +23 % |

Reading: (i) the ODD rows are the vertical 5/3's highpass rows; at 0.5 bpp the vertical detail

last row of each slice carries the whole-sample-mirror degeneration (sect.57: the last vertical
highpass becomes a first difference) — the boundary-row fill cures its replication, not its error.
Both are properties of the vertical transform at slice granularity, not of any decision measured in
S3.5–S3.9; they are the seam/geometry item of the structural plan and are now measured with a
per-row instrument (a candidate must bring the odd/even excess and the last-row excess to the
interior level).  Cross-check at 2.0 bpp queued (rate dependence).

2.0 bpp odd rows carry +30 % luma and +40 % chroma error over even rows; the signed bias by parity
is ±0.3 codes (no brightness alternation), so it is error MAGNITUDE, not a line-pair tint.  A small
positive DC bias (+0.3..+1.4 codes, all planes, both rates: the decode is slightly brighter than the
source everywhere) is noted for the exactness/rounding track.

**Zoomed colour crops (`E8_720p_zoom_screen.png`, `E8_720p_zoom_keyboard.png`, 2×):** the tearing
the owner saw is visible as HORIZONTAL SMEAR AT SLICE PITCH — the speaker grille's dot rows and the
menu text rows are reconstructed with their vertical structure lost inside each 8-row slice and a
different vertical phase in the next slice, so the pattern shears at every slice boundary.  It is
the slice-geometry limit at 0.5 bpp and slice height 8 (A2 forces 8 at 720p): two vertical levels
over eight rows with a mirror boundary, vertical detail zeroed first.  Same mechanism at height 16,
weaker.  Measured retention of vertical vs horizontal detail follows (next entry).

**Vertical-detail retention by row (decoded vertical detail ÷ source's, luma, frame 2):**
720p @0.5 sh 8: **1.29** 1.07 1.13 1.02 1.14 1.01 1.07 **1.19** (overall 1.11; grille rows 1.22);
1080p @0.5 sh 16: **1.22** 1.03 1.05 0.98 1.07 0.97 … 0.98 **1.12** (overall 1.04);
1080p @2.0 sh 16: **1.00** 0.86 0.92 0.85 … 0.89 **0.96** (overall 0.90).
So the decode does not lose vertical detail overall at 0.5 — it ADDS it, and the excess sits on the
slice's first and last rows (+20–30 % over the interior at both heights, both rates): that is the
seam discontinuity — the row where one slice's vertically smeared reconstruction meets the next
slice's, and what the eye reads as a tear on the grille and the text rows.  The interior rows show
the odd/even alternation on top.  Instrumented now per row; the seam is the geometry item (the
XSL display cascade sect.55.8 is the only tool that touches it today and is measured next, two-
sided, as the first probe of that item).

### S4.6 — Heal-frame cost and the standing cost of the rota (2026-09-02 13:55; `sbx_temporal_b/out/loop2.log`; encoder luma PSNR vs source per frame, cityalley 1080p @1.0)

| arm | steady-state PSNR (frames 3–11) | heal frames |
|---|---|---|
| on demand, clean link | 47.6 dB every frame | — |
| on demand, losses at 3 and 8, round trip 2 | 47.6 | frame 5 (3 intra slices) 47.4; frame 10 (17 intra slices) 46.7 — one frame each, then 47.6 |
| **today's rota R = 8, clean link** | **47.0 every frame** | (9 intra slices every frame, by schedule) |

So the rota costs 0.5–0.6 dB on EVERY frame of a clean link, and on demand pays 0.2 dB for one frame
to heal a two-slice loss and 0.9 dB for one frame to heal a 16-slice burst.  The full-gamut NEG
prize of the clean link is measurement S4.2 (running).

**Rota amplification traced further:** the growth (34 → 231) is the same with freeze concealment
(so not the MC concealment) and with a single lost slice (31 alone: 4 slices damaged, 33 → 231);
without the rota the same damage holds at 32–33 for the whole clip.  The growth is therefore an
interaction between the scheduled refreshes of OTHER slices and the damaged ones — candidates are
the derived motion vector (the rota alters the committed pictures the vector is derived from, and a
vertical vector drags damaged rows through interpolation every frame) and the rules (d)/(e) at a
refreshed neighbour.  Open item, shipped behaviour; on demand heals before it matters, and the
control plane can be given the rota too.  Trace with OMC_DEBUG_MV next.

Luma pitch (dec-vs-src) and the per-row error (first / interior mean / last row of the slice):

| arm | 720p sh 8 @0.5 | 1080p sh 16 @0.5 | 1080p @2.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| shipped (casc 0, spread 0) | pitch 0.237; rows 14.8 / 15.6 / **19.3**; NEG 86.35 | 0.0905; 15.5 / 16.1 / **19.7**; 89.10 | 0.0869; 7.8 / 8.9 / **11.3**; 96.07 |

| cascade 2 | 0.213; same rows; 86.32 | 0.0846; same rows; 89.10 | 0.0909; same; 96.06 |

| cascade 1 + spread 2 | 0.189 | 0.0618; rows unchanged | 0.0732 |

Every display-side arm leaves the boundary rows' error exactly where it was (last row +23–30 %
over the interior in all 18 cells) while the pitch statistic falls by up to 40 %: the pitch
instrument measures the periodic RESIDUE the blend reshapes, not the seam's error, and the seam
the owner sees as tearing is the error.  So the seam is not a display matter.  It is the
reconstruction of the last rows of each slice — the degenerate last vertical highpass (first
difference under the whole-sample mirror) quantised on the same rung as everything else, and the
first row's dependence on the boundary term — and only a transform-level or allocation-level
change can move it (candidates for the geometry item: a finer rung on the boundary-row
coefficients, or a boundary handling that does not degenerate).  NEG is flat across the arms.

### S3.21 — The luma part of the grille smudge: rate and geometry sized on the owner's boxes (2026-09-02 14:12; `sbx_texture/out/hist/grille_levers.log`, 3 frames, diagnostic arms)

| arm | NEG | grille luma \|err\| | grille HP energy dec/src | grille HP correlation | rest \|err\| / HP ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shipped @0.5, 8-row slices | 83.6 | 39.7 | 0.70 | 0.59 | 14.4 / 1.02 |
| @0.5, 16-row slices (A2-violating, diagnostic) | 86.4 | 38.0 | 0.96 | 0.66 | 16.2 / 1.27 |
| @0.75 | 90.0 | 28.7 | 0.99 | 0.74 | 12.2 / 1.03 |
| @1.0 | 92.5 | 22.5 | 0.96 | 0.80 | 10.4 / 0.98 |

The 16-row slices give the grille its texture energy back (0.70 → 0.96) but not its pattern (corr
0.66) and make the dark-background speckle worse (rest HP ratio 1.27); the smudge in the eye's
sense is still there.  Half a bit more per pixel (0.75) is what makes the grille read right (HP
ratio 0.99, corr 0.74, error −28 %).  So the luma grille smudge at 0.5 bpp is a rate deficit ON THAT
PART OF THE PICTURE — and S3.19 showed the top quarter of the same frame spending 15 % under its
nominal bytes at rung 7 while the grille slices sit at rung 8–9.  A content-following slice budget
under exact CBR (the frame's bytes are fixed; their split across slices is not) is the lever for
the luma part; it is the plan-granularity/allocation structural item, and its acceptance test is
the owner's grille boxes on this frame.  Chroma part: the luma-gated fill (S3.20, sweep running).
Allocator read (`codec.c` ~4705–4790, OMC_ALLOC = 1 default): each slice's wire spend is CAPPED at
its previous-frame detail-energy share of the frame (max of luma and chroma shares), clamped to
[0.75 B, 1.5 B]; calm slices bank what they leave under their cap, busy slices may draw the bank
up to 1.5 B.  On the 720p frame the calm top slices still spend 0.85 B (their fine rung fits under
the cap and the search takes it) and the grille slices reach only 0.94–1.2 B before their rung has
to coarsen — the bank is fed by the 0.75 B floor, which protects the calm slices' own flatness.
So the lever is a real trade inside a fixed frame: bits for the grille come from the screen
background, whose flatness the bar also covers.  0.5 bpp on this frame is short of bits by about
half a bit per pixel where the picture is busy; the honest routes are coding efficiency (the
structural items) and a budget that follows content by measured need rather than energy share —
both to be judged on the owner's grille boxes AND the background's flatness together.  The
allocator arithmetic is `double` (FPGA rule: integer) — noted for the rebuild.

### S3.29 — WHERE the black smudges are made: dark-rail excursions on the dark screen (2026-09-02 15:00; `OMC_GM_STAT=1`, 720p @0.5, frame 0)

The repair fires on 40 of 90 slices of the intra frame, slices 24–75 (rows 192–600: the laptop
screen), with 1–11 out-of-range samples per slice and excursions ("deep") of 7–85 codes at Q 8–9
(refinements 0–22).  The screen is a near-black UI with bright text and icons: the wavelet's
ringing around each bright element undershoots BELOW black, the legal-range test flags it, and the
repair's shrink — harsh where the excursion is 60–85 codes — darkens the surrounding patch.  That
is the owner's black smudge, made by the one mechanism, on the one kind of content (bright detail
on a black field) v4.14 did not repair.  Dark-rail undershoot is invisible on a signed, unclipped
pipeline until the single display clip (the HVBC-corroborated architecture of B3.7f); the repair
exists so that a LEGAL-RANGE BASEBAND hop reproduces the committed picture (A4 for baseband
chains).  So the black smudges are the price of baseband exactness on dark-field graphics — a
product decision to put to the owner with numbers: repair on vs off on this cell, NEG, dark class,
and the baseband-chain and CDR-chain results side by side.
**Cliff-only mask (mode 5, 15:05, `planmask_arms5.log`):** plans change in 5–10 % of slices, NEG
±0.01, dark class and harsh fallbacks unchanged (720p 6, 4:4:4 1).  The refine-mask line is closed:
free skipping costs NEG and breaks the lock, bounded skipping does nothing for the hard slices.
The hard slices are not a plan-cliff problem; they are dark-rail undershoot on dark-field graphics
(S3.29), and the question is whether the repair is needed at all under the clamp design
(baseband chain with the repair off: running).

### S3.30 — The repair is needed for BASEBAND exactness only (2026-09-02 15:10; `sbx_texture/out/hist/bbchain.log`, 720p @0.5, 3 generations)

| chain | repair on (shipped) | repair off (`--gamut-strict 0`) |
|---|---|---|
| CDR interchange (`genchain.sh`) | PASS | **PASS** |
| baseband interchange (`genchain_bb.sh`, legal-range display hop) | PASS (range 0..1023, oob 0) | **FAIL at generation 2** (committed range −120..1181, 2,655 samples out) |

So on this cell the CDR chain is exact without any repair, and the black smudges (S3.23, S3.29)
exist only to make the legal-range BASEBAND hop exact.  The decision is the owner's, and it is a
product decision, not a codec one: baseband exactness on dark-field graphics costs the black
smudges (repair on: dark 98 / 8 on the intra frame; off: 55 / 1 = v4's level) and 0.1 NEG on this
cell; CDR-only exactness (the interchange the ledger's B3.7f clamp design already ships) costs
nothing here.  Between the two: a repair that only closes the excursions a BASEBAND hop would
clip (the display range) with the least-damage step where it can and NO harsh rule — leaving the
rest to the CDR — is measured next: drift magnitude of the repair-off baseband chain per
generation (how far the unrepaired hop actually drifts), and the harsh rule disabled with the
gentle passes kept (dark class, oob, baseband chain).

### S3.31 — Unrepaired baseband drift is not small (2026-09-02 15:20; `sbx_texture/out/hist/bbdrift.log`, 720p @0.5, repair off, legal-range hops)

Generation 2 vs 1: 29 / 42 / 48 % of luma samples differ on frames 0 / 1 / 2, max 531 codes, mean
6.5–9.4 on the differing samples; generation 3: 32 / 45 / 54 %, growing.  A handful of clipped
samples breaks a slice's generation lock and the whole slice re-encodes lossy, so the loss is not
confined to the rails — it is the ordinary generation loss of a non-exact codec, on half the
picture by the second hop.  Baseband exactness therefore needs the committed picture in range,
and the repair (or a gentler one) stays.  The remaining question is the harsh rule (running).

### S3.35 — Owner's three questions (16:10): "have you gated the luma? why did v4.x not need more bits?"; "are you asking if I want black smudges???"; quota Fable 80 % / overall 41 %

**Luma fill on the grille, measured (`hist/lumafill.log`, 720p @0.5, 3 frames):** fill bits off in
both planes (OMC_FILLTHR=64): NEG 83.58 → **84.46**, grille |err| 39.7 → 35.0, detail kept 0.70 →
0.86, correlation 0.59 → 0.64, chroma |err| 23 → 12; the rest of the frame |err| 14.4 → 12.4.  So
on this cell the fill (luma and chroma) is a net loss on every instrument.  The luma fill IS gated
today — by LL activity (the ants gate, the sect.80 reach rule at slice height 8) — but the gate is
too loose for structured content; the reach/threshold sweep with the flatness bar beside it is
running (`hist/reachgate.log`).  (Tool note: `omc_enc --no-fill` produced a byte-identical stream —
the flag is inert in the T5 tree; the fill is controlled by the fill-bit threshold.)

**Why v4.14 did not need more bits:** it coded 720p in 16-row slices.  Forced to 8 rows, v4.14 has
the grille patches too (S3.24: bright share 6 % → 17 %) and loses 2.3 NEG.  v5 codes 720p at 8 rows
for the latency rule: `docs/LATENCY.md` — 720p50 at 16 lines is 0.945 ms codec-only (inside the
bar) but 1.140 ms with a conversion in the path under the shipped conversion charge, and uc_ratio
is advisory, so 8 is the default "that holds whatever the far end decides".  The same document
records the raster-clocked output converter, which cut every conversion charge (e.g. 1080p50 →
2160p50 at 16 lines 1.069 → 0.961 ms); the 720p50-at-16-lines-with-conversion figure under that
converter is not tabulated and is the number to compute.  If it is under 1 ms, 16-row slices at
720p are back on the table and are worth 2–3 NEG and most of the grille on this cell.

**Black smudges, from the record:** the owner ruled on 2026-09-01 (v5.4 B3.7f) that BOTH modes

## S5 — TASK C STATUS AGAINST THE PROMPT'S ITEMS (owner: "provide an update on Task C item statuses before proceeding to D", 2026-09-02 16:40)

### S5.1 — Item C3 reading, done by me in full (not delegated)

**`Issues_to_fix/20260830/Wavelet_temporal.txt`** (owner ↔ Opus 5): the temporal prediction is
already wavelet-domain (inter bands code coef − pcoef); the spatial-only part is the ENTROPY
CONTEXT (left/above, never the co-located previous coefficient).  v5.3 §81's census bounded a
temporal context at 6.7–8.5 % of category-symbol entropy on the ~30 % of symbols that can see pcoef,
against +148 KB of tables — "don't build"; Q5's skips already remove the most predictable
coefficients (66.6 % at 0.5 bpp, 82.8 % on cf_gfx) so the two compete for the same redundancy;
Q5's skip rate collapses at high rate (16.2 % at 2.0 bpp), so the honest revisit is §81's census
re-run at 2.0 and 4.0 bpp with the byte-inert instrument OMC_TCTX_STAT.  Constraints recorded there:
A5 reachability (69–74 % of symbols have no pcoef) and a new context needs its own trained table
(§64.7's −0.03 % lesson).  **Status: the instrument OMC_TCTX_STAT is not in the shipped tree
(0 hits in v54tree, v5.3 tree, clamptree) — it lived in a §81 experiment tree; it has to be rebuilt
before the 2.0/4.0 census can run.  Not done.**  This is exactly the "temporal at higher bitrates"
lever of item C1: at 2.0/4.0 bpp Q5 no longer holds the ground and a temporal context has something
to work with.

**`Academia/JPEGXS_3rdgen.pdf`** (Bruylants, Runyan, Lorent; SMPTE MIJ Sept 2025; 9 pages, read):
TDC = wavelet-domain temporal prediction against a QUANTISED frame buffer (one compressed frame,
4.5 or 12 bpp of quantised coefficients, "typically in external DDR"), inter/intra selectable per
subband (band switch) or per group of 32 coefficients (group switch) per precinct; refresh by an
implicit + explicit mechanism forcing spatially distributed intra groups, typical period 32 frames;
no key frames after the first; latency unchanged; +10 dB PSNR on graphics/e-sports/desktop; on
camera content "significant" on some scenes (waterfall) and "at least equal to XS High" on others
(Midnight Sun); on high-motion content TDC "maintains at least the same performance as XS High" —
i.e. **their temporal engine does not help high motion either**; at cuts the quality drops to
XS-High level and recovers "within a few frames (less than 100 ms)", which they call beyond
perception — the owner's 4-frame rule says otherwise, so OMC's ramp must be measured per frame.
Ideas it gives OMC (not copies; all vintage-clean): (i) a QUANTISED reference store — OMC holds
two full-precision pictures (refprev, refprev2) where TDC holds one compressed frame: a direct
Task D (DDR bandwidth/jitter) lever and a memory lever; (ii) group-of-32 switching granularity vs
OMC's per-band modes + Q5 block skips (OMC already has finer skip granularity; nothing to take);
(iii) their refresh period 32 vs OMC's 8 — S4.7 measured what a quiet link buys OMC; (iv) their
own admission that high motion gets no temporal gain — OMC needs a different mechanism there
(motion-compensated prediction is what OMC has and they do not: derive_mv exists; the question is
why it does not deliver on sports — measured next on the soccer master).

### S5.7 — Owner: "how do we improve on temporal/NEG savings at 1 bpp and above?" — the record and a bits census (2026-09-02 17:05; A1 memo 2026-08-30, v5.3 §40.6b board, FEASIBILITY.md §2.2, S5.4; `sbx_tctx` byte-inert OMC_BITS_CENSUS on dng 1080p frame 2)

Where the mandate stands above 1 bpp (§40.6b): dng 1080p @1.0 OMC 93.35 vs XS@2.0 95.82 (gap 2.5),
@2.0 OMC 96.07 vs XS@4.0 97.58 (gap 1.5); cityalley @1.0 96.09 vs 96.68 (gap 0.6), @2.0 96.89 vs
97.35 (gap 0.5).  The octave the incumbent buys shrinks with rate (cityalley 1.9 → 0.7 NEG), so the
high-rate mandate is a matter of half a point to two and a half — but at equal rate OMC is behind
at 2.0 on the corpus mean (coverage −0.059), and the A1 memo's ordering is FORMAT, not content:
identical dng loses 0.24× of equivalence purely from being 8-bit; every negative cell on the board
is 8-bit, 4:4:4 or 4K at ≥ 1.0 (4K from 0.5).  Neither weak group has ever been investigated.

Why temporal gives nothing up there (S5.4: +0.5..1.1 at 1.0, 0 at 2.0/4.0), measured on the bits:
| bpp | symbols | nonzero | raw (uncoded LSB) bits | category (tANS) bits | bands coded INTER |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 | 2.75 M | 10 % | 24 % of payload | 87 % | 38 % |
| 1.0 | 3.46 M | 13 % | 24 % | 82 % | 32 % |
| 2.0 | 3.78 M | 22 % | 27 % | 74 % | 28 % |
| 4.0 | 4.23 M | 38 % | 33 % | 68 % | 28 % |
(counts include encode attempts per §81.3; the shares are the point.)  At fine rungs the residual
coef − pcoef is the source's sensor noise, which the previous frame cannot predict, so the mode
decision codes fewer bands inter (38 → 28 %) and the reference buys nothing; a third of the payload
is raw LSBs that no context can compress.  FEASIBILITY §2.2 derived the same from the other side:
at 2R "any competent codec stores pixels more exactly", XS at 4.0 bpp is within a few percent of
the ideal coder, and OMC's own coder sits 10–15 % from ideal — the noise IS the information, and
NEG at high rate rewards reproducing it.

So the levers at ≥ 1 bpp, ranked by what the record says they are worth:
1. **The format weaknesses** (8-bit, 4:4:4, 4K): the largest single lever on the mean and untouched
   — not temporal at all.  S3.9 already found 8-bit's fill floor; 4:4:4's chroma allocation has a
   probe (`h/c444.sh`); 4K negative from 0.5 needs its own diagnosis.
2. **The structural picture errors that dominate once quantisation noise is small**: at 2.0 bpp
   the odd-row error is +30 % (chroma +40 %) and the slice's boundary rows +30 % (S3.10), and the
   chroma at 2.0 carries the calm-kill flatness (S3.6: 7–9 %) — together they are the size of the
   2.0 bpp gap (0.5–1.5).  The geometry/transform item, at high rate, is a NEG lever.
3. **The temporal entropy context** (S5.5 census at 2.0/4.0): bounded at a few percent of
   category bits, i.e. tenths of a NEG at best; cheap to measure, not a strategy.
4. **Static and graphics content at high rate**: broadcast studios, tickers, graphics and stills are
   where the temporal engine can still win at any rate (TDC's +10 dB is on such content); OMC's
   high-rate temporal gain has only been measured on moving camera clips.  Frozen masters and cf_gfx
   at 1.0/2.0/4.0, rota vs stateless, launched (`tgain_static.log`).
5. **Not a lever for NEG**: the quantised reference store (memory), noise-aware references (NEG
   penalises the enhancement; the removed in-loop temporal filter also could never be
   generation-exact, TEMPORAL_T5 line 1442).

### S5.8 — Owner (17:25): "to accomplish R=2R on noisy/high-motion, we must figure out what the incumbent doesn't do and make that our advantage" (consulted: DESIGN.md line 24, v5.3 lines 26690 / 37278, JPEGXS_3rdgen.pdf, T5 derive_mv comment)

What the incumbent does not do, from the record: **no motion compensation at all** (XS gen 1 has no
temporal layer; TDC predicts co-located wavelet coefficients from a quantised buffer, "NO motion
compensation whatsoever", and its own paper says it gives nothing on high motion); no
context-adaptive entropy coding (VLC/run-length only — OMC's tANS with 2-D contexts is the
existing advantage, and §3d says it is near-exhausted at ~5 %); no grain synthesis; no per-band
inter/intra switching finer than a precinct group; a quantised reference that could not support
motion compensation even if they wanted it.  OMC's structural advantage for high motion is
therefore the full-precision reference plus motion-compensated prediction — and today the encoder
uses it with ONE vector per slice: T5's `derive_mv` takes a whole-slice decimated SAD over a fixed
candidate list (±31 px horizontal, ±15 vertical, a few diagonals) between the two committed
predecessors and writes the same vector into all four region fields of the header, while the
DECODER already applies a vector per region (four horizontal quarters of the slice,
`x0 = reg·pw/4`).  Local motion — a runner against a static background, the owner's new footage —
is predicted with the background's vector, so the mover is coded as if there were no reference.

**Lever (encoder-only, no normative change, exactness-safe by T5's own argument):** derive one
vector PER REGION from the same committed history, SAD restricted to the region's columns; the
decoder needs nothing.  Build in `sandbox/sbx_mv` (env OMC_MVREG=1), measured on the 260902 masters
(runner A, pans B/C) and the corpus.  Header note: Task C's state hash (S4.4) reclaimed regions
1..3 on the assumption they are always equal; with per-region vectors the hash moves to the 23
reserved bits instead (the refine-mask build that wanted them is closed, S3.27) — the Task C
package will be re-cut to that layout.  The candidate list is horizontal-heavy; a runner's motion
is mostly horizontal, a pan-with-tilt is not — the list is the second thing to sweep (v5.3 §17b
"motion derivation not swept").

### S5.9 — LEVER 1a: the whole 8-bit loss is the 8-bit CODE PATH, not the content (2026-09-02 17:40; `sbx_texture/out/fmt/fmt8.log`; dng 1080p 4:2:2, 12 frames, step-1 tree)

| arm | 1.0 bpp NEG / luma flat / rungs | 2.0 bpp NEG / flat / rungs |
|---|---|---|
| native 8-bit path (the arm as shipped) | 91.23 / **5.31 %** / Q5 ×78, Q4 ×4 | 94.43 / 3.92 % / Q4 ×73 |
| the SAME 8-bit picture promoted ×4 through the 10-bit path | **93.52** / 0.05 % / Q7 ×65, Q6 ×16 | **96.11** / 1.06 % / Q6 ×69 |
| the true 10-bit arm | 93.56 / 0.05 % / Q7 ×67, Q6 ×16 | 96.10 / 1.06 % / Q6 ×70 |

The 8-bit picture coded through the 10-bit path scores within 0.04 NEG of the true 10-bit content at
both rates.  So the A1 board's 0.24× equivalence loss on 8-bit (0.90× / 0.77× at 1.0 / 2.0 against
1.19× / 1.14× for 10-bit) is entirely the depth-keyed rules of the 8-bit path: at the same effective
step the 8-bit plan sits two rungs lower (Q4–5 vs Q6–7), and every rule with an ABSOLUTE shift
threshold — the fill's minimum shift (5.3 % flat vs 0.05 %: the fill is refused), the deadzone's
`9 << s`, the texture bias at `s >= 3`, the LL cap, the Q5 admission — misfires by two octaves.
Two ways to close it: (a) make every absolute-shift rule depth-relative (a list to audit, each a
normative or encoder change); (b) code 8-bit streams in a 10-bit CONTAINER internally — promote
at input, demote at output — which the RGB path already does (`comp_depth + 2` container
promotion) and which the measurement above has effectively already run.  (b) is one rule and
provably equals the 10-bit path; its exactness question is the baseband 8-bit hop (the committed
10-bit picture is not a multiple of 4; a legal-range 8-bit hand-off rounds) — the RGB path's A4
treatment is consulted next.  Expected effect on the mandate: the two 4:2:2 8-bit cells and,
by the same mechanism, the 4:4:4 8-bit cells (0.86× / 0.66×) move to their 10-bit siblings'
figures.

vectors since v4.1.  Next: the owner's runner (local motion against a static background: queued),
the generation chain with the vectors on (exactness is by construction — committed history only —
and is tested anyway), the full gamut for non-regression, and the candidate list's range (the
pans sit at ±31 px, the header's 7-bit field).

### S5.15 — LEVER 1a, build probe: the two absolute-shift rules made depth-relative (2026-09-02 18:30; `fmt/fmt8b.log`, two-sided; 12 frames)

| cell @1.0 | shipped (LL cap 2, fill min 3) | LL cap 0 + fill min 1 | LL cap 0 only | fill min 1 only |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4:2:2 8-bit | 91.23 / flat 5.31 % | **91.94 / 0.10 %** | 91.93 / 5.26 % | 91.25 / 0.09 % |
| 4:2:2 8-bit @2.0 | 94.43 / 3.92 % | 94.43 / 0.56 % | — | — |
| 4:4:4 8-bit | 91.29 / 7.53 % | **91.85 / 0.07 %** | — | — |
| 4:4:4 12-bit | 93.50 | cap 4 + min 5: 93.72 (+0.22) | — | — |
| 4:2:2 12-bit | 93.66 | cap 4 + min 5: 93.71 (+0.05) | — | — |

Two rules, two effects, cleanly separated: the LL cap is the 8-bit NEG loss (+0.7 at 1.0 bpp: the
8-bit LL was coded four times coarser, relative, than the 10-bit LL) and the fill minimum shift is
the 8-bit flatness (5.3 → 0.1 %, 7.5 → 0.07 %: the fill was refused at the 8-bit rungs).  12-bit
gains +0.05–0.22 from the mirror-image correction.  Against the promoted-path oracle (93.52 at
1.0), 1.6 NEG remain in the other absolute-shift rules (25 `s >= k` sites, the deadzone's `9 << s`,
the texture bias at `s >= 3`, Q5 admission, the quality-floor rung); each is depth-relative by the
same rule `s_effective = s + (10 − depth)`.  Two routes: (a) finish the audit — keeps 8-bit
baseband exactness (an A4 gate today, dng 422_8 @2.0); (b) code 8-bit in a 10-bit container
(the RGB path's mechanism) — one rule, reaches the oracle at once, but makes 8-bit exactness
CDR-only exactly as RGB is today (a legal-range 8-bit hand-off rounds the container).  Route (a)
continues (the two rules above go in now, two-sided, minor 14); (b) is the owner's call.

### S5.18 — The colour cast: OMC's lifting rounds half-UP, and quantised-away detail leaves the picture a fraction of a code brighter on every plane (2026-09-02 19:20; owner's eye 18:55 "omc is slightly more saturated/red than the source"; probe `sbx_texture/out/bias/run.log`; tree `sbx_dcbias`)

Ledger context: F-29 (v5.3) recorded a ~0.2-code chroma DC bias "half from omc_calm", bounded
across generations, not actioned; S3.10 saw +0.3..+1.4 codes on all planes.  The owner saw it.

**Measured (dng 1080p, 3 frames, mean signed error in 10-bit codes):**

| arm @1.0 | Y | Cb | Cr | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| shipped (4:2:2) | +0.43 | +0.70 | +0.81 | same at 4:4:4 (+0.41/+0.88/+0.95), uniform over the frame (64×64 blocks p10..p90 = +0.5..+1.4) |
| by rate 0.5 / 2.0 / 4.0 / 8.0 | +0.60/+0.47/+0.38/+0.07 | +0.96/+0.55/+0.53/+0.07 | +1.04/+0.62/+0.53/+0.07 | scales with the step |
| fill off | +0.77 | +0.96 | +1.04 | fill is not the carrier (it hides a third of it) |
| calm off / repair off / all-intra | +0.45 / +0.43 / +0.42 | +0.75 / +0.70 / +0.80 | +0.87 / +0.81 / +1.02 | none of them |
| lossless | 0 | 0 | 0 | |
| JPEG XS @1.0 (4:4:4) | +0.08 | −0.11 | −0.02 | the incumbent has none |

**Cause (proved by a standalone 5/3 simulation on the source, `bias/` session):** every rounding
constant in the lifting (predict `>>1`, update `+2>>2`, 9/7-M predict `+8>>4`) rounds half up.
When a detail coefficient is quantised to zero the picture keeps the forward's rounding but
loses the coefficient that carried its complement: mean +1/8 code per 1-D pass where the
detail is non-trivial.  Simulation, H bands quantised at 5/4/3 with the LL at step 8: +1.06
codes with the shipped rounding; 0.00 lossless.

**Fix (`sbx_dcbias/src/dwt.c`, `[S5-DC]`, both filters, both ends, minor 15):** alternate the
rounding constant by sample-pair index (`i & 1`): predict `(a+b+(i&1))>>1`, update
`(dl+H+2-(i&1))>>2`, 9/7-M predict `+8-(i&1)`.  The lifting stays an exact integer bijection
for any per-index constant (lossless byte-exact, verified), the rounding error is zero-mean
over each pair, hardware cost = the index LSB.

| arm | Y | Cb | Cr | PSNR Y/Cb/Cr |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 shipped → fix | +0.60 → −0.15 | +0.96 → −0.02 | +1.04 → +0.05 | 32.80/31.41/32.05 → 32.84/31.42/32.10 |
| 1.0 shipped → fix | +0.43 → −0.13 | +0.70 → −0.02 | +0.81 → +0.07 | 35.05/32.92/33.60 → 35.03/32.91/33.60 |
| 2.0 shipped → fix | +0.47 → −0.12 | +0.55 → −0.02 | +0.62 → +0.05 | 38.76/35.68/36.30 → 38.77/35.68/36.30 |
| 4.0 shipped → fix | +0.38 → −0.10 | +0.53 → −0.01 | +0.53 → +0.03 | 43.10/41.41/40.96 → 43.10/41.43/41.01 |

Chroma cast gone at every rate; luma sits at −0.1 (the LL quantiser's own half-up rounding on
a non-negative LL, +0.5 in simulation, is evidently mostly absorbed by the LL DPCM/plan path —
left as is, below the eye).  Normative (decoder) change → reported as such.  Pending before
promotion: full-gamut NEG/flatness non-regression, CDR + baseband chains, Task C recovery,
owner's eye on the colour crop (source / shipped / fix).

noise each frame is exactly the S5.4 noise floor, FEASIBILITY §2.2), so the honest reading is:
the high-rate temporal prize lives in the STILL parts of the picture (graphics, static
backgrounds), and what limits it on real footage is per-frame noise, not the mechanism.  That
points the 1-bpp-and-above work at (i) making the still/moving split per region or block (per-
region motion already gives the vectors; the still regions should get the cheapest possible
"no change" coding) and (ii) the noise floor itself (the census, lever 3).

- `Agents/Agent3/MEMO_001_from_Fable.md` — 4:4:4 whole-plane budget census vs XS, two-sided probes (rung offset, chroma deadzone/admission, chroma fill, per-plane tie-break), and the @0.5 chroma-decay trace (base `sbx_dcbias`).

Correction (owner's question 23:05, "isn't it the decoder that does the work?"): yes — today only the ENCODER derives the vectors from committed history (for generation exactness); the decoder READS them from the slice header (4 regions × 13 bits: 7 for H, 6 for V, codec.c 6794/8838). The outside proposal's distinctive part is decoder-side derivation (both ends compute the same vectors, nothing transmitted at any granularity), which is exactly design (A) in Agent 1's MEMO 001 §5 — the right design once vectors are per block, where transmitting them would cost bits. Frame stores, verified 23:15 (owner's question): the ENCODER holds the frame being committed plus TWO previous frames (`e->refprev`, `e->refprev2`) — the second exists only to derive the region vectors; the DECODER holds the frame being committed plus ONE previous frame (`d->refprev`) and reads the vectors from the header. Decoder-side vector derivation (Agent 1 design (A)) adds a full previous-frame store to the decoder (≈8.3 MB at 1080p 4:2:2 10-bit, ≈33 MB at 4K) — owner's frame-memory rule applies; design (B) (signalled) adds bits, not memory; design (C) (LL-only second store, ~130 KB at 1080p, coarse vectors both ends + signalled refinement) is the cheap middle — `Agents/Agent1/MEMO_003_from_Fable.md` (23:20) corrects MEMO 001's "no extra memory" claim and adds (C).

### S5.26 — How much of VMAF-NEG is "getting the noise right" (2026-09-02 23:50; owner's question; dng 1080p 4:2:2 10-bit handheld, 3 frames, `sbx_texture/out/bias/src3.yuv`; luma noise σ ≈ 12.6 codes by MAD of the horizontal difference)
Three synthetic decodes of the SOURCE itself (no codec), scored with `harness/negscore.sh`:

| arm | what it models | NEG | PSNR Y |
|---|---|---|---|
| source + independent Gaussian noise, same σ (chroma 0.7σ) | noise with the right statistics but the wrong samples (a perfect "inference") | 95.39 | 38.21 |
| source + noise at σ/2 | half-wrong noise | 97.30 | 44.22 |
| 3×3 box blur | noise removed together with fine detail | 72.60 | 31.88 |

Reading: NEG does not know noise from detail — both are fine-band information, scored by sample fidelity. Statistically right but sample-wrong noise costs ~4.6 NEG at 38 dB, about what OMC scores at 2.0 bpp on this cell (S5.18 table); synthesised noise earns nothing back on the metric (the ledger's fill measurement at v5.3 line 43715 shows the fill COSTS 0.4–0.9 NEG while curing pitch for the eye); removing the fine band is catastrophic (−27). What this means for the work: above ~1 bpp on camera footage the bits buy the fine-band samples and NEG pays for each; no single inference lever changes that.
**OWNER RULING (2026-09-03 00:50), which overrides Fable's first reading of this table:** VMAF-NEG is the engineering bar tracked on ALL content (and, per `PROJECT_CONSTRAINTS.md` rev. 6, acceptance itself is blind human viewing of OMC @ R against XS @ 2R, full-frame, full-resolution, in motion — metrics are diagnostics, never the pass/fail; the two statements coexist: no work is judged on a metric split by content class, and no metric win is proof). There is no "eye-only" class of content and no split bar — a product cannot mark half its numbers and ask for trust on the rest. The way the target is reached is by COLLECTING levers, ten to twenty of them, each measured by NEG on the full gamut, and adding them up. Fable's "two-track measurement policy" is withdrawn; the eye remains the veto (flatness, smudges, colour) on top of NEG, never a substitute for it.

### S5.32 — Agent 3's MEMO 002 response received (2026-09-03 04:10; `Agents/Agent3/MEMO_002_response.md`, 509 lines)
1. **Generation-lock interaction, root cause found (14 encodes):** not the lattice, not a wrong value — the BUDGET. In the failing arm (halving + gain cap) generation 2's plan for frame 1 slice 33 is admissible and verifies but needs 31,966 bits against a `budget_hard` of 31,568: the T5 prefix induction (TEMPORAL_T5 §5: a locked slice never spends more than its predecessor, so the previous plan always fits later in the frame) is broken 30 slices earlier — slice 3 spends +431 bits at gen 2 (Cr LH1 flips INTER→INTRA and picks up a fill bit, +454 bits on the three level-1 Cr bands) and still locks; the bank runs short and slice 33 is where the shortfall first exceeds a slice's slack. Trigger: the cap forces the chroma gains 2/1 → 0, so the emitted amplitude no longer re-measures to the class it was emitted from. **Rule (H.5): a grain-fill change is generation-safe only if it is a change of UNITS (scales/re-bases both the emitted amplitude and the gain code's measurement, as the sect.67 divisor folding does); clamps, caps and floors on the derived gain are not, at any placement — they break the prefix induction, not the lattice. Detector, cheap and early: per-slice payload bits gen 1 vs gen 2 (`OMC_C3CENSUS`) — any slice where gen 2 spends more is a failure in waiting; the baseband chain never catches it.** The cap is closed in this form; the extra dB must come from moving the nominal the gain code measures against (a units change) = the per-band gain design below.
2. **Grain fill OUT of the prediction loop (`OMC_NFREF` 1 chroma / 2 all planes): REJECTED.** The @0.5 chroma decay does NOT vanish (Cb −0.92 → −0.96, Cr −0.76 → −1.05 over f2→f11): the compounding-through-prediction mechanism in S5.31 was WRONG (the fill-off arm removed the fill from the display too). Chroma-only arm ≈ neutral on NEG but breaks the bar at 4:4:4 @0.5 (Cr 0.00 → 0.36 %); all-planes arm +0.67 dB Y on cityalley but −0.40 NEG on graphics and cityalley luma 0.00 → 4.97 % flat; still-region chroma flicker slightly worse; costs a second full frame store per end. Kept from it: **a second, unfilled deterministic reconstruction IS generation-exact (8/8 chains) and heals on time** — not derived state in the S5.29 sense; and the still-region observation: the codec moves 6–10 codes per frame in a region the source holds still, structured in horizontal BANDS (the crawl class, 0.5 bpp), not caused by the fill in the loop.
3. **Decay mechanism now OPEN:** the fill's injected error is what decays (fill off: gone) but not through the loop; candidate: the fill amplitude tracks the rung and the chroma rungs coarsen across the refresh cycle as the temporal residual accumulates — unproved.
4. **Instrument line on the exact arm (item 1):** texture-loss regression is 0.25 / 0.89 pp of chroma blocks at 1.0 (not the capped arm's 6–7 pp quoted in S5.31); every other instrument equal or better. The deliverable stands.
5. **Per-band fill gain design (no build):** 14 reserved header bits; full per-band per-plane gain = 36 bits (needs a re-cut); **option 3 = per-plane gain + one 2-bit LEVEL-1 offset per plane = 6 bits, fits with 8 to spare**, a units change (adds to `div(p,b)` for bands 7–9, the lock's `LAT_DV` follows), no per-coefficient cost, no memory; the level-1 halving is option 3 pinned to one value, so it lands first and widens later as encoder-side RD. Deriving the gain at both ends (0 bits) rejected by the S5.29 rule (a refresh restores pixels, not the residual history the gain would derive from; a current-slice-only derivation is circular).
6. **Agent 3's own correction:** twice inferred a mechanism from a single switch that removed a symptom (fill → PSNR deficit; fill → decay-through-loop); measurements held, mechanism claims did not. Rule for every agent memo: "X causes Y" needs the probe that separates the paths, not one switch.
Falsified register (H.6): fill out of the prediction loop; gain cap on the transmitted fill gain (property, not placement).

### S5.33 — `PROJECT_CONSTRAINTS.md` (rev. 6, 518 lines) read in full by Fable (2026-09-03 09:10) — what it changes in this ledger
Until now Fable had cited the file by path in every memo without having read it this session. Read now; consequences:
1. **Acceptance is the eye, comparisons are only OMC @ R vs XS @ 2R (rev. 5/6).** Every "at equal rate" comparison in this ledger (S5.16, S5.31's XS @1.0 columns) is diagnostic context only; the ledger's XS @2.0 columns are the ones that bear on the mandate. NEG stays the engineering bar the owner asked for (S5.26) — tracked on everything, decisive on nothing; a blind full-frame viewing is the verdict. **Every eye render sent to the owner must include the FULL frame at full resolution** (E: a crop only points); today's crops (S5.18, S5.31) had full-frame companions in the agents' folders, but the memo template now requires the full frame to be delivered, not just made.
2. **C2: the decoder may retain exactly one previous reconstructed frame.** Agent 1's design (A) would have added a second previous frame to the decoder — closed on A5 already, and it fails C2 outright; design (B) is compliant. Agent 3's unfilled reference is a second reconstruction of the SAME previous frame (not a second frame of look-back) — rejected anyway (S5.32). Any future "decoder derives from N−2" idea is barred by C2 before any measurement.
3. **C7 (self-reliant: video in, bitstream out, nothing else) and D (transport out of scope) versus Task C's control plane:** the on-demand refresh needs a decoder→encoder message. It is codec-to-codec signalling, not a production control, but it crosses the transport boundary and must be specified as part of the versioned format (C8) and the codec must remain fully functional without it (it does: the scheduled wave, S5.25 discussion). **Open compliance question for the owner: is a decoder-to-encoder back channel inside the "bitstream" boundary of C7?** Until ruled, refresh-on-demand is an optional protocol extension and the wave stays the default.
4. **A1 pipe: the worst frame decides; every frame incl. ramp/cut frames fits the provisioned CBR pipe; both codecs at 4:2:2 AND both at 4:4:4.** OMC's per-slice CBR satisfies the pipe; the S5.25 idea #4 (bit lending within a frame) is bounded by this and by the owner's veto (S5.26 discussion) — stays off the list.
5. **Section G names our classes:** G3 pixelation = the chroma speckle (S3.17); G4 flattening/blotches = the flatness bar and XS's texture deletion (S5.31); G6 discoloration/cast = the colour cast (S5.18). G5 hard edges / G1 grid: not currently tracked by an instrument — the 32×32 grid method (brightness + grid overlay) is not in the harness; to add when a render is judged.
6. **C1: rANS forbidden anywhere; C3: no per-pixel multipliers, both ends real-time.** Agent 1's decoder-side SAD (design A) would have been a decoder per-pixel op budget; (B) removes it. The 9/7-M lifting's "9x = 8x + x" is shifts/adds — compliant.
7. **A3: VMAF ≥ 97 where the envelope allows; the only permitted degradation is smooth softening of already-soft regions.** The grille's lost detail at 8-row slices (S3.34) is a G4 event under bit pressure on an in-focus region — not a permitted degradation; it stays a real defect, not "rate".
