5. **The legal track (owner-directed; rulings in its §54): the binding test is "a decoder must be able to produce the filled picture from the bitstream using no field whose value the encoder chose by looking at the source."** The fill's base amplitude is already `1 << (s−2)` (a quarter step, a pure function of the transmitted quantiser step — "dequantisation reconstruction", prior art 1960s dithered/noise-feedback quantisation); the 2-bit per-plane gain is the only source-derived amplitude field and **can be removed (per-plane constant): 10/10 chains at luma constant 2, but the wider sweep says the constant should be 1 (flatness prefers low, detail prefers high; two of six cells are worse at every constant; readysetgo Cb 0.00 → 0.23 % regression) and L1 has NOT been chain-gated.** The 18-bit per-slice/plane/band mask is NOT solved: a parameter-free fill is exactly reproducible within a frame but fails temporally (0 % → 8.3 % → 13.4 % closure failure over frames, five formulations), because **the fill is a REPRODUCTION mechanism** — `lock_verify` derives the fill bits that reproduce the input coefficients bit-for-bit; at generation 2 the input holds ±a where the previous generation filled. The decoder cannot re-derive the amplitude from what was sent (conditional R −0.034 for the distribution-scale feature).
6. **The candidate architecture (`[A3-DDITHER]`): code with NO fill (locks by the plain lattice argument, 0 of 4067 bands break) and add a deterministic position-hashed ±amp pattern to the EMITTED picture only, the encoder subtracting the identical pattern from every input (at the display-blend inverse site).** All 20 fill bits leave the format. Round trip exact on the CDR (biased, unclipped) path at every amplitude; NOT exact through a legal-range baseband hop (18–235 samples per frame at the rail). Quality of the layer unmeasured. **Fable's reading for the owner to confirm: baseband exactness IS required — the step-1 legality work exists for the baseband hop and gamut-strict is on by default — so the dither must be made rail-safe (headroom-aware sign / fold) or it is not a candidate.** Legal (Q2): out-of-loop buys severability, not clearance; build it because it makes zero-parameter achievable; (Q5) compliance is binary — the amplitude removal ships WITH the mask solution, not before.
7. Also from the track: the fill paints texture into 83–100 % of genuinely smooth blocks (`invented.py`, threshold-sensitive); the fill switches OFF as the rate rises (the systemic high-rate flatness anomaly, S5.27's cityalley 10 % is not a quirk); the chroma fill OVER-textures and the flatness bar cannot see it (texstat AMP, S5.35 item 8); the incumbent beats us at equal rate on the honest instrument; a FILL_MIN_SHIFT verification-mirror asymmetry (live rule `base_s >= FILL_MIN_SHIFT + filldiv + …` vs mirror `base_s >= FILL_MIN_SHIFT`) is a real latent defect. To buy the memory the limit would have to be **normative** (field narrowed or a profile defined) = a one-way door in the bitstream. **General rule now binding on Task D: a resource bound that depends on what an encoder chooses to emit is not a bound; only the bitstream's own limits bound a decoder.** Agent 4 instructed to re-check parts 2–5 for anything else resting on that assumption.

Mechanism confirmed two-sided: on an intra band inside an inter plane a Q5F-skipped coefficient takes its value from the **prediction**, and that value sets `left`/`rowsig` — the **tANS contexts**; after a loss the decoder's reference differs from the encoder's, contexts diverge, the entropy decoder desyncs (`rc −3` / `rc −4`) on intact data. `OMC_Q5INTRA=0` on both ends removes it completely. **Trigger:** the intoPIX/JPEG XS TDC part question (S5.40) surfaced their compressed frame buffer; the owner asked whether we had already measured the same lever for OMC. **Documentation check done by Fable, result: NEVER MEASURED, NEVER BUILT.** The lever is idea **a7 "Compressed reference store"** (`LEDGER_v5_3.md` §38.12c table, §38.12e item 1, Q13, Q-DAN) — logged with the note *"never proposed; NOT a rate idea — likely costs NEG (prediction from quantized reference); frame-memory rule: Dan must rule before any build"* and the standing instruction *"Q13. a7 compressed reference store: DO NOT BUILD without Dan"*; also listed in S5.28 among the levers ruled out pending an owner ruling. Owner's acceptance conditions, verbatim in substance: **"if we lose generation byte-exactness or if we lose (noticeable) picture quality, then it's not worth it. If we can retain those advantages, then it could (not decided) be worth it."** So the probe is a GATE test, not a development task: it is dead the moment either condition fails, and a pass does not authorise promotion — it returns a decision to the owner.
**The prize (why it is worth a probe at all):** OMC's decoder holds rolling + `refprev` UNCOMPRESSED, ~2 stores ≈ **40 bpp of reference at 4:2:2 10-bit against TDC's 4.5–12 bpp** (§38.12e item 1) — a 4–9x memory/bandwidth lever. Under S5.40's ruling it is no longer needed to make any format fit; it now buys **headroom** (8K 4:4:4 is the tightest cell at ~13 %) and, potentially, a much cheaper part.
**What the record already predicts, to be falsified or confirmed by the probe:**
1. **Nearest measured neighbour FAILED:** `OMC_A2LP` low-pass-first prediction (a degraded reference) — **−0.86 NEG / −1.5 dB on frozen content and it BREAKS the flatness bar on cityalley**; in the falsified register (S5.28 headline). Dead-zone quantisation is a different degradation (removes small values across all bands, not high frequencies) so it is not the same experiment, but it is the closest one run.
2. **The incumbent claims the opposite:** Foessel & Richter measured a quantised/low-pass reference **beating** the raw one on natural content by **+0.2–0.4 dB** (S5.22 item 1). Our A2LP result contradicts theirs for the low-pass variant; the probe must say which holds for dead-zone.
3. **The structural risk, and the reason to measure this one carefully:** S5.8's finding is that **OMC's advantage over TDC on high motion IS the full-precision reference plus motion-compensated prediction** — *"a quantised reference that could not support motion compensation even if they wanted it"* (Foessel p. 28: the DDR buffer cannot be searched; intoPIX's own admission that TDC gives nothing on high motion). `derive_mv` searches the committed predecessors; quantising them degrades the input to the one tool the incumbent does not have. **The probe must report motion-clip cells (soccer, soccer2, runB, runC) separately from static/graphics cells** — a mean over the gamut would hide exactly the loss that matters.
4. **Generation exactness is OPEN, not closed.** The in-loop temporal filter (OMC-TF) was killed because *"a temporal filter re-applied at each generation compounds and can never be generation-exact"* (`TEMPORAL_T5.md`, `tf_mode` removal comment) — that argument does **not** transfer: a signalled quantised reference is a closed loop with a bit-identical buffer at both ends (intoPIX: *"no temporal drift by construction"*). But it is unproven for OMC, `lock_verify` must re-derive the reference quantisation exactly, and **the XS committee released multi-generation robustness for the inter-frame scenario** (wg1n v3.0 AND v3.2) — i.e. compressed reference + byte-exact generations is a combination the incumbent chose not to attempt, and it is §38.11's market position.
**Probe design (non-normative, both ends behind one env lever; NOT a bitstream change at this stage):** dead-zone quantise `refprev`/rolling at Fbblev-like levels (12 / 4.5 / 3 bpp equivalents) with the level applied identically at encoder and decoder; then, in order — (a) **generation chains 20 / CDR 10** (any break = dead, stop); (b) **the full gamut cell line** with per-plane flatness and texstat, motion cells reported separately (§3 above); (c) **owner eye check** in colour, full frame at full resolution plus |decode − source| maps, on a motion clip and a static clip; (d) the memory/bandwidth saving actually realised, per format, against Agent 4's band-ring table (S5.40). Report the level at which each condition first fails.

**§5.3 `omc_recoff` — BRANCH 3, NOTHING CLEARS IT, and it was already in the ledger.** `OMC_RECOFF` is in the decoder's C8 conformance-freeze list, so a two-sided A/B needs the agent's post-freeze alias `OMC_RECOFF_X` (read after `omc_dec_conformance_freeze()`, both ends; default byte-identical to `v54tree_int`; decoder verified to HONOUR it — checked explicitly because a silently-ignoring decoder yields a flattering mirage; `rt = 0` passes). **Every value breaks generation exactness: `FAIL pixels-gen2` on 8-generation CDR chains at n = 1, 2 and 3, on cf_gfx @0.5, dng 4:2:2 @1.0, dng 4:4:4 @0.5, highway 4:4:4 @0.5, with the base passing on the same harness.** `LEDGER_v5_3.md` **§30.5** already recorded this for n = 4 ("A contradiction in the record, resolved: RECOFF does break exactness"; the offset moves the reconstruction, the next generation's forward transform sees shifted pixels and they quantise to a different `q`; "not available for a conforming encoder"). Agent 2's contribution is to extend it to n = 1/2/3; he states he should have found §30.5 before running the sweep. **Recorded because someone will want to re-try it:** n = 1 is attractive on everything except the thing that matters — NEG **+0.773** on cf_gfx @0.5, +0.182 highway, +0.096 dng 4:2:2 @1.0, and it brings the cf_gfx cast to **−0.195, inside ±0.2**, with no other cell pushed out. Unusable at any quality.
**§5.3b — THE REFRAME, PROVED: the column parity is HORIZONTAL HIGH-PASS QUANTISATION LOSS in the 5/3 lifting, not a rounding defect.** Agent 2 consulted the codec expert BEFORE sending, on the grounds that Fable had called §5(a) the most important thing of the day and was about to act on his framing; the expert's verbatim instruction: *"Do not send the column-parity finding to your coordinator as a rounding-defect memo… first prove that mechanism with a coefficient-domain ablation"*, and *do not alter any rounding constant until the three prescribed tests are complete*. All three run. **Mechanism:** in horizontal reversible 5/3 lifting the odd/even polyphase branches are not reconstructed symmetrically once high-pass detail is quantised (the odd branch is interpolated from the low-pass), so a period-2 residual is the natural signature of strong horizontal near-Nyquist source energy. **Test 1, oracle ablation** (`[A2-BANDFINE]`, `OMC_BANDFINE="b:N"`, both ends, off-switch byte-identical; band 8 = HL1, finest horizontal detail; highway 4:4:4 12-bit @2.0, alternation in codes): HL1 **forced to zero** → Y −0.060 / Cb +0.328 / **Cr −0.538**; **as shipped** → −0.128 / +0.248 / −0.174; finer by 1/2/3 → monotone collapse; **finer by 5** → **Y −0.000 / Cb +0.022** / Cr −0.076. **It rises when HL1 is destroyed (Cr 3x) and falls monotonically when HL1 is retained.** Cr's residual at 2.0 traced to a CBR confound (finer HL1 ⇒ coarser elsewhere ⇒ same mechanism fed back), confirmed two ways: making any OTHER horizontal band finer by 5 makes Cr parity WORSE (HH1 −0.302, HL2 −0.295, HH2 −0.289 vs −0.174 baseline — an unplanned negative control behaving as predicted); and **repeating at 4.0 bpp where there is rate slack takes ALL THREE PLANES to essentially zero** (finer by 8: Y +0.005, Cb −0.009, Cr −0.007) — the expert's lossless-restore arm satisfied in both directions. **Test 2, phase:** shifting the source 1 pixel horizontally **REVERSES Cb's parity sign** (+0.248 → −0.177) — a fixed column-indexing error would stay tied to absolute output column, a polyphase signature reverses; and excluding a 64-column margin changes nothing (−0.128/+0.254/−0.162), so it is not boundary handling. **Test 3:** decays monotonically with rate to Cr −0.067 by 8.0 bpp; a fixed rounding constant would persist. **CONSEQUENCE: the remediation is BAND ALLOCATION (bits into HL1), not a rounding constant, and the ablation is a direct measurement of the exchange rate. Fable's "the rounding constants are then mine to revisit" is void; S5.43 amended in place.** Opposite Cb/Cr signs are expected (the expert: sign depends on the local phase of the source's chroma structure relative to the transform grid; no requirement that planes agree). **Still open and not an agent's call: whether ~0.6 codes peak-to-peak at 0.5 bpp is VISIBLE.** The expert declined to call it from magnitude alone; it has not been in front of the owner.
**§5.3 — a CHROMA stripe 3–4x the luma defect, invisible to a mean-based gate.** highway 4:4:4 12-bit @0.5: **Cr mean −0.005 (dead centre, passes any mean gate) with even col +0.307 / odd col −0.317 = alternation −0.624**; Cb mean +0.100, alternation **+0.292**; Y mean −0.027, alternation −0.074. `recoff` barely touches it (~5 %). **Fable's cast gate is structurally blind to this** — the same class of miss as the luma one, one plane over. **Renders:** `renders/A2_colprofile_highway_chroma.png` shows **Cr as a regular period-2 square wave clipping the ±0.6 scale** (real structure, not statistical residue), Cb the same at ~half amplitude, Y irregular and small; `A2_colprofile_cfgfx_recoff.png` shows base and recoff n=1 overlapping almost everywhere. **Two renders discarded first** (raw per-column mean auto-scaled a ±0.2 alternation into invisibility against ±10 codes of content; then 1920 columns into 1100 pixels saturated the panel) — both arithmetically correct and useless as evidence; only the parity component in a 100-column window shows anything. **The mean alternation UNDERSTATES the local amplitude** (local parity repeatedly exceeds ±0.6 while the mean is 0.15 luma / 0.62 Cr), so a mean-based threshold is looser than it looks.
**§5.4 DZW w = 10 — GATES PASS; Fable's "deadzone never binds" hypothesis DISPROVED; NEG IS SATURATED AND BLIND.** Gates on `v54tree_int`: **CDR 8-generation chains PASS** (dng 4:2:2 @1.0, dng 4:4:4 @1.0, cf_gfx @0.5, highway 4:4:4 @0.5 + base control); **baseband 8-generation chains PASS** (3 cells + control, new harness `notes/h_int_chain_bb.sh`); **Task C recovery PASS** (lose `3:30-31`, request `5:29-35`, `none` from frame 5, identical to base). **The three exact-zero cells are not "the deadzone never binds":** streams differ, decodes differ, and pushed to w = 16 (full-step deadzone) — runB @0.5 **70.6 % of samples changed, max Δ 130, luma PSNR 41.17 → 39.46 (−1.71 dB)**, runC @1.0 59.9 % / −0.73 dB, soccer2 @1.0 62.5 % / −1.24 dB — **and NEG reports 99.039 → 99.039, 99.562 → 99.562, 99.584 → 99.584, zero change to three decimals.** These cells score 99.0–99.6 and **NEG is saturated there and cannot resolve the lever at all** — S5.42's instrument-blindness finding one metric over (flatness blinded by added energy; NEG blinded by a high score). **Recomputed excluding the three blind cells the w10 recommendation SURVIVES:** 15 cells — w10 mean +0.130, **12/15 improved**, worst −0.033; w11 mean +0.195, 10/15, worst −0.092. **Any gamut mean that includes runB, runC or soccer2 is diluted by cells where NEG cannot respond.**
**THE EXPERT'S RULING ON NEG, passed on unsoftened: *"Do not use VMAF-NEG as a pass/fail gate anywhere in this project."*** Reasoning: a bounded 0–100 learned metric operating near its ceiling; three-decimal rounding has limited sensitivity there; VMAF-NEG is specifically built to subtract enhancement-related score gain, not to guarantee sensitivity to every small or structured high-quality regression. **They note this restates the project's own rule** (PROJECT_CONSTRAINTS: blinded full-frame motion viewing is decisive, PSNR/VMAF are diagnostics). **Prescribed instead: a dashboard, never a single gate** — worst **frame** PSNR (not corpus mean), high-pass correlation and AMP change, artifact counts, parity amplitude, exact generation conformance, and visual review whenever an artifact detector moves; plus a **pre-registered saturation ceiling** (they suggest 98.5 or 99.0, explicitly a project threshold to be chosen from our own response curve, not a VMAF standard) above which cells are marked *metric-saturated* and scored on the dashboard instead of averaged in. **FABLE'S RULING: the ceiling is 99.0**, because that is what our own data evidences (blindness demonstrated from 99.039 up; 98.5 would be extrapolation). NEG is a diagnostic, never a gate, in every future memo — **Fable's own ±0.1 NEG bars in MEMOs 004/005 are withdrawn as GATES and retained as diagnostics.** Earlier gamut means are NOT recomputed wholesale; only where a live conclusion depends on a saturated cell.
**§5.5 item 1 — IP REVIEW ACTION 1a, fill ON vs fill OFF, 19 owner-owned cell/rate points (`out/fill/run.log`; no NC footage anywhere in the table; 12 frames).** **Fill OFF beats fill ON on: NEG 16 of 19 cells (up to +1.100 spotrobot @0.5; worst −0.047); luma PSNR ALL 19 (+0.63 to +3.48 dB); chroma PSNR ALL 19 (+2.08 to +6.60 dB); luma source correlation ALL 19 (+0.011 to +0.166); invented texture (dng 4:2:2 @0.5 chroma 100 % → 0 %).** **Fill ON buys exactly one thing — the flatness bar — and buys it completely** (dng 4:2:2 @0.5 Y 0.06 % → **56.10 %** with the fill off; dng 4:4:4 0.06 % → 56.53 %; cf_gfx 4.95 % → 48.87 %; winterdrive 0.00 % → 49.30 %). **The trade is worst at 2.0 bpp:** fidelity cost is roughly flat across rate while the flatness benefit collapses (0.5 bpp prevents 33.6–56.5 % flat; 2.0 bpp prevents **1.5–15.0 %**), and at 2.0 the fill is **NEG-NEGATIVE on two owner-owned cells** (dng 4:2:2 −0.047, dng 4:4:4 −0.045) while on fbtrain it prevents **1.53 %** flat blocks for 1.37 dB luma and ~2.2 dB chroma. **Neither state is right on chroma texture energy** (dng 4:4:4 @0.5 texstat AMP, ideal 1.00): fill ON **Cb 2.20 / Cr 2.55**, fill OFF **Cb 0.26 / Cr 0.29** — the fill puts 2.2–2.6x the source's chroma texture energy in, without it we have a quarter. Counsel must NOT be told that removing the fill makes the picture correct; it makes it measurably closer to the source while making it visibly flat. **Flatness readings of 0.00 % under fill-ON are accompanied by AMP well above 1.0 — read them as "the meter is quiet", not "the picture is right" (S5.42).**
**§5.5 item 1 ADDENDUM — the expert's third statistic, and it is the most damaging number we have on the fill.** They ruled **AMP must not stand alone** ("there is no defensible universal upper AMP limit"; it is a reconstruction-energy statistic, not an information-fidelity measure, and a pure-energy flatness detector "certifies synthetic grain as texture preserved"). Prescribed triple, built as `notes/hperr.py` over **textured blocks only**, on flatplane's own 16x16 grid and source-median rule, with the identity `E_HP^2 = 1 + A^2 − 2*A*rho` printed as a self-check and **matching to three decimals on all six readings**: `A = σ(HP(dec))/σ(HP(src))`, `rho = corr(HP(dec), HP(src))`, `E_HP = ‖HP(dec) − HP(src)‖ / ‖HP(src)‖`. dng 4:4:4 @0.5 — **fill ON: Y A 1.014 rho +0.659 E_HP 0.831; Cb A 2.005 rho +0.013 E_HP 2.229; Cr A 2.364 rho +0.016 E_HP 2.552. Fill OFF: Y 0.899 / +0.758 / 0.667; Cb 0.210 / +0.117 / 0.997; Cr 0.252 / +0.142 / 0.996.** **Emitting NO texture gives E_HP ≈ 1.0 by construction; the shipped chroma fill gives 2.23 and 2.55 — the fill is MORE THAN TWICE AS WRONG AS EMITTING NOTHING on chroma, at a correlation of +0.013 (i.e. essentially uncorrelated with the source).** Fill-off is better on luma too (0.667 vs 0.831). Against the expert's interim engineering thresholds (**A > 1.5 AND rho < 0.3 = automatic invented-texture failure candidate**; A ≈ 2.2–2.6 with low correlation "presumed synthetic until visual and source-alignment evidence proves otherwise") **the shipped chroma fill sits squarely in the automatic-failure region on both planes.** Two cautions recorded with it: these are **engineering review thresholds, not perceptual law**, and must not become product pass/fail limits until calibrated against owner-blinded viewing; and the right bound is **two-dimensional (A > A_max AND rho < rho_min)**, set prospectively per plane, per 4:2:2/4:4:4, per depth and per texture cell scale from a locked corpus — **so Fable's §6 task as written ("propose the upper bound from the distribution") must NOT be done as a single number; it must produce an exclusion region.**
**Not run:** §5.5 item 2 (720p grille, 8 vs 16-row slices) and item 3 (AMP bound, §2 renders). Agent 2 reported at the legal-deadline item's completion rather than at exhaustion, per the S5.43 early-report exception, and because §5.4 corrected a number already given to Fable. **Token note: ~60k output tokens across this assignment plus three peer replies.**
**Agent 2's open questions for Fable/owner:** (1) is HL1 allocation to be owned as a lever (exchange rate measured; should not be built until the owner rules the stripe visible); (2) who owns the highway Cr stripe; (3) the NEG ceiling number and whether earlier gamut means are recomputed; (4) **is the zero-flat bar itself to be re-examined at high rate** (at 2.0 bpp the fill is NEG-negative while preventing as little as 1.5 % flat blocks) — **owner's call**; (5) confirmation that the stale still-regions assignment was not live (it was not).

### S5.45 — OWNER RULING: the flatness bar becomes RATE-DEPENDENT (2026-09-05; on S5.44's fill ON/OFF evidence; supersedes the absolute form of the owner bar of 2026-09-02 above 1.0 bpp)
**The evidence that forced it (S5.44, Agent 2, 19 owner-owned cell/rate points):** the fill's FIDELITY COST is roughly flat across rate while its FLATNESS BENEFIT collapses — 0.5 bpp prevents 33.6–56.5 % flat luma blocks, 1.0 bpp prevents 25.1–45.3 %, **2.0 bpp prevents only 1.5–15.0 %** — and at 2.0 bpp the fill is **NEG-negative on two owner-owned cells** (dng 4:2:2 −0.047, dng 4:4:4 −0.045) while on fbtrain it spends **1.37 dB luma and ~2.2 dB chroma to prevent 1.53 % flat blocks**. The owner was given four options (keep absolute + eye review; keep absolute, no review; rate-dependent; re-examine the fill itself) and **ruled: RATE-DEPENDENT.**
**THE BAR, as Fable has set the threshold from the data (owner picked the shape, not the number; he may move it):**
- **At and below 1.0 bpp the bar is UNCHANGED and ABSOLUTE — zero flat textured blocks, every cell, every plane** (0.5 bpp and up to 4K; 1.0 bpp and up above 4K, per the 2026-09-02 owner bar). This is where the fill demonstrably prevents 25–56 % flat blocks and it keeps its full obligation there.
- **Above 1.0 bpp the numeric bar is RELAXED and the flatness COUNT becomes a diagnostic, not a gate.** The governing test above 1.0 bpp is the eye: no *visible* flat block. Fidelity is not to be spent driving a flatness count to zero above 1.0 bpp without a visible artifact to point at.
- **Threshold chosen at 1.0 bpp because that is where the measured cliff is** (25.1–45.3 % prevented at 1.0 against 1.5–15.0 % at 2.0). It is a project threshold, not a law; a response curve that puts the knee elsewhere moves it.
- Consistent with, and reinforced by, **S5.42** (flatplane is a pure energy test with no structure term — a count of 0.00 % can mean a blinded meter) and **S5.44** (NEG is never a gate). The pattern across all three: **no single number is a gate; the eye is, and the numbers are the dashboard.**
**IMMEDIATE CONSEQUENCE, commissioned as Agent 3 MEMO 007:** the fill's obligation above 1.0 bpp is now much weaker, so a **rung-keyed fill stand-down above 1.0 bpp** becomes measurable — recovering the 1–3.5 dB luma / 2–6.6 dB chroma the fill costs there, and shrinking the surface of the item under IP review. It is NOT an opt-in trade-off (H.0 item 5): the rate rung is derived from the header, so a rung-keyed stand-down is automatic per slice and generation-invariant, the same machinery `omc_filldiv_pr` already uses. Branches in the memo.
**What does NOT change:** Agent 3's L0/L1 flatness failures (VolleyballGame Y 0.94 → 7.25 %, WinterDrive Cb 1.18 → 7.82 %) must be re-read against the rate they were measured at — if at or below 1.0 bpp the absolute bar still applies and L0 still fails it.

### S5.47 — CORRECTION TO S5.45: the flatness bar is NOT rate-keyed. It stays ABSOLUTE, restated as the paired test (2026-09-05; owner challenged the form: "are you sure it should be a rate gate or should it be something else?")
**S5.45 was the wrong shape and the owner caught it. Five reasons, recorded so it is not re-proposed:**
1. **It weakens the quality bar exactly where the customer pays more.** A broadcaster running 2.0 bpp expects a better picture than at 0.5, not permission to be flat. A bar that relaxes as rate rises is backwards.
2. **Rate is a proxy for the wrong variable.** Agent 3 has now proved twice over that the flatness split is **by CONTENT** — no depth key, no format key and no plan-derived key separates it (S5.42, S5.44, MEMO 006 §5.4), and a plan-derived key makes the rule generation-variant, which is the disease not the cure. Rate has the identical weakness: 2.0 bpp on noisy 4K can flatten worse than 0.5 bpp on clean graphics.
3. **The evidence did not support a BAR change.** What Agent 2 measured (S5.44) is that **the FILL's** benefit collapses with rate while its cost stays flat. That is a statement about the tool's cost-effectiveness, not about how much flatness is acceptable. Fable moved the requirement when the finding was about the instrument used to meet it.
4. **The flatness NUMBER is not the bar anyway.** S5.42 and Agent 3 MEMO 006 §5.5 show `flatplane` is an energy threshold that is blind in BOTH directions — blinded by added broadband energy (dither a12+ reads 0.00 % while smudge groups climb to 6,903 blocks), and blind to the opposite failure (fill-off reads 57.71 % while smudge sees **0/0/0** on luma). Keying a rate rule to an untrustworthy number compounds the error.
5. **New IP review §5.1 category (c)** — "constant bound, content-dependent decision to apply" — is **grey art and already live in the product** (`OMC_FILLREACH`). While the FTO search is uncommissioned, inventing new keyed gates around the fill is exactly the wrong direction.
**THE BAR, RESTATED (supersedes S5.45; the 2026-09-02 owner bar otherwise stands unchanged):**
- **Zero flat textured blocks at ≥ 0.5 bpp up to 4K and ≥ 1.0 bpp above 4K, every cell, every plane, AT EVERY RATE.** Rate does not enter the bar.
- **The bar is a PAIR, per the codec expert's mandatory form: `PASS = not flat AND source-structure retained`, and a gain in one may NEVER compensate for a failure in the other.** Evidence for any flatness claim = the flatness count **plus** the smudge groupings **plus** COR; the eye decides where they disagree. A 0.00 % flatness reading is evidence of "clean" only when the smudge count has not risen and COR has not fallen.
- **Correlation must be hardened as the expert specifies** (not yet built): per plane, per wavelet subband, in source-textured regions only, after removing local mean/DC, weighted by source detail energy, reported as **worst-case and percentile, not the average**, with low correlation counted as failure only where source detail energy exceeds a floor.
- **A third axis we do not measure at all:** temporal consistency `|rho(t) − rho(t−1)|` over motion-aligned regions — catches correct average energy with plausible single-frame correlation but temporal sparkle / chroma crawl / pattern switching. To be built before further fill work.
**WHAT IS RATE-DEPENDENT IS THE FILL'S BEHAVIOUR, NOT THE BAR — and that stays commissioned.** MEMO 007 §5.2 (the rung-keyed fill stand-down above 1.0 bpp) is still exactly the right measurement; only its acceptance condition changes. **The stand-down arms must meet the UNCHANGED ABSOLUTE bar.** If standing the fill down above 1.0 bpp still meets it, the fidelity (1–3.5 dB luma, 2–6.6 dB chroma) is recovered for free and legal surface shrinks with it; if it does not, we keep the fill there and pay. The fill already self-attenuates with rate — it fires only where a coefficient quantised to zero — so this is a measurement of how much of its high-rate firing is unnecessary, judged against a fixed requirement. **Correction issued to Agent 3 as MEMO 008 (a NEW memo — MEMO 007 is delivered and is never edited).**

### S5.48 — UPDATED IP REVIEW received from the legal review team (2026-09-05; `OMC1_IP_REVIEW.md` rev. of 2026-09-04/05, 1,016 lines; prompted by Agent 1's request for clarification). What changed, and what it binds
**STANDING, now explicit and directed at us:** *"This is an engineering review of algorithm provenance. It is not a legal opinion and it is not a freedom-to-operate search… Nothing in here is a ruling. In particular the design target in §1.2 is a heuristic for steering engineering, and **it was read as binding once already** — no engineering decision should be recorded as this review's, and no line from it belongs in a brief without a lawyer's review."* **Correction to S5.46 and to every memo: the design target ("a decoder should be able to produce the filled picture using no field whose value the encoder chose by looking at the source") is an ENGINEERING HEURISTIC, not a legal test.** It has no legal standing, was not drafted against claim language, and must not be cited as counsel's ruling. Read literally it also catches the quantiser step, which is not the intent; the operative distinction is narrower — ordinary coding parameters (quantiser step, refinement count) describe **how transmitted data was scaled** and are out of scope; the fill amplitude and mask describe **statistics of DISCARDED data** and are used to **generate content that was never sent**. *"Nothing here argues against making a chroma quantiser step respond to measured source content."*
**THE FTO SEARCH ON THE GRAIN FILL REMAINS UNCOMMISSIONED and is "still the thing that answers the question this document raises."** Review's action 2: commission it now, it is the long pole, and **scope it to cover three things at once — the fill itself, the boundary-keyed refusal `OMC_FILLREACH`, and coefficient-domain range enforcement in the in-gamut repair loop; same searcher, same afternoon.** The edge-directed scaler goes in its own lower-priority search (optional module, need not gate the core sale). **Owner action.**
**THE REFINEMENT THAT MATTERS MOST FOR OUR CURRENT WORK: "The base amplitude was always clean; only the modulation is not."** `codec.c:3653,3662` sets the base to `1 << (s − 2)` — a pure function of the transmitted quantiser step; the 2-bit gain (`3675–3679`) is a ±75 % modulation layered on top. **Strip the modulation and what remains is a step function that sits in the dequantisation-reconstruction family beside the centroid offset already shipped.** This is precisely Agent 3's constant-amplitude deliverable and it validates the direction. Calibrations: **zero transmitted parameters is "substantially the answer, though not a guarantee"** — what protects a parameter-free fill is which body of prior art it lands in (amplitude from the step, position from a normative rule, character fixed → dithered/noise-feedback quantisation prior art running back to the 1960s); **so specify it beside dequantisation, derive amplitude explicitly from the step, and STOP CALLING IT GRAIN in the normative text — "the name in the spec is part of what a claim chart is read against."** And **partial reduction is close to worthless**: 18 bits down to 4 crosses no line; every fill change is normative and costs a stream-minor bump and a decoder redeployment, so **spend that once, on the version that reaches zero.**
**TENSION FABLE MUST FLAG:** the review records the fixed-constant route as **"Closed — measured worse than the gain on every clip at every rate across four masters, and no single constant is safe on the flatness criterion."** That verdict rests on the OLD four-master, `sbx_dcbias`-era data. **Agent 3's re-run on `v54tree_int` (MEMO 006 §5.4) is materially better** — L0 now passes NEG on 10 of 11 cells and breaks flatness on ONE (VolleyballGame Y 0.20 → 8.99 %), against 0/11 and 2 before; L1 breaches fell 5 → 3. **The route the review calls closed on quality is the route it also says is the legally clean one. That collision is the central v5.4 decision and it is the owner's.**
**NEW LIVE FINDING — `OMC_FILLREACH` IS NOT DORMANT, and our team reported it wrongly.** It refuses to synthesise where the co-located LL magnitude plus half the local gradient comes within a margin of `mid` = 2^(depth−1) — i.e. **a content-dependent refusal to synthesise, keyed to the legal range boundary.** Verified state against our claims: "disabled by default" is **wrong** — default is −1 = AUTO (`codec.c:2518`) resolving to `fr_ = (vvis <= 8) ? 64 : 0`, **active at every 720p-class format**; "encoder-side" is **wrong** — it is **normative**, in the decoder conformance freeze list (`codec.c:8491`); it runs at decode time in shipping product on a supported format class. It is §5 category (c) grey art, **live in the product rather than under consideration**, and belongs in the FTO scope. **Removing it is NOT cheap** — our own measurement: blotch n>40 **147 with it off against 56 with it on at 720p, plus 0.49 VMAF-NEG** — normative, so deletion is a stream-minor change. **Owner decision, not a cleanup.** (`OMC_FILLRAIL` IS genuinely dormant, default 0 — **delete it**, review action 2b: dead code in a flagged area is pure cost.)
**§5 IS NEW AND IT REDIRECTS WORK THAT WAS ABOUT TO BE BUILT — range enforcement / "adaptive clipping".** The flagged art is clipping bounds *derived from picture content and signalled in the bitstream* (JEM/JVET, recent filings). Five categories: **(a)** bounds transmitted — **avoid, this is the art proper**; **(b)** bounds derived at both ends from decoded content, not transmitted — **avoid, claims routinely recite *determining* a clipping parameter without requiring transmission**; **(c)** constant bound, content-dependent decision to apply — **grey, and already live** (`OMC_FILLREACH`); **(d)** modifying coded data so output lands in range without clipping — **lower risk than it looks**, encoder-only, emits an ordinary conformant stream; **(e)** limiting an additive synthesis term to the remaining headroom — **THE ONE TO RECONSIDER.** **Why (e) is not safe:** the bound never moves, but the operation makes grain amplitude a function of the sample's own value — attenuated near black and white, full in the mid-range — which **is intensity-dependent scaling of synthetic grain, structurally what AV1's piecewise-linear scaling function does.** The fill has three surviving distinctions and distinction 2 is *"no intensity-dependent scaling function — your gain is one flat scalar per plane per slice"*; **build (e) and that sentence stops being true. It spends one of the three on the highest-risk item in the product.**
**§5.3 — THE FORMULATION TO BUILD INSTEAD: apply the fill unmodified, then a SINGLE UNCONDITIONAL SATURATION to the bit-depth constant, identically at both ends, with no signalled or derived parameter.** Reasons: the clamp is **generic** (applies to every sample whether or not it was filled, so the synthesis rule stays intensity-independent and distinction 2 survives); it is **sufficient on its own** (a clamp forces every sample into range by construction, so the headroom limiter is not needed for correctness — only as a quality refinement against visible hard clipping); and **the mechanism already exists** — `reconstruct_slice` already has an unconditional constant clamp to `[0, maxv + 2*OMC_REF_BIAS]`, so the change tightens an existing clamp's constant rather than introducing clipping to a loop that had none. **Sequence: build the clamp, measure whether hard clipping is visible on the failing clip, add the headroom limiter ONLY if it is.** **§5.4, to prove BEFORE building:** behaviourally the change is real even though structurally the operation exists — the wide clamp essentially never engages, a legal-range clamp would engage routinely, and `omc1.h:70–78` names the unclipped biased domain as one of three pillars of the generation-exact guarantee. **That proof must be REWRITTEN, not carried over by analogy: `committed = clamp(inverse_transform(lattice point))` is still an exact function of the emitted point, just a different function — write the proof before the code.**
**Review's ordered actions and our status:** (1) the two outstanding fill measurements — **BOTH NOW DONE** (fill-on/off = Agent 2, S5.44; fixed amplitude vs 2-bit gain = Agent 3, S5.42/S5.44/MEMO 006 §5.4) — the review does not yet know this; (2) **commission the FTO — owner**; (2a) plain clamp first, hold the headroom limiter, rewrite the proof; (2b) delete `OMC_FILLRAIL`; (3) delete OMC-TF (already on the S5.39 list); (4) get the v5.3 escape path assigned in writing — **owner**; (5) copyright headers + licence — **owner's entity name, still the one item only he can unblock**; (6) hold the fill's phase-advance until the search reports (already ruled, S5.40 — the machinery to re-animate is intact at `codec.c:8688`, offsets computed then discarded at `3701`); (7) re-run published comparisons on cleared footage; (8) PQ/Dolby conversation — **owner**; (9) BBC HLG grant — **owner**; (10) FSE credit + convert the ledger into dated invention records.
**What the review says we did right, recorded because it has value if willfulness is ever raised:** *"documented failed design-arounds, explicit non-claims, and two favourable characterisations they withdrew themselves when the evidence did not support them. That record is hard to attack as bad faith."* And on §5's existence: *"the codec team asked before building rather than after — which is the order that saves money… it is worth keeping as the working pattern."* **Counsel gets the three surviving distinctions and the design-target section, and NOT the "no model" line** — *"a defence that a competent opponent dismantles by reading one function is worse than a narrower one that holds."*

### S5.49 — v5.4 HAS A PRE-EXISTING GENERATION-EXACTNESS FAILURE AT 4:4:4 8-BIT @2.0, and it is the SAME LL-shift-0 mechanism Agent 3 found (2026-09-05; Fable's own verification)
Agent 3 reported (MEMO 006 §0d) that `v54tree_int` fails `pixels-gen2` at 4:4:4 8-bit @2.0 **in its pristine state**, with none of his changes active. **Fable replicated it and extended the control to the pre-integration tree:**
```
v54tree_int      dng_1920x1080_444_8  @2.0 : FAIL pixels-gen2
v54tree_int      dng_1920x1080_444_8  @1.0 : PASS
v54tree_int      dng_1920x1080_444_10 @2.0 : PASS
v54tree_pretaskc dng_1920x1080_444_8  @2.0 : FAIL pixels-gen2
```
**It fails on `v54tree_pretaskc` too — the backup taken BEFORE Task C and the rounding fix were merged — so it is neither Fable's integration nor any agent's work. It is in v5.4 itself.**
**[WITHDRAWN 2026-09-05 — see S5.62. The LL-shift-0 mechanism is FALSIFIED in both directions, and the claim below that the pristine failure 'sits on the same curve' DOES NOT HOLD: Agent 3's earlier failing cells were measured with his own L1HALF rule ON and both PASS on the pristine tree, so the two failure sets are different sets. The curve was his, not v5.4's. Kept with its reasoning intact because the falsification is the useful record.]** ~~And it is not a separate defect: it is the mechanism Agent 3 isolated.~~ Chasing his own 8-bit chain failure he found, with generation 1's plan frozen and replayed, that the pixels still differ (so plan movement is a consequence, not the cause), that the first divergence is **frame 0, slice 9, plane Cr, band 0 — the LL band**, and that **the failure requires an LL band coded at shift 0**, where nothing quantises the perturbation away: 8-bit @1.0 has shift 0 on 12 slices → FAIL; 8-bit @0.5 has none → PASS; 10-bit @1.0/@2.0 all shift 2 → PASS; **10-bit @4.0 has shift 0 on 6 slices → FAIL**; 12-bit all shift 2 → PASS. Higher rate → finer LL → the shift reaches 0. **The pristine 8-bit @2.0 failure sits on the same curve.** He also established that **keying on the LL shift does not work** — the LL shift is plan-derived and the plan is what moves between generations, so gating on it makes the rule generation-variant; both failing cells still failed. Reverted.
**Why this matters more than either report alone: byte-exact multi-generation is a core product claim** (PROJECT_CONSTRAINTS; the XS ecosystem explicitly released it for inter-frame, which is §38.11's market position). **A shipped operating point that fails it is a defect in v5.4, independent of the fill work, and it must be resolved or the operating point must be excluded in the normative text before the v5.4 zip.** Owner question raised by Agent 3 and now sharpened by the control: **is 4.0 bpp inside the product's operating range, and is 4:4:4 8-bit?** PROJECT_CONSTRAINTS A1 states the mandate at 1.0 and 2.0 bpp explicitly and "at any rate a broadcaster would run"; B4 fixes resolution and frame rate but does not bound rate above. **Fable's position: this is a v5.4 blocker to be understood, not an envelope to be written around, because the same mechanism will reappear at any operating point where the LL reaches shift 0.**

### S5.50 — Agent 5's MEMO 001 response (Task E, latency waste): THERE IS NO LINE TO REMOVE — the risk is per-slice COMPUTE, three published hardware bounds are wrong, and the project's own latency model is 35 % low (2026-09-05; `Agents/Agent5/MEMO_001_response.md`, 2,080 lines, base `v54tree_int` copied 2026-09-04 21:26:08; codec expert consulted three times)
**THE REFRAME, and it inverts the assignment.** The four stages Task E expected to find delay in — the plan search, the candidate walk, the emit attempts and the in-gamut repair — **contribute EXACTLY ZERO lines of algorithmic delay.** Only capture, paced transmission, a 2-line input look-ahead, the XSL display blend and the resolution converter contribute any. **There is no line to remove.** What those four stages consume is per-slice **COMPUTE**, and because `xsl_prep()` makes slice k's transform depend on slice k−1's **committed reconstruction**, that compute **cannot be pipelined across slices at all** — so a content-dependent compute spike becomes a **stall**, and a stall is exactly the latency wander A2 forbids. **That is the half of A2 actually at risk, and no line count can see it.** (The agent's first statement of this was unconditional; the expert corrected him and he restated it conditionally — it holds only while per-slice compute fits a slice period and XSL removes the concurrency that would otherwise make it true.)
**DELIVERED, byte-identical, gated against the pristine base:** `[A5-LAZYCOST]` — the per-shift cost table computed on demand — **−17.3 % of encoder CPU over a 50-cell rate sweep**, per cell −3.6 % to −43.5 % by content and rate; byte-identical stream and decode on every gate cell. Plus a corrected `latency_model.py` (see below). Candidates 2, 3 and 4 closed as **structurally impossible with a proof for each**, not as things that failed.
**THE COMPUTE SWING IS A LOW-RATE PROBLEM, and it is severe there.** On owned footage at 0.4–0.5 bpp the **worst slice costs 11–16x the mean**; one slice reached **128 emit attempts** and another **32 in-gamut repair passes**. The same clip swings **11.2x at 0.5 bpp, 3.9x at 1.0 and 1.4x at 4.0** — so the codec is close to constant where it is meant to run and **the problem is the low tier.** Cause: `goto encode_attempts` re-enters **above** the attempt loop, and `gm_iter` is reset at **five** sites (four reachable at defaults).
**THREE PUBLISHED PER-SLICE BOUNDS ARE WRONG, AND AN RTL TEAM WOULD SIZE AGAINST THEM — this is an FPGA-first defect, not documentation tidying.** `docs/HARDWARE.md` §7's *"hard cap 40 attempts … a proven bound"* **measures 128** over the 50-cell sweep and is exceeded on **5 of 10 clips**; the repair's hard clamp `OMC_GAMUT_MAXPASS` = 16 **measures 32**; `docs/HW_TIMING_METHOD.md` §3's *"≤ 48 candidate reconstructions per slice"* is **4096** (`OMC_LOCK_CANDS`; T5 deliberately removed the try cap so the previous generation's plan is always found). **And a fourth in the source itself:** `src/codec.c:2234` states the repair's worst case as `(1 + omc_gm_redomax) × gamut_strict` = 24, counting one of three reset paths — measured 26 and 33 exceed it. **None is a code defect — the true bound is 48 at defaults and holds under adversarial test — but four statements of it are all too small.** The expert escalated two further structural concerns and **the agent's audit showed he was wrong on both**: the repair IS bounded (48 at defaults, verified adversarially — it is the *stated* bound that is wrong), and when it cannot close the encoder **does not silently clip or silently ship — it declares the shortfall, counts it, names the remedy and exits non-zero.**
**THE PROJECT'S OWN LATENCY MODEL IS WRONG.** `.work/sandbox/harness/latency_model.py` disagrees with the codec in **four places and is 35 % low at 1080p50** (Agent 4 found two of the four independently). A corrected model matching `omc_config_latency()` on **39 of 39 cells** is delivered, and is independently checked by six further cells including slice heights no default format exercises.
**THREE UNCOUNTED TERMS found in Part 3:** the whole-frame input un-blend and the frame-end reference rotation — **both per-frame bursts landing inside one slice's budget** — and **concealment searching DOWNWARD for a neighbour, which defers a lost slice's output by up to a whole frame.** The agent also corrected one claim of his own that was simply wrong (§4.5c), and corrected his own framing of the tANS question after the expert answered it: the whole-slice dependency does not set `T_transmit` (which exists whatever the entropy coder is) — it costs the decoder its **OVERLAP** with arrival, **~6 % of the 1080p50 budget, not the 47 % he first claimed.**
**FABLE'S RULINGS (issued as MEMO 002):**
- **Q1 tANS overlap — NO.** Not worth a bitstream change: ~6 % of budget, compute is the binding constraint, and a stream-minor bump is a decoder redeployment we must spend on the fill instead (IP review: "spend that once, on the version that reaches zero").
- **Q2 `a2_strict` — DEFAULT IT TO 1 in the product build.** Measured, every one of these is reachable from the shipped CLI, prints "WARNING A2" and **encodes**: 720p50 `--slice-h 32` reports **1.793 ms**; `--slice-h 16 --uc-ratio 1` **1.194 ms**; `--slice-h 16 --uc-ratio 2` **1.306 ms**; `--slice-h 32 --uc-ratio 2` **2.147 ms**. **A2 says sub-1 ms with no exceptions at every supported resolution from the 720p floor up.** A bar that warns and proceeds is not a bar. The defaults are safe; the guard is not.
- **Q3 — YES, the encoder must consult `omc_uc_scale_latency_ex()`.** The CLI's A2 warning calls `omc_config_latency()`, which knows only the dyadic path, so **rational conversions are not covered at all** and the rational checker is called by no product code path. Defect.
- **Q4 — ONE RULE, and it is the encoder's** (`height <= 720 ? 8 : 16`, as in `config.c:36`, `codec.c:3294`, `omc_enc.c:227`, `omc_loop.c:73`). `omc_uc_tool.c:171` uses `(H >= 2160 && H % 16 == 0) ? 16 : 8` and therefore **understates 1080p → 2160p conversion latency as 0.463 ms where the shipped configuration is 0.762 ms.** Fix the tool.
- **Q10 — CORRECT ALL FOUR STATEMENTS to the measured 48-at-defaults**, in `HARDWARE.md` §7, `HW_TIMING_METHOD.md` §3, `codec.c:2234` and the `OMC_GAMUT_MAXPASS` comment. **FPGA-first (H.0) requires bounded work to be stated correctly; a bound that is published too small is worse than none, because it will be provisioned against.**
- **Q6 concealment — measure, do not assume.** A2's "constant and deterministic" carries no loss exception and Task C exists for loss, so the presumption is that concealment must not look downward; but the quality cost of upward-only concealment is unmeasured and I will not rule it blind. Commissioned with branches.
- **Q7/Q8/Q9 — yes, yes, yes.** State the streaming un-blend form normatively before an RTL team inherits `omc_enc_frame()` as written; carry the pipeline depth as its own model term rather than charging it zero; and **lossless 4:4:4 12-bit being unreachable through the CLI is a defect** — `omc_enc` refuses `bits_per_slice` above a 24 bpp equivalent while the source is 36 bits/pixel, so `--lossless` reports 0/2 frames bit-exact and cannot do better. Lossless is a claimed mode; the guard has outgrown the format matrix.
- **Q11 `slice_h` 32 below 2160p — SPEC DEFECT, mine to resolve.** `BITSTREAM.md` §7 contains both readings **twelve lines apart**: *"an implementation that declares support for 32 must size for it"* (optional, declared) and *"not a per-leg profile and not a conformance point"* (universal). **Those cannot both be operative.** The latency half is settled — the section already prohibits 32 below 2160p and the agent's model agrees independently (720p50 **1.794 ms**, 1080p50 **1.213 ms**, 1080p60 **1.011 ms**, all over; 2160p50 0.607 ms passes) — but byte 12 carries `slice_h` with nothing in the syntax narrowing it by resolution, so **a conformant decoder can be handed 32 at 1080p**, and by the owner's own rule (S5.40) *an encoder-only prohibition is not a bound*. **The answer changes Agent 4's memory numbers, not Agent 5's latency ones.**
- **Q13 legal-range repair — take the expert's option (3), and it is the same answer the IP review reached independently.** He offered four, least to most invasive: (1) prove a conservative coefficient-safe region from the lifting schedule; (2) a normatively finite repair projection with a guaranteed-feasible fallback; **(3) move range legality into the rate-control candidate set so the controller only ever compares LEGAL candidates — "search within a legal subset" instead of "search, then repair, then perhaps invalidate the rate"**; (4) change the canonical sample domain. **Option (3) is IP review §5.1 category (d) — "modifying coded data so the output lands in range, without clipping … lower risk than it looks; encoder-only, emits an ordinary conformant bitstream"** — and it converts the largest content-dependent compute stage into a hard bound rather than a large one, which is exactly what the compute-stall finding needs. **It is complementary to the review's §5.3 plain-clamp prescription, not an alternative to it: the clamp guarantees correctness, (3) removes the compute spike.** Not built yet; scoped in MEMO 002.
**OWNER QUESTION, and it decides how much of the above matters: which rate tier must the encoder be predictable at?** The compute swing is **1.4x at 4.0 bpp, 3.9x at 1.0, and 11–16x at 0.5 and below**, and the wrong published caps are exceeded **only in the low tier**. `docs/HARDWARE.md` §7 explicitly budgets a *"low tier 0.4 bpp (program)"*, so the low tier appears to be in scope — and if it is, **hardware must be provisioned for ~16x the mean slice.** If the contribution profile is ≥ 1.0 bpp the issue is much smaller. Also to put to the owner: **is anyone provisioning hardware from the wrong published bounds today?**

### S5.51 — OWNER RULINGS on Task E's two questions (2026-09-05, on S5.50)
**1. THE PREDICTABILITY GUARANTEE APPLIES FROM 0.5 bpp UP — not 1.0, and not down to 0.4.** The owner declined both offered options and set the floor himself at **0.5 bpp**. Consequences, all of which follow from Agent 5's own measurements:
- **The provisioning target is the 0.5 bpp swing: worst slice ≈ 11.2x the mean** (his figure for 0.5 specifically; the 11–16x range he quoted spans 0.4–0.5, and the 16x end sits below the new floor). Hardware must be sized for ~11x the mean slice, not for 1.4x and not for 16x.
- **`docs/HARDWARE.md` §7's budgeted "low tier 0.4 bpp (program)" now sits OUTSIDE the predictability guarantee** and must say so. 0.4 bpp still encodes; it is not a determinism target. This is a documentation change with product meaning and it goes in the same pass as the four wrong bounds.
- **Agent 5's option (3) — range legality inside the rate-control candidate set — is now LOAD-BEARING, not an optimisation.** At an 11.2x swing the largest content-dependent stage has to become a hard bound rather than a large one. Its scoping (MEMO 002 §5.2) keeps its honest exit: if the legality test costs as much as the repair it replaces, that is a real answer and the idea stops.
- **A graceful stand-down is NOT the chosen route** — the owner did not take it, and Agent 5's objection stands on its own: the candidate walk exists so the previous generation's plan is always re-found, so a stand-down risks the generation fixed point, which is a core product claim.
- **Note the coherence this produces:** the owner's flatness bar also starts at **0.5 bpp** (2026-09-02, restated S5.47). The product now has ONE floor across bars rather than two, and 0.5 bpp is the lowest rate at which any guarantee is made.
**2. NOBODY IS PROVISIONING HARDWARE FROM THE WRONG BOUNDS TODAY — correct them in place.** No standalone correction note is required. All four statements are corrected to the measured true bound (**48 at defaults, verified adversarially**) in the same pass: `HARDWARE.md` §7 (published 40, measured 128), `OMC_GAMUT_MAXPASS` (16, measured 32), `HW_TIMING_METHOD.md` §3 (48, actual `OMC_LOCK_CANDS` 4096), and `codec.c:2234`'s own comment (24, measured 33). **The FPGA-first rule stands behind this: a published bound that is too small is worse than no bound, because it will be provisioned against — it simply has not been yet.**

### S5.52 — Agent 4's MEMO 002 response (Task D, second pass): the part question NARROWS, a second encoder-only bound of his own found and corrected, and a BITSTREAM decision that must be made BEFORE v5.4 freezes (2026-09-05; `Agents/Agent4/MEMO_002_response.md`, 882 lines, base `v54tree_int`; codec expert consulted twice, Agents 1 and 5 both contributed)
**THE PART FINDING IS MUCH NARROWER THAN S5.40's, AND IT PARTLY CORRECTS THE OWNER'S PREMISE.** Block-accurate re-derivation (`notes/uram_packing.py`; URAM288 = 4096 x 72 bits; ZU7EV = 96 blocks): **ZU7EV holds everything up to and including 2160p 4:4:4 12-bit (both coefficient buffers in UltraRAM, 66–90 of 96 blocks), and holds 8K 4:2:2 10-bit too at slice_h 16 (79–94 of 96) provided the packing is exact and the store narrows. Only 8K 4:4:4 12-bit needs a larger part (ZU19EG / KU15P class), and it is UltraRAM-BOUND rather than capacity-bound — on such a part the coefficient buffer simply moves to BRAM.** The owner's S5.40 ruling was taken on a table that said every format fits ZU7EV with no cap; **that was naive-packed and it was wrong for 8K. 4K in all formats is comfortable (~19 % headroom); 8K 4:2:2 fits at slice_h 16 and NOT at 32; 8K 4:4:4 does not fit.** Branch 3 of MEMO 002's tree taken correctly: spec stopped at the part section (`DDR_WINDOW_CACHE.md` §7 now reads *"a requirement, not yet a specification: pending the owner's part decision"*), numbers written, smallest class named per format, **no cap invented, ruling not re-opened**, parts 2–5 finished on the assumption a sufficient part is chosen.
**HE FOUND A SECOND FIGURE OF HIS OWN RESTING ON ENCODER BEHAVIOUR — the rule from S5.40 applied by the agent to himself, and this one was worse than the first.** The frame store was sized at `depth` bits **from a measurement of what OUR encoder emits**; the format's own bound is the decoder's clamp at `maxv + 2·OMC_REF_BIAS` = **13 bits at every depth**, which put **~30 % on every traffic and memory figure at 10-bit**. He also found the band must be sized for the **worst legal `slice_h`, not the shipped one**, and that **the dominant on-chip structure at 8K is not his band at all — it is the slice coefficient buffers**, and that the tANS table figure in **both** existing project documents is wrong for a decoder **in opposite directions**.
**A RECOMMENDATION OF HIS OWN WAS WRONG IN THE WORST DIRECTION, and he corrected it:** he had written "8K 4:2:2 at a 13-bit store → ZU11EG". **ZU11EG has 80 UltraRAM blocks against ZU7EV's 96** — it trades UltraRAM for BRAM, so moving there would have given LESS of the resource we are short of. Corrected everywhere.
**THE 8K CLIFF WAS UltraRAM WORD PACKING, NOT BUFFER COUNT.** The UltraRAM word is a fixed 72 bits and **neither 13 nor 16 divides it**: 5 x 13-bit samples per word (65 of 72) and 4 x 16-bit coefficients per word (64 of 72) **waste ~10 % of every block — about the size of the entire shortfall.** He had been counting bits, not blocks. Exact stripes recover it: 10-bit 36 samples per 5 words = 100 %; **12-bit 6 per word = 100 % with no stripe at all**; 13-bit 72 per 13 words; 16-bit 9 per 2 words. The stripe address generator is a divide-by-constant = multiply-by-reciprocal on constants, **no per-pixel multiplier, C3-safe**. **12 bits is the magic width for UltraRAM (72/12 = 6, zero waste) — a second, independent argument for narrowing the store on top of the traffic argument.**
**THE NORMATIVE CLIP — THREE INDEPENDENT LINES HAVE NOW CONVERGED ON THE SAME CHANGE.** The expert **rejected** Agent 4's `depth + 1` sizing as *"the same error you were corrected for the first time — a measurement of our own encoder is not a bound"*, and prescribed instead: **clip the committed picture normatively at BOTH ENDS to `bias + [0, maxv]`.** Then the store is `depth` bits **by construction**; `rt = 0` survives because both ends apply the identical clip; **and the generation induction gets STRONGER, because clipping is idempotent — the chain becomes a projection onto a finite set closed under the operator, rather than a bound asserted by a clamp constant.** It also removes the C8 burden on third-party encoders, and it is what VC-2 and every deployed inter codec do. Built as `OMC_CLIPGAMUT` (normative, both ends); 8-generation CDR and baseband chains running, including 720p @4.0 and 4:4:4 cells that exercise 9/7-M per the expert's caution. **THE CONVERGENCE:** this is the same change the updated IP review prescribes in its §5.3 (*"apply the fill unmodified, then a single unconditional saturation to the bit-depth constant, identically at both ends, with no signalled or derived parameter"*, S5.48) and it is adjacent to Agent 5's option (3) (S5.50/S5.51) — **memory sizing, legal exposure and the encoder's largest compute spike all point at the same normative clip, reached independently three times.** **The follow-on prize Agent 4 names: the in-gamut repair step could probably be DELETED** — which is exactly Agent 5's 11.2x compute swing and the IP review's category-(d) concern. **The IP review's §5.4 caution binds it: rewrite the generation-lock proof before the code, do not carry it over by analogy** (`omc1.h:70–78` names the unclipped biased domain as one of three pillars).
**THE BITSTREAM DECISION THAT MUST BE MADE BEFORE v5.4 FREEZES — line-based inverse DWT.** The expert named the one lever that would remove the whole-slice coefficient buffer entirely: a **line-based inverse DWT** (Chrysafis & Ortega 1999 plus the VLSI follow-on literature), holding O(levels x width) line buffers instead of O(slice height x width) — **order 1–2 Mbit instead of 5.90 at 8K 4:4:4**. **It requires coefficients to arrive row-interleaved across bands, so it is a COEFFICIENT SCAN-ORDER DECISION IN THE BITSTREAM, not an implementation choice — a C8 item, dramatically cheaper before freeze than after.** Logged as the largest available memory lever, owned by whoever owns the bitstream. **IP note from the agent, and it is the right instinct: JPEG XS is line-based and the resemblance will be noticed; the schedule is 1999 open literature predating it by two decades, so take it from Chrysafis/Ortega and cite the vintage per C1 — do NOT read JPEG XS's normative text for it.**
**REJECTED WITH REASONS RECORDED (durable arguments):** the expert's option (b), serialising the forward DWT ahead of entropy decode inside one slice period — needs ~3x the entropy decode rate, and **tANS is a serial state recurrence whose parallelism is a BITSTREAM property**, so it would cost a syntax change, rate efficiency against the A1 mandate, **3x tANS table replication in BRAM (68 → ~204 blocks against a ZU7EV's ~305 total)**, and A2 schedule slack. And the expert's single-coefficient-buffer scheme: **they CONCEDED it — two buffers is correct**, because a row–column inverse DWT holds the whole slice so slice k+1's prediction cannot be written into the same buffer during slice k. **Buffer count is set by PIPELINE DEPTH, not by prediction-vs-residual: separate + cross-slice pipelined = 4; separate, not pipelined = 2; in-place accumulate + pipelined = 2; in-place accumulate, not pipelined = 1. So in-place accumulate is worth adopting as the insurance that keeps us at 2 rather than 4 the moment cross-slice pipelining is needed. Recorded as a design rule.**
**FABLE'S READING CORRECTION TO THE MEMO ITSELF:** §6.6 still poses the single-vs-two coefficient buffer question as open and warns that "if the answer comes back two, subtract 5.9–11.8 Mbit of relief from the 8K rows". **That question is closed by §4ter.1 in the same memo — the expert conceded and two buffers is correct — and §4ter.3's final part table already assumes two ("two buffers and no single-buffer trick").** §6.6 is stale from the incremental write; the part table stands as written. No action needed from the agent.
**CROSS-AGENT WORK, all of it useful:** **Agent 5's question made him test a stall-and-sprint compute profile — every format still meets its deadline with positive margin under it.** **Agent 1 confirmed the ±16 px block-vector rule costs nothing** — their block vectors are deltas on the region vector but the search bounds the ABSOLUTE total at ±15 vertical / ±31 horizontal by construction, so the sum can never leave the header field; measured committed totals over 17,820 blocks per cell: soccer2 [−15, +12] vertical, runC [−15, +10], runner [−9, +9]. **So the 97-row band and all its BRAM figures stand — and Agent 1 rightly asks that it be written as a NORMATIVE DECODER-SIDE EXPECTATION rather than left resting on an encoder search that happens to respect it**, which is Fable's own S5.40 rule applied back to Fable. Done in the spec. Agent 1 also confirmed the half-pel vertical tap reads `sy0` and `sy0+1` only, matching the `sh + 32` already assumed. **Agent 5 and Agent 4 independently reached the same reading of the `slice_h` 32 spec defect from latency and memory respectively.**
**DELIVERED AND GATED:** every gate green on a frozen build — **20/20 chains, 9/9 byte-identity, all packet/pixel/loss gates**, packet gates re-run after two header fields added on the expert's advice. **`refresh_r == 1` fix delivered as its own diff with its own gate — and that gate caught a segfault the agent had introduced with it.** §7 of `DDR_WINDOW_CACHE.md` deleted; `OMC_MVYCAP` demoted to a probe. **Diagnostic honesty:** of the expert's two "tells" on his excursion data, **tell 1 evaporated — that row was his own harness defect, withdrawn**; tell 2 survives and is the whole finding (3 samples, all at 0.5 bpp, on 720p and graphics = the boundary/edge-overshoot signature predicted, the benign explanation), with per-sample coordinate logging added (`OMC_CLIPSTAT=2`) so it can be confirmed rather than inferred.
**OPEN, FOR THE OWNER:** (1) **is 8K 4:4:4 in the product?** — it is the only format that does not fit the chosen part class; (2) **the line-based inverse DWT scan-order decision, before the bitstream freezes.** **OPEN, FOR FABLE:** the `slice_h` 32 conformance question (now a hardware decision, not academic — at 16 lines 8K 4:2:2 runs on the part we have, at 32 it does not); whether the store-narrowing route is taken (subject to the agent's three conditions: our encoder does not currently meet the constraint, the clamp should be derived by affine arithmetic rather than asserted, and the chains must be re-run on 9/7-M specifically because generation exactness may be relying on the wide domain to absorb per-level shifts); the decoder output path from DDR vs a 2·`slice_h` line buffer (saves 8.85 Mbit at 4K 4:4:4, 17.69 at 8K, costs one more frame read — priced, not chosen, belongs with the part decision); and the stale `HARDWARE.md` §2/§8 figures (tANS table set **8.6x too small**, and the "297 KB on-chip decoder" that follows from it).

The review's read: the **classic form** — a fixed-weight overlapped blend across block boundaries — is **H.263 Annex F advanced prediction mode (1996) and MPEG-4 Part 2, thoroughly expired**; **AV1's OBMC** is a more elaborate construction (causal neighbour selection, variable block sizes, specific blending masks) and is **live AOM-member territory, reachable only under the AOM licence, which covers AV1 implementations and does not extend to a codec that is not AV1.** Provisional read **from description, not code**: an unconditional fixed odd-weight ramp over ±8 luma pixels applied wherever two neighbouring blocks' vectors differ, with no inspection of picture content in the decision, is close to the classic form and **likely well covered by expired art — a starting hypothesis for the search, not a clearance.** **THE THREE QUESTIONS THE SEARCHER NEEDS SETTLED FIRST, and they decide whether this is a footnote or a FIFTH pre-release item: (a) is the blend normative or encoder-side; (b) is anything about it signalled in the bitstream; (c) are the ±8 ramp and the neighbour rule fixed constants or derived from anything?** Assigned to Agent 1.
**(3) The removed edge veto, recorded with its reasoning.** An earlier configuration inspected the reference picture's gradient at each block boundary and suppressed the blend where a real edge sat there. Removed on engineering grounds that were not close (**59-cell corpus +14.668 → +19.286, worst cell −0.106 → −0.015**, and it eliminated committed samples falling outside the legal range), **reversing the responsible engineer's own earlier recommendation.** Recorded as *"an engineering decision with a favourable IP side effect, which is how it was offered and how it should stand."* **The general principle, and it recurs: *a conditional performance of a claimed method still infringes on the occasions the condition fires.* The veto never bought avoidance of anything — it added a SECOND surface (a content-inspecting decision rule) on top of whatever the blend itself reads onto. Deleting it removes that surface and leaves the base exposure where it already was.** **Delete the lever rather than disabling it** (action 2b now covers `OMC_OB_EDGE` as well as `OMC_FILLRAIL`), with a stronger reason available from our own codebase: `include/omc1.h:303–308` already states *"Never an environment variable: a lever that changes normative reconstruction from the environment is an encoder/decoder disagreement channel."* Git history serves reproducibility.
**(4) §3.3 in-gamut repair — adjacency noted, VERDICT UNCHANGED, and one instruction that binds us.** The loop is content-dependent range enforcement driven by the legal bounds and sits near the "adaptive clipping" art of §5. **It stays CLEAR for a structural reason: it never saturates an output sample, it is encoder-only, and it emits an ordinary conformant bitstream — "that is the weakest infringement posture available."** *"Name it in the FTO search scope so coefficient-domain range enforcement is covered; **do not redesign it ahead of the result**."*
