### S5.72 — THE PLAN THE STREAM ALREADY CARRIES IS SUFFICIENT: coefficients regenerate BYTE-IDENTICALLY with the candidate walk disabled outright, on 6/6 cells — and the 15.9 % swing is NOT the lock walk (2026-09-05; `Communication/Agent5_toFable_EARLY_plan_sufficiency.md`, MEMO 007 §5.3 branch 1)
**THE RESULT: 6 cells, 2 frames each, `out/plansuff.log` — forced re-encode vs the fixed-point stream is IDENTICAL on every one, with ZERO slices refused.** dng 1080p 4:2:2 10-bit @0.5 and @2.0, dng 1080p 4:4:4 12-bit @0.5 and @2.0, fbgame 4:2:2 10-bit @0.5, cf_gfx graphics @2.0 (136 slices each, 64 for cf_gfx). **`N_lock = 1` is reachable on the normal path.**
**HE CORRECTED FABLE'S TEST FRAMING BEFORE RUNNING IT, and the correction is structural: the fixed point does not start at generation 1.** At generation 1 from a camera master **no slice locks at all — 0 of 136, measured — because verify demands bit-exact reproduction of its input, so a locking slice would have to be coded losslessly.** "S1 vs re-encode(R1)" therefore compares two streams that are **not required to be equal**. The chain he used instead: `S1 = enc(master)`, `R1 = cdr(S1)`, `S2 = enc(R1)` — **S2 is the first fixed-point stream** — `R2 = cdr(S2)`, `S3 = enc(R2)`, and `S3f = enc(R2)` with the plan **forced from S2's headers and the walk disabled**. The test is `S3f == S2` byte for byte.
**THE SUFFICIENT SET IS SMALLER THAN FABLE SPECIFIED, and this contradicts part of the expert's analysis.** Forced from S2's own 48-byte headers by `harness/lat_planparse.py`: **Q, profile, n_steps, partial_chunks, the mode mask, the fill bits and the per-plane fill gain.** **He did NOT force the per-band tANS table-group ids and did NOT force the motion vectors — and the streams came out identical anyway, so those are RE-DERIVED CORRECTLY from the reconstruction and are not part of the necessary descriptor.** The codec expert's S5.70 split listed *"entropy-table IDs when they are merely coding choices"* and *"motion vectors and mode mask if multiple prediction decompositions reconstruct the same picture"* under **NOT recoverable from pixels**. **This is a direct empirical contradiction of two of his items and he should be told.** Agent 5 is careful: *"I can tell you what suffices, not what is minimal."*
**DESCRIPTOR WIDTH, MEASURED:** over 272 slices (dng 1080p @2.0) the tuple (Q, profile, n_steps, partial_chunks) takes **21 distinct values → 5 bits to name one.** The header already carries 30 bits for it.
**THREE CONTROLS, because this is the class of instrument that lies — and all three were demanded or borrowed.** **(a) The wrong-plan control Fable required:** `OMC_PLANFORCE_WRONG=3` perturbs Q and n_steps and **the stream differs on all 6 cells** — a wrong plan does not produce the right stream, so the instrument is not inert. **(b) The walk disabled OUTRIGHT, not merely overridden:** his first version set the forced plan *after* the walk had run, which leaves open that some side effect of its running mattered; he then set `e->nlcand = 0` so **the walk loop never executes**, rebuilt, re-ran — **still 6/6 identical** (`out/plansuff_overrideonly.log` is the first run, `out/plansuff.log` the second). **(c) Agent 2's positional verifier, which he asked for specifically because his own could have been fooled the way the earlier pin was.** Agent 2 told him their `h_planfit.sh` **PROPOSES rather than FORCES** — the same `goto encode_attempts` mechanism as the inert pin — and that its value is as the **verifier**: compare handed against **committed** plans positionally and report a length difference as its own condition. Implemented as `harness/lat_planheld.py`, parsing the plan back out of `S3f`: **`PLANHELD : HELD 0/136 slices differ (0.00 %)` on five cells and 0/64 on cf_gfx.** **His force REFUSES rather than falls back** — an overflow prints `PLANFORCE-REFUSE` with slice, plan, `used_bits` and budget and returns a hard error, never laddering and never re-planning. **It fired zero times, which is itself the result.**
**THE LIMIT, AND IT IS THE IMPORTANT HALF: this bounds `N_lock` from generation 2 onward and does NOTHING for generation 1 — and generation 1 is the live contribution encode.** Measured (`vtries` = lock verifications per slice, dng 1080p 4:2:2 10-bit): **generation 1 from the master — 0 of 136 slices locked, vtries mean 0.00, max 0**; generation 2 from CDR @0.5 — 136/136 locked, mean **18.3**, max **84**; @2.0 — 136/136, mean **34.1**, max **81**.
**CONSEQUENCE THAT ANSWERS THE EXPERT'S Q2 BY MEASUREMENT: at generation 1 the walk does not lock a single slice, so THE 15.9× WORST-SLICE SWING MEASURED ON MASTERS IS NOT THE LOCK WALK AT ALL — it is the emit and repair loops, both of which are boundable.** The expert's taxonomy separated a variance problem from a provability problem and said *"you should not infer one from the other"*; **the attribution is now measured and they are indeed different: the unbounded term does not execute in the live first encode, and the term that does execute there is bounded in principle.** The expert's correction to Fable stands untouched — *a live contribution encoder does not get a free first generation* — and this result does not soften it.
**WHAT IT BUYS, wall clock, generation-2 encode, 3 runs each: −54 % at 0.5 bpp (3.56 s → 1.62 s) and −44 % at 2.0 (3.17 s → 1.79 s). Roughly half the generation-2 encoder disappears, and the unbounded term disappears with it — but only on hops 2 and beyond.**
**WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT PROVE.** It proves **sufficiency**: the carried plan is enough to regenerate the bytes. It does **not** prove **recoverability**: the test read the plan from S2's headers, which a baseband hop destroys. **The expert's collision experiment — do two distinct plans produce the same hand-off picture — remains the open gate for topology (b).** Under the owner's S5.70 correction, sufficiency is already enough for topology (a), the OMC-to-OMC hop where a side channel is permitted.
**NO BUILD, NO DESCRIPTOR, NO NORMATIVE PROPOSAL, candidate list untouched** — `[A5-PLANFORCE]` is an A/B probe in `tree_planforce/`, defaulting to shipped behaviour, offered for nothing.
**A BITSTREAM FACT HE HAD WRONG AND CORRECTED, flagged because "it may be in other people's heads too": SLICES ARE VARIABLE LENGTH ON THE WIRE.** A slice is `48 + ceil(used_bits/8)` bytes; measured stride **7,589–7,823 for a nominal 7,680**. The **frame** is exactly `nslices × slice_bytes`; the slice is not. **A parser that strides by `bits_per_slice/8` desynchronises after slice 0 — his did, and it failed loudly rather than quietly, "which is the only reason I noticed."**

Nothing was re-run except the renders, which had not met the magnification rule.** He also reports the earlier catches: his in-codec plan-fit check was wrong **in the specific way Agent 2 warned him it would be, and their control caught it**; his flatness numbers needed proving to be the bar's quantity rather than raw flatness before any verdict could rest on them; and **his first stand-down eye crop landed on a genuinely smooth region and would have shown nothing either way**, so it had to be re-aimed at the blocks the meter actually flagged.

### S5.74 — THE EXPERT'S THIRD ANSWER: Fable's "canonicalisation is the only route" is REJECTED as too strong; the architecture is a HIERARCHY; and the grain fill moves from suspect to LEADING MECHANISM with a structural trilemma attached (2026-09-05)
**HE ATTACKED FABLE'S READING, WHICH FABLE ASKED FOR, AND FABLE WAS WRONG.** *"Does this make canonicalization the only route? **No. Your conclusion is too strong.**"* Descriptors buy real value even given the GFX case: they eliminate the generation-2 lock search for unchanged OMC-to-OMC hops (**54 % of low-rate wall clock, our own measurement**); they enable **per-slice** fast paths in mixed frames — *"a lower-third may dirty only a small vertical region while most slices remain eligible for a one-attempt path"*; they are **an independent verification oracle for developing a picture-only canonicaliser**; they allow exactness-preserving bypass/remux; and they let an OMC-aware processor distinguish "known untouched" from "must conservatively replan". **"Topology (a) buys something real: it shrinks the number of slices requiring canonicalization from 'all' to 'only changed or unknown.'"**
**THE ARCHITECTURE IS A HIERARCHY, NOT A CHOICE:** `verified descriptor → bounded canonicaliser → bounded non-exact fallback → explicit failure / non-real-time recovery`. ***"The hard problem is the second arrow."*** If a generic GFX node makes a slice UNKNOWN, what happens next **must still meet the low-latency promise — "you cannot make the answer 'run the unbounded plan walk' and retain deterministic timing."*** Framing to keep: **the descriptor provides TEMPORAL locality (unchanged content reuses a cached successful plan); canonicalisation provides CONTENT locality (any picture maps to a bounded canonical plan from its observable reconstruction). They solve different, complementary cases.**
**HE RETRACTED HIS OWN EARLIER POSITION, unprompted.** *"I would retract the idea that the unbounded walk is automatically fatal merely because it resides in the same binary. What matters is reachability in the latency-guaranteed execution profile."* A single binary may safely contain a deterministic source-ingest path with `N_lock = 0`, a paired OMC-to-OMC exact-chain path with `N_lock = 1`, and a non-real-time conformance path that may run the general walk. **"What you cannot do is claim content-independent deterministic latency for a profile in which the general unbounded walk remains a reachable fallback."**
**Q1 ANSWERED — YES, CONDITIONALLY, and the condition is a word we had not thought about.** If the generation-1 low-latency profile can prove `N_lock = 0` **for every ADMITTED source slice**, a complete counted bound over the nested emit/repair control flow is sufficient in principle. ***"The key word is ADMITTED. 'Camera master' is not a machine-checkable format condition by itself."*** Four defensible ways to define it: a normative rule that generation-1 input is always treated as non-locking and lock verification is disabled by profile; an explicit generation-state flag or side channel saying "new source, no exact-lock test"; a bounded preliminary classifier that determines whether lock logic is reachable; or a split product promise separating deterministic source-ingest from a non-real-time exact-chain conformance mode. **And the timing budget must fit the slice period with hard margin because XSL serialises committed slices — "there is no 'average throughput will catch up later' argument available."**
**THE GFX CASE — the owner's question — answered, and it needs a THREE-STATE model, not a Boolean.** He separates four properties we had conflated: descriptor **integrity** (received uncorrupted), **provenance** (originated with the upstream OMC stream), **validity** (corresponds to the exact pixels presented now), and **suitability** (still a good rate-distortion decision for modified pixels). **"A graphic inserter can preserve descriptor integrity and provenance while invalidating descriptor validity. Even if the old plan still fits, it may no longer be a good coding decision."** The model: **`VERIFIED_IDENTICAL`** (token and picture binding verify; force the descriptor once), **`DECLARED_MODIFIED`** (an OMC-aware node cleared the token), **`UNKNOWN`** (token absent, invalid, unrecognised, mismatched or untrusted). ***"`UNKNOWN` must be treated exactly like modified content for correctness."*** **A per-slice token must BIND the plan to the exact pixels, not merely identify the plan:** `H_k = Hash(format_id, k, P_k, R_k, S_{k−1})`, own-work design after legal review, and **not a bare CRC if a collision could let an invalid descriptor be treated as valid.**
**AND HE CONFIRMS THE OWNER'S INSTINCT ABOUT THIRD-PARTY DEVICES:** *"Do not make validity depend on third-party nodes behaving correctly."* A generic graphics inserter is neither codec-aware nor metadata-aware and will not see, preserve or clear an OMC descriptor. **Conservative default: no verified descriptor ⇒ descriptor invalid.** On carriage: ST 2110 keeps video, audio and ancillary as **separate synchronised flows** (ST 2110-40 carries ST 291-1 ANC in RTP), so a token is technically carriable in a managed system — *"but it also illustrates why it cannot be assumed to survive arbitrary routing or processing: the associated data is a separate flow and can be omitted, replaced, or separated from video."* Same caution for SDI ANC. **The fail-safe is that a generic device's output simply has no trustworthy token and therefore cannot use the fast path — it does not need to clear anything.**
**§5 — THE MISSING BOUNDED PATH, and this is the real product requirement the GFX question exposed:** *"What is the bounded, low-latency plan-selection method for new or modified picture content at 0.5 bpp?"* **"If the answer remains an unbounded lock/candidate walk, no descriptor protocol can fix worst-case latency for arbitrary production modifications."** Four honest resolutions: **(1) bounded canonicalisation** — `P = C(R, S_{k−1})` over a finite profile family, accepting the rate-distortion cost; **(2) bounded constrained planner** — fixed maximum candidate set and deterministic fallback for modified slices, which may lose the strongest exactness property in those slices unless the fallback is itself canonical; **(3) system-level admission control** — restrict the profile to workflows where modified slices come from an OMC-aware compositor; **(4) relax the product promise** — technically honest, *"likely undermines the headline claim."* **He recommends pursuing 1 and 2 IN PARALLEL:** build a minimal canonical profile family first (fixed profile, `n_steps`, allocation-table class, a small bounded `Q` rule), keep the descriptor fast path for `VERIFIED_IDENTICAL` slices, **define a fixed fallback plan for dirty slices that always fits CBR even if visually conservative**, and **measure how often real GFX workflows dirty full 16-line slices**.
**§6 — THE GRAIN FILL IS NOW THE LEADING MECHANISM FOR THE 8-BIT DEFECT, and it carries a STRUCTURAL TRILEMMA.** *"This is an excellent diagnostic result. It moves grain fill from a speculative suspect to the leading mechanism."* His hypothesis: **`Q_s(ĉ_s(m) + g_s) ≠ m` even where `Q_s(ĉ_s(m)) = m` holds fill-free** — at 8 bits a fill amplitude that is a fixed fraction of Δ can repeatedly push marginal values **across a decision boundary or in/out of the dead zone**; the next generation quantises a different index, reconstructed coefficients shift slightly, and **across generations that produces exactly the monotonic contraction we measured until all affected values land in stable cells.**
***"THE LIKELY FAULT IS NOT NECESSARILY A SIMPLE GRAIN IMPLEMENTATION BUG. It may be a FORMAT-LEVEL INCOMPATIBILITY between a fixed fractional-step fill and a generation-exactness requirement… If so, you cannot retain all three of: fractional grain fill; ordinary scalar dead-zone quantization; generation-2 exactness across picture-only re-encoding."*** **Possible structural repair: constrain the fill to a self-quantising lattice `g_s ∈ Δ_s ℤ`, or — more realistically — require centroid plus fill to land strictly inside the same quantiser cell, `r_m + g_s ∈ interior(I_m)`, for every permitted `m, s`.** That permits sub-step fill only if its magnitude is bounded by the distance from each centroid to its nearest decision threshold **including all integer-rounding uncertainty** — and *"it will likely be too restrictive near the dead zone and at saturation, which is exactly where an 8-bit issue would surface."*
**HIS SIX-STEP PROBE, to be run narrowly:** for every active band/plane in the failing 8-bit cell log (1) the pre-fill dequantised centroid `r_m`, (2) the fill contribution `g` **including sign, clipping/saturation and all rounding**, (3) the post-fill coefficient `r_m + g`, (4) the exact quantiser interval and output index on the next encode, (5) **flag every location where `Q_s(r_m + g) ≠ m`**, (6) **compare flagged locations between the failing normal-fill arm and the successful stand-down arm.** Then test whether the fill is applied **in the same domain and order at both ends** — before/after dequantisation, before/after inverse lifting, before/after XSL construction, before/after any internal 8-bit conversion, before/after a legal-range test, and **with the same fixed-point precision and rounding rule in encode and decode.**
**HIS FIVE IMMEDIATE RECOMMENDATIONS:** (1) approve a descriptor fast-path mode with a verified per-slice token and a one-attempt force/refuse path for unchanged slices; (2) **do not make third-party GFX invalidation a requirement** — treat unverified metadata as `UNKNOWN`; (3) **define dirty-slice behaviour now — "a per-slice marker only tells you not to use an old descriptor; it does not create a bounded replacement plan. The dirty-slice planner is the real remaining latency requirement"**; (4) run the collision test, still required before claiming a picture-only canonicaliser; (5) **prioritise the grain-fill algebra — "the experimental controls make this the highest-information next probe."**
**FABLE'S NOTE FOR THE OWNER: the fill is now implicated in THREE separate problems at once — the IP exposure (it is the item the legal review will not sell without a search), the flatness bar (it is the only thing delivering it, and the incumbent fails that bar anyway per S5.73), and now generation exactness. Any decision about the fill is now a decision about all three.**

### S5.75 — OWNER RULING ON THE FILL: "if it causes a problem, rip it out and solve any quality issues another way" (2026-09-05)
**The ruling, verbatim.** It supersedes the design-around track: the question is no longer how to make the fill legally clean, it is whether it stays at all.
**WHAT RIPPING IT OUT BUYS, all of it already measured, none of it speculative:** **(1) IT REMOVES THE LARGEST LEGAL EXPOSURE ENTIRELY** — the fill is the one item the legal review *"would not sell without a search"*, it is normative and in-loop, and twelve design-arounds plus the decoder-estimate route are closed (S5.48). Deleting it deletes the FTO long pole. **(2) IT IMPROVES EVERY FIDELITY MEASURE WE HAVE** (S5.44, 19 owner-owned cell/rate points): fill OFF beats fill ON on **NEG 16 of 19** (up to +1.100), **luma PSNR all 19** (+0.63 to +3.48 dB), **chroma PSNR all 19** (+2.08 to +6.60 dB), **source correlation all 19**, and invented texture goes **100 % → 0 %** on dng 4:2:2 chroma. The expert's third statistic is the sharpest: **the shipped chroma fill measures `E_HP` 2.23 and 2.55 against ≈1.0 for emitting NOTHING — more than twice as wrong as emitting nothing — at a source correlation of +0.013.** **(3) IT PROBABLY REMOVES THE 8-BIT GENERATION DEFECT** — Agent 3 measured that both fill stand-down arms turn the failing cell into a passing one (S5.73), and the codec expert has since made the fill the leading mechanism with a candidate algebra (S5.74). **(4) It ends a trilemma** the expert states as possibly structural: *"you cannot retain all three of: fractional grain fill; ordinary scalar dead-zone quantisation; generation-2 exactness across picture-only re-encoding."*
**WHAT IT COSTS, stated honestly: the flatness bar, and only the flatness bar.** Fill off takes luma flat blocks from **0.00–5.21 % to 1.53–56.53 %** (S5.44). **BUT the bar is not being met today either — Agent 3 ran the SHIPPING codec against it for the first time and it fails on 5 of 6 cells at 0.5 bpp (S5.73).** And the meter itself is unreliable in both directions (S5.42): `flatplane` is a pure energy test, blinded by added energy and blind to the opposite failure. **So the honest statement is not "the fill delivers the bar and removing it loses the bar". It is: nothing delivers the bar today, the fill trades large measured fidelity for an unmet bar, and the instrument we would use to judge the trade cannot tell restored texture from added noise.**
**WHAT DIES WITH IT:** Agent 3's constant-amplitude deliverable (L0/L1) existed to make the fill *legally clean*; if the fill goes, that work is moot and its L1 conclusion is not needed. **`OMC_FILLREACH`** — the live normative boundary-keyed synthesis refusal the review flagged (S5.48) — is a **fill gate**, so it goes with the fill and its own FTO scope item disappears. The rung-keyed stand-down (S5.73) is superseded by outright removal.
**THE ONE DECISION FABLE STILL NEEDS FROM THE OWNER IS TIMING, NOT PRINCIPLE.** Removing the fill is **normative** — it is in every conformant decoder — so it costs a stream-minor bump and a decoder redeployment. **v5.4 already carries ONE bump for four queued normative changes (S5.53). Either the rip-out joins that bump, or v5.4 ships with the fill and the removal costs a SECOND redeployment later.** Fable's recommendation: **join the bump.** One redeployment either way; the legal exposure is what gates first sale; fidelity improves on every axis; it probably removes a shipping generation defect; and the bar it protects is not met today regardless.
**AND ONE LOOK IS NEEDED BEFORE COMMITTING, because no number we own can answer it:** the owner must see **fill-off at 0.5 bpp**, full frame at full resolution, with a magnified crop meeting all three render requirements (S5.69/S5.71), on the cells where the meter reports the worst flatness. **56 % flat blocks by an instrument we have proved unreliable may be invisible or may be unacceptable, and only the owner's eye can say which.** That is the gate on the recommendation, not on the ruling.

### S5.77 — OWNER RULE ON RENDERS: frame selection is part of the instrument. A flatness render must show the TEMPORAL ENGINE AT WORK, not the intra ramp (2026-09-05)
**The owner, on the fill-off render Fable asked for:** *"if I'm being given a 0.5 bpp full frame to detect flatness, it should be the computer screen one and not f0-2. It should be f11 or something similar, **where the temporal engine has done its work**. Hence, the agent shouldn't only render f11, since that would be the same as only rendering intra/f0. **I want to see the results of the temporal engine at play.**"*
**Two separate requirements, and the second is the subtle one.** **(1) Not the ramp.** Frames 0–2 are the intra ramp — PROJECT_CONSTRAINTS exempts them from the full quality bar — so **a render of f0–f2 measures the ramp, not the codec's steady state.** Use a frame deep enough into the refresh period that temporal prediction has acted; **f11 or similar.** **(2) Not a single frame either.** *"The agent shouldn't only render f11, since that would be the same as only rendering intra/f0."* A single steady-state frame is still a single frame. **A run of consecutive frames is required so the temporal engine's behaviour is visible across them** — which is the same principle the owner's own rules already state for crawl: *"Crawl/ants is made visible through motions, meaning, they are revealed over the course of multiple frames."*
**THE FOURTH RENDER REQUIREMENT, added to the three of S5.69/S5.71: FRAME SELECTION.** A render offered for any artifact claim must state **which frames, and why those frames** — a run in the steady state (e.g. f8–f15), never the ramp alone and never one frame alone. **And the clip must suit the artifact:** for flatness at 0.5 bpp that is the **computer-screen/graphics content**, not a camera master. **Rendering the wrong frames is the same class of error as rendering at the wrong magnification: the protocol is followed, the file is correct, and the thing being judged is not the thing that matters.**

### S5.78 — CORRECTION, and it is one the owner says he has had to make repeatedly: THE LEGAL ISSUE IS NOT "FILL OR NO FILL". It is the two SOURCE-DERIVED TRANSMITTED FIELDS. And fill-off's fidelity gains are needed for R=2R (2026-09-05)
**The owner:** *"the main legal issue is not fill overall but the specific type of fill that the IP Review targets. Still, everyone constantly thinks it's fill or no fill. But we do need to keep the benefits of fill off — those we do need for our R=2R goals."*
**FABLE MADE THIS EXACT CONFLATION IN S5.75 and must correct it.** S5.75 said *"the question is no longer how to make the fill legally clean, it is whether it stays at all"*, and MEMO 015 told Agent 3 his constant-amplitude work would be *"moot if the fill goes"*. **Both wrong. The constant-amplitude deliverable IS the legal fix and always was.**
**WHAT THE REVIEW ACTUALLY TARGETS, in its own words: "The base amplitude was always clean; only the modulation is not."** `codec.c:3653,3662` sets the base to `1 << (s − 2)` — **a pure function of the TRANSMITTED quantiser step**, which sits in the dequantisation-reconstruction family beside the centroid offset already shipped. **The exposure is the two fields the encoder MEASURES FROM THE DISCARDED SOURCE and TRANSMITS:** the **2-bit gain** (a quantised measurement of the source's own discarded grain amplitude, `sum += |e->coef|` over positions that quantised to zero, normalised, thresholded, transmitted, and used to scale decoder synthesis by 1.00/1.25/1.50/1.75×) and the **18-bit mask** (`fon` thresholds that identical source-derived mean against `omc_fillthr` and transmits the result — *"a second source-measured parameter, spatially resolved per band and plane, rather than the presence flag it looks like"*). Roughly **24 bits per slice of encoder-measured synthesis control.** **A fill is not the problem. A fill whose parameters are measured from the source and transmitted is.**
**AND THE SECOND HALF, which changes the target: fill-off's fidelity gains are NEEDED, not merely nice.** Measured by Fable on dng 1080p 4:2:2 10-bit @0.5, 12 frames, the same pair rendered for the owner: **NEG 90.195 → 90.443; luma 33.76 → 35.04 dB (+1.28); Cb 31.39 → 34.62 (+3.23); Cr 31.82 → 35.71 (+3.89).** Agent 2's 19-cell corpus (S5.44) gives the same shape everywhere: fill-off better on NEG 16/19, luma PSNR all 19, chroma PSNR all 19, source correlation all 19. **Those are exactly the gains that count toward OMC@R = XS@2R. Keeping the fill as it is spends them; removing the fill spends the flatness bar and, by the owner's eye on the f8–f11 grid, visible detail.**
**THE ACTUAL SPECIFICATION, stated three-way for the first time. A solution must satisfy ALL THREE:**
1. **LEGALLY CLEAN** — no field whose value the encoder chose by looking at the source. Amplitude derived explicitly from the transmitted quantiser step; position from a normative rule; character fixed; **nothing measured from the source, nothing transmitted.** Specified beside dequantisation and **not called grain** in the normative text.
2. **KEEPS FILL-OFF'S FIDELITY** — recover the ~+1.3 dB luma and ~+3 dB chroma and the correlation gain, because they serve the rate mandate.
3. **DOES NOT INCREASE FLATNESS** — hold fill-on's flatness (Y 0.05 %, Cb/Cr 0.00 % at f11 on the measured cell), judged by the PAIRED test with the owner's eye deciding.
**EVERY PREVIOUS ATTEMPT OPTIMISED ONE OR TWO OF THE THREE.** The twelve mask variants and the decoder-derived amplitude chased (1) alone and broke exactness. L0/L1/L2 chased (1) and traded (2) against (3) — no single constant satisfies both because **the split is by content**. The rung-keyed stand-down chased (2) and lost (3). The dither chased (3) and lost (2). **None was ever given all three as the target.**
**TWO ROUTES REMAIN UNEXPLORED AND BOTH ARE COMPATIBLE WITH (1) BY CONSTRUCTION:**
**(a) TARGETING — fill only where it is needed, from state both ends already hold.** Agent 3's own proposal, never commissioned: *"target from state both ends already hold — a local-activity measure coarse enough that ±20 codes cannot change the classification would let the decoder dither only flat regions and the encoder strip the same set."* His diagnosis of why his own dither failed is the argument for it: ***"density and amplitude cannot substitute for TARGETING."*** The shipped fill already fires only where a coefficient quantised to zero; the question is whether a **coarse, decoder-derivable activity classification** can restrict it further — filling genuinely flat regions and leaving textured ones alone. **That attacks (2) and (3) together: keep the flatness benefit, stop paying fidelity where fill was never needed.** It transmits nothing, so (1) holds.
**(b) LATTICE-ALIGNED AMPLITUDE — the codec expert's structural repair.** `g_s ∈ Δ_s·ℤ`, or centroid-plus-fill strictly inside the same quantiser cell, `r_m + g_s ∈ interior(I_m)`. **Removes the generation-exactness failure by construction** (S5.74's trilemma dissolves), and it changes the fidelity arithmetic, because part of the current fill's damage is that it lands *between* lattice points. Amplitude still derives from the step, so (1) holds.
**ONE EXISTENCE PROOF THAT "BETTER ON BOTH" IS REACHABLE:** Agent 3's sparse dither at k2 a20 **beat the shipped fill on BOTH metrics simultaneously on cf_gfx — +0.30 NEG and 4.28 % → 0.00 % flatness — with zero syntax** (S5.42). It did not generalise, and it was abandoned. **It is nonetheless proof that the joint target is not impossible, on at least one content class.**
**AND THE DIAGNOSIS OF WHY THE CURRENT FILL COSTS SO MUCH FIDELITY, which points at both routes:** it fires where it is not needed, and what it emits is **essentially uncorrelated with the source** — `A` 2.0–2.4 at correlation **+0.013**, `E_HP` 2.23–2.55 against ≈1.0 for emitting nothing (S5.44). **More than twice as wrong as emitting nothing. A fill that fired less often and landed on-lattice attacks a different point on the trade entirely.**

### S5.79 — THE R=2R FLATNESS LADDER, measured across all three rate pairs on both codecs: OMC@R BEATS XS@2R ON FLATNESS AT EVERY PAIR — and LOSES to it on texture CORRELATION at every pair (2026-09-05; Fable, owner's question)
**Method:** `dng_1920x1080_422_10` (the screen capture), **12 frames encoded from source frame 0, measured at f11** (steady state, not the ramp). OMC at 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0 with fill ON and fill OFF; **JPEG XS at its best settings** (`--quantization 1 --rc 2 --slice-height 32`, the project-established best per `xsrun.sh`) at the 2R partners **1.0 / 2.0 / 4.0**. Paired test throughout: `flatplane` **and** `texstat` (AMP, PER, COR) per plane. Logs and arms in `.work/scratch/r2r/`.
**FLATNESS — % of textured blocks gone flat, Y / Cb / Cr:**
| pair | **OMC @ R (shipped, fill ON)** | **XS @ 2R** |
|---|---|---|
| **0.5 vs 1.0** | **0.05 / 0.00 / 0.00** | **54.94 / 63.97 / 69.00** |
| **1.0 vs 2.0** | **0.01 / 0.00 / 0.00** | **21.05 / 5.79 / 10.97** |
| **2.0 vs 4.0** | **0.14 / 0.00 / 0.00** | 0.28 / 0.00 / 0.25 |
**On the owner's flatness bar, OMC at R beats JPEG XS at DOUBLE THE RATE at every pair, and by three orders of magnitude at the two low pairs. The owner's concern that flatness threatens the product is NOT borne out by this measurement — on this axis we are far ahead of the incumbent at half its rate.** (Consistent with the single pair measured 2026-09-03, S5-era: XS@2.0 flattened more than OMC@1.0 on 11 of 12 plane-cells, and the owner's eye ruled *"the image on the far right is incredibly flattened"*.)
**BUT THE PAIRED TEST INVERTS IT — texture CORRELATION with the source, Y / Cb / Cr:**
| arm | AMP | **COR** |
|---|---|---|
| **OMC 0.5 fill ON** | 1.017 / 1.138 / 1.297 | **0.768 / 0.103 / 0.110** |
| **XS 1.0 (its 2R partner)** | 0.916 / 0.498 / 0.510 | **0.880 / 0.415 / 0.436** |
| **OMC 1.0 fill ON** | 1.063 / 1.178 / 1.205 | **0.785 / 0.258 / 0.212** |
| **XS 2.0** | 0.945 / 0.836 / 0.763 | **0.922 / 0.731 / 0.671** |
| **OMC 2.0 fill ON** | 1.028 / 1.208 / 1.315 | **0.876 / 0.482 / 0.376** |
| **XS 4.0** | 0.987 / 0.977 / 0.951 | **0.969 / 0.927 / 0.893** |
**JPEG XS at 2R has BETTER texture correlation than OMC at R at every rate pair and on every plane — and the chroma gap is enormous: 0.415 against 0.103 at the first pair, 0.731 against 0.258 at the second, 0.927 against 0.482 at the third.**
**THE MECHANISM, and it is our own fill: OMC puts roughly the RIGHT AMOUNT of texture energy back (AMP 1.02–1.32) but in the WRONG PLACES (chroma COR 0.10–0.48). XS puts LESS energy back (AMP 0.50–0.98, which is why it scores flat) but what it does put back is in the RIGHT PLACES (COR up to 0.93).** This is exactly the *"right amount of energy, in the wrong places"* signature Agent 3 identified when validating the flatness meter — **and here it describes the SHIPPED codec, not an experimental arm.**
**AND FILL-OFF CONFIRMS THE ATTRIBUTION.** Removing the fill makes OMC flatter **and more correct at the same time**: at 0.5 bpp chroma COR rises **0.103 → 0.271 (Cb)** and **0.110 → 0.312 (Cr)** while AMP falls from 1.14/1.30 to 0.41/0.46. At 2.0 bpp fill-off reaches **COR 0.928 / 0.694 / 0.625** against fill-on's 0.876 / 0.482 / 0.376. **Every point of chroma correlation the fill costs is a point XS is beating us by.**
**THE CONCLUSION THAT MATTERS FOR THE MANDATE: we win the flatness bar by INVENTING texture, and we lose the texture-fidelity comparison to the incumbent at double our rate in the same act. The bar and the mandate are pulling in opposite directions, and the fill is the reason.** This is the strongest argument yet for the three-way fill v2 target (S5.78): a **targeted** fill raises COR by not firing where texture was never lost, and a **lattice-aligned** fill raises COR by emitting an amplitude the reconstruction can actually support. **Neither costs a transmitted source-derived field, so both stay legally clean.**
**LIMITS, stated: one clip (a screen capture), one frame (f11), one format (4:2:2 10-bit), 12 frames of source. The direction is consistent across three rate pairs and both instruments, but the corpus is one cell wide and must be widened before any of this is quoted as a mandate figure.** The 12-frame source length is itself the constraint — see S5.80.

### S5.97 — 2026-09-06 — Codec expert reply to MEMO 006 (`~/.claude/uploads/.../e3c220cb-Reply_to_Fable_5.1___baseband_hops...md`): repair stays; in-gamut as BITSTREAM conformance; make the repair exact; truncation not re-plan; ±0.002 % is the wrong number; k−1 is the vertical synthesis (R = 6 rows); the 9-frame outlier vs the refresh period
**§0 (for the owner):** generation exactness is TWO promises. CDR hops: the plan is carried → exactness is a verification, reproducible across vendors once the allocator is normative. Baseband hops: C7 forbids a side channel, the plan is destroyed at every hop, gen n+1 must SEARCH; two conformant encoders satisfying rt = 0 may choose different plans → baseband exactness across implementations needs a NORMATIVE PLAN-SELECTION RULE (specifying the encoder search), unscoped. Decide which promise is sold: "CDR bit-exact; baseband stable within a stated bound" (cheap, true once §1 lands) vs "all generations picture-exact across implementations" (the strongest multi-generation claim any contribution codec has made).
**Q1:** the repair is FORCED on baseband hops (the clipped output IS the next input; exactness requires the clip to change no sample). Trade space closed (widen interface / side channel / move saturation / shrink legal set — only the last is available). **Draft as bitstream conformance:** "every sample of the picture produced by the decoding process shall lie within the legal range; a decoder shall clip any that does not and treat the result as conformant" — testable, makes the output clip provably inactive, the repair becomes an implementation of a requirement (do NOT put the algorithm in the spec). Surviving: derived guard g as DATAPATH width (trial reconstructions go out of gamut); 13-bit stripe packing; W_b + coefficient saturation. **Danger:** a bounded-effort repair under a normative requirement = a non-conformant-bitstream generator (residue 1–2 samples/clip, rising with rate — an effort budget scaled to the step). **Fix:** gamut into the admissibility predicate `rt==0 ∧ model_bits≤budget ∧ in_gamut(reconstruct)` + a provable TERMINAL RUNG: (1) zero the highpass bands — provably in gamut for 5/3 (odd rows = rounded mean of lowpass neighbours, convex) but NOT for (9,7)-M (negative taps); (2) per-slice filter fallback to 5/3 (a C8 syntax commitment); (3) an exact/escape slice mode (in gamut by construction; does not fit CBR → **decide explicitly what gives when gamut and rate collide; measure escape frequency on cf_gfx before sizing the reserve**). gen-6 not gen-1: marginal stability — a tiny per-hop perturbation integrating across a decision threshold (the spent_bits shape again); consider a hysteresis property on re-encode.
**Q2:** rule amended: "feedback from the entropy coder may control padding and TRUNCATION; never quantisation, never plan selection." Re-plan disqualified (re-introduces emitted-bit feedback intra-slice). Truncation must be (1) syntactically expressible — per-slice coded length with early termination (VC-2 LD; JPEG 2000 truncation via HTJ2K under C1) — and (2) the tail of a specified TOTAL ORDER (band, refinement pass, position), finest/highest first; LL and each band's first refinement never reachable. At 0.002 % on an 8K slice the overshoot is ~4 bits — a non-event. **The ±0.002 % is NOT the model error** — it is the permutation experiment's coder-state sensitivity; the quantity that sizes reserve/truncation is `gap = |Σ model codelengths − emitted tANS bits|`: coding approximation (dominant, content-dependent) + tANS final-state flush (~log2 L per stream, EXACT, put in the model) + byte alignment (0–7 bits, exact). **Measure it directly** across the sweep. Model arithmetic normative and integer (1/256-bit units, specified width/saturation/rounding). Lock walk: admitted by construction by INDUCTION over slice index (bank at k = f(plans < k)); three predicates (rt==0, model_bits ≤ budget, in_gamut); locked-generation cost drops to one reconstruct-and-compare. **Trap: verify the EMITTED picture (after truncation), not the planned one** — third placement defect in three memos (clip domain, saturation domain, verification stage).
**Q3:** k−1 is EXPECTED — the 5/3 synthesis update step reads row 2n+1 (below) and predict reads 2n+2; reconstructing a slice's bottom rows needs the slice below. Reach R = 2^(J+1) − 2 = **6 rows** for two vertical levels (more for (9,7)-M: enumerate); **prediction: 720p (8 rows, 75 % affected) k−1 mean ≈ 2× ≥1080p (16 rows, 37.5 %)** — check the ORDERING of the measured 0.18–0.73 means. Tests: row profile within k−1 (bottom-R decaying = transform; flat/top = a write outside the region — bug); **concealment OFF, injector re-run — if k−1 goes clean the concealment writes above its slice (decisive, ten minutes)**; one-level run (R 6 → 2). k+3 one-code residue = integer-lifting non-linearity; **state the footprint by affine arithmetic (`vc2_bit_widths`), not measurement.** Temporal ≥ 9-frame sports outlier: if ≈ the refresh period (8) → bound = "one refresh period", document; if materially longer → prediction is reaching across the refresh boundary (corruption leaks back behind the wave) → a normative restriction on the prediction source relative to refresh state (**IP care: derive from pre-2003 literature; do not read AVC/HEVC constrained-intra / GDR text**). Guarantee wording: "bottom R rows of k−1, all of k, k+1; k+2… only a bounded rounding residue; nothing outside k−1…k+3."
**§4 IP:** all clear except the refresh-boundary prediction constraint (care) and tANS counsel confirmation still owed. **§5:** (1) the §0 decision to the owner; (2) in-gamut as bitstream conformance + exact repair + decide what gives; (3) measure `model_bits − emitted_bits`. ### S5.111 — 2026-09-06 — A2 Msg 15 (complete): the smudge instrument cannot be validated on the owner's boxes; a successor finds a third of the grille marks; by that successor the artifact is in EVERY tree; trailer parked with its state
**Step A:** area precision/recall (his first overlap matcher rewarded a blob — caught). **The 78 non-grille boxes of S3.19 are historical:** inside them the current decode is marginally BETTER than the unmarked frame (|err| 14.4 vs 15.8; HP ratio 1.02 vs 1.07) — the live target is the 9 grille boxes (0.98 % of the frame; |err| 39.7; HP ratio 0.88). **`smudgegroups.py` cannot find them at any setting (best F1 0.031):** it thresholds the SIGNED level map at 6 codes, and the grille boxes' level shift is −2.0…+5.5 codes while their |err| is 33–52 — **the owner's grille marks are texture loss at high absolute error, not level shift; the level-map instrument measures the wrong quantity.** Successor `[A2-SMUDGE2]` (src_hp > p80, err > 2× textured median, hp_ratio < 1.10): precision 0.852, **recall 0.338**, F1 0.484; goes quiet with rate (0.5: 0.39/0.31/0.72 %; 1.0: 0.08/0.25/0.39; 2.0 and 4.0: 0). ### S5.117 — 2026-09-06 — L1-0, the older "cut" failure FOUND: `[S5-DC]` zero-mean lifting rounding × the main-track in-gamut repair's hand-mirrored synthesis
Arms on `v54tree_int`: `OMC_LOCK_TIEACT=0` 0/10, `OMC_MVREG=0` 0/10, Task C refresh reversed 0/10 — all cleared. **`v54tree_int` with `v54tree`'s `dwt.c` (the `[S5-DC]` alternating rounding constant reverted): 0/0 PASS.** `sandbox/sbx_dcbias` carries `[S5-DC]` and passes, so the fix is not wrong on its own: it fails only together with the main-track repair (B-family, absent from the sandbox), which reproduces the 5/3 synthesis arithmetic by hand to predict which coefficient change clears a rail sample. That mirror still uses the old half-up constants, so on hard plates its prediction is off by one code on alternate pairs and the last 10 samples are never cleared — the "exactness by hand-mirrored search" defect class the IP review names (its §? line 244). Coordinator's merge defect (2026-09-04). Fix: make the repair's mirror use the same `(i & 1)` alternation as `dwt.c:143/147` (or call the transform rather than mirroring it); gate: G-T5-CUT4 "cut" 0 on `_next`, chains, recovery, byte-identity where the repair never fires.
**S5.117 addendum — mechanism in the source:** `latt_probe.inc:67 latt_measure_basis()` measures ONE Q12 impulse response per band at the band centre through the real inverse and `latt_est_excess2()` reuses it at every position with symmetric rounding `(prod ± 2048) >> 12`. `[S5-DC]` makes the synthesis rounding alternate by pair parity (`dwt.c:143/147`), so at the actual step size the true pixel change differs from the estimate by one code on some samples; on plates at the exact rail that one code is the whole margin, the estimate "lies", and the bounded lie allowance (`latt_probe.inc` ~523) is exhausted with 10 samples left. Options: (a) raise/replace the lie bound with an exact final pass through the real inverse on the remaining samples; (b) model the parity rounding in the estimator. Testing (a) first (cheapest, exactness-neutral: the repair only ever commits what the real inverse confirms).
**Owner ruling 2026-09-06 (late):** the coordinator conceptualises, plans, diagnoses and integrates; every coding task goes to an agent. Applied: L1-0(b) repair fix → next free builder; F0 fill removal and F2 housekeeping → builder assignments; my lie-bound experiment is left to finish as diagnosis only (killed twice by the memory monitor while the agents' encodes ran).

### S5.143 — 2026-09-12 — Coordinator diagnosis: every vector is yesterday's motion (T5 design), the structural cap on high motion
Reading `src/codec.c` header + `[A1-MVBLK]`: since minor 10 the region seed AND the block deltas are derived by decimated SAD of refprev (t−1) against refprev2 (t−2), both committed pictures, never against the source ("nothing here ever reads the source frame"), so the vector replays exactly in every generation. Consequence: the vector applied to frame t is the displacement between t−2 and t−1: constant-velocity extrapolation, one frame stale, blind to acceleration, direction change and newly appearing motion — precisely the sports cases. Consistent with SA2's findings (no motion premium; disagreement flat vs |v|; half-pel never selected: the search is SAD on two noisy committed pictures). The trade was made for exactness-unlimited (source-searched vectors flip between generations; the documented `--mv-regions` failure). Idea queue additions for SA2 (after I2): V25 source-searched vector ORACLE — same syntax (seed + offset list), searched on source vs committed reference, encoder-only, quality at exact CBR on the four clean motion cells + static control, plus the derived-vs-searched disagreement rate and the share explained by acceleration (seed_t − seed_{t−1}); this is the upper bound of motion modelling for this codec. V26 (only if V25 is large): lock-safe use of a source search — at a CDR (re-encode) input, identify the generation-1 vector among the candidates by lattice alignment of the residual (the true vector's residual is already on the quantisation lattice; a wrong one is not, except with vanishing probability), cheap on the LL band; plus the trend-extrapolated seed (previous slice seed stored, tiny state, exact by construction) as the partial that needs no source. Perplexity "temporal methods" document (owner upload 2026-09-12): its activity forecasters (persistence, EWMA, CUSUM, hold counters, phase tables) answer a question the codec does not ask — the per-band mode already decides intra/inter on the real frame's measured cost — so none help; its one transferable idea is trend extrapolation, applied to the vector, not to an activity score. Its premise that the source-searched/per-block field "was removed" is wrong (block field ships, minor 16, derived not searched).

### S5.170 — 2026-09-13 — new_ideas/09132026 markdowns (summary + proposals 1–5, Perplexity, prompted "do not parrot the files") — read in full by Fable
Eight mechanism classes; the thread itself retracts one (clamping the evens inside the inverse predictor: H stays free, odds can still cross; and it is in-loop clipping, S5.105(4)). The rest against our record: (1) canonical coefficient-lattice legalisation = the I2 family (closed, S5.155). (2) explicit legalisation field = bits + generation-sensitive, rejected by the thread itself. (3) safe-codeword quantisation (choose only q with S(q) legal and Q(A(S(q))) = q) = the goal restated; no method. (4) "marginised LL": force the coarse reconstruction ≥ M from the rails, M = worst remaining fine swing — this is admission-by-bound (S5.138: the bound is hundreds of codes against content 8–38 codes from the rail) applied to the LL, i.e. a level shift of up to M near black/white = the smudge; and its existence proof is trivial in a form we already have: with all fine coefficients zero the swing is exactly 0, so the legal continuation is the LL-only rung, proven and exact (S5.150). Reject as stated; keep the rung. (5) interval-admissible fine quantisation (admit each fine index only if its EXACT swing keeps every touched sample legal; q = 0 always admissible) = L-I6 (S5.169, FAIL) with one difference the thread insists on: exact per-position-class synthesis kernels (interior / slice-top / slice-bottom / cross-slice) generated from the normative inverse, where SA1b used the basis table and found errors up to 169 codes on one-step deltas that it attributed to the stencil's shift-invariance approximation. The inverse is linear apart from rounding, so exact per-class kernels should predict a one-step change to within a few codes; if SA1b's kernels were single-class, that is the flaw, and the admission idea is not yet falsified. (6) tile + halo = an implementation structure, not a mechanism. (7) dual kernel (2-tap near rails) = the 5/3 oracle (S5.166: 0.3–6.5 %), dead. Fixed-point accept test per candidate = a forward transform per candidate, unaffordable per coefficient; the T5 lock already covers S(q) as the committed picture.
Verdict: not a solution as written; one component earns one measurement, queued as L-I8 after L-I7: generate exact per-class synthesis kernels from the shipped inverse and test predicted-vs-true contribution of a one-step change at every position class (must be within rounding, ≤ 4 codes, on 100 % of samples, including XSL edges); if that holds, re-run the L-I6 admission with them (bar unchanged: −90 % violations, tail no worse, cycle budget); if it does not, the admission family is closed on the same fact as L-I6.

### S5.171 — 2026-09-13 — Higher expert's reply (via owner): agrees the 09132026 proposals are search frameworks; proposes a RAIL EXCEPTION LAYER
Expert: coefficient admission/legalisation is "a more formal version of the repair family" unless the transform gives a usable local control direction (SA1b's kernel result is that prerequisite); the failure is structural: a lossy, high-gain, finite-support fine transform cannot be asked to produce an arbitrary legal bounded reconstruction. Proposal: split the source before the transform into a legal BASE B = clamp(X, L+G, U−G) and a sparse rail residual R = X − B; code the base through the ordinary lossy path; code R losslessly with a sparse, run/shape syntax, applied after reconstruction; derive the rail-zone mask from the DECODED base (with a three-zone hysteresis and a small signalled state map for ambiguous blocks) so the decomposition is canonical and the next generation reproduces it; no in-loop clip; five falsification tests (rail coverage per plane/content class; exception entropy vs G; base quality at the target rate; fixed-point decomposition X → X* → X**; rate reality against the fixed per-slice CBR).
Coordinator assessment: a genuinely different mechanism — the first that does not rely on transform control; it is "fix at the input" literally (the split happens before the transform), fixed work (no loop), and the legality argument becomes trivial IF the residual is defined against the DECODED base, R = X − B̂ on the zone derived from B̂: in-zone samples reconstruct to X exactly (legal), out-of-zone samples are B̂ < U−G (legal), so legality holds by construction for ANY G — no proven bound is needed, which removes the admission-bound problem entirely; G becomes a rate/quality knob only. Generation lock: in-zone base is the constant U−G at both generations, out-of-zone base is B̂ itself, and the zone map is a function of B̂ at both ends — reduces to the existing T5 lock plus zone-map equality. Costs and risks: normative syntax (minor bump, a lossless residual coder per slice); the residual is noise-like where the base rings at rail-adjacent edges (X − B̂ is not run-compressible there), so the bits scale with rail-zone TEXTURE coverage; under exact CBR those bits squeeze the base on rail-heavy textured slices (spotrobotL is pressed against both rails: its base could be starved); the plan search must price the residual per candidate (one base reconstruction per candidate). The decider is the rate reality check on the failing cells and on limited-range content (L-I7: if limited-range sources never approach the container rail, the layer is empty on broadcast content and costs nothing). Queue: after L-I7, L-I8 = the expert's tests 1, 2, 5 as one measurement (coverage, exception entropy with R = X − B̂, bits against the slice budget, per cell/rate/plane), then 3–4 if the rate survives; the exact-kernel test (S5.170) drops to L-I9 as a cheap check only.

The lock is a bit-exact fixed point, not a basin: any mechanism that feeds the encoder a value it never committed breaks it. Root cause statement (owner's question): legality must be achieved INSIDE the committed lattice — only the repair does that, and only the repair keeps the baseband lock; every out-of-lattice mechanism (clip, exception layer, predicted edits) breaks a fixed point that has no basin. The cost of the in-lattice mechanism is passes, and passes are many because the repair is untargeted (S5.147: 62 % of pass-2+ slices — the shrink never moves the offending sample) and slice-granular against a coupling that crosses slices (un-blend + vertical span), so a handful of samples cascades into tens of slices. ### S5.178 — 2026-09-13 — new_ideas/09132026/new (README + proposals 1–5, written against memo 010) — read in full by Fable
README's own verdict: most of its proposals re-enter falsified families; three components are "materially different, unvalidated": (1) syndrome/group quantisation (choose a small vector of coefficients under an exact cancellation invariant) — depends on EXACT accounting of a group's synthesis, the same prerequisite that killed items 4 and 6 (basis-table inexactness); nothing new to test beyond the queued exact-kernel check (L-I9 old, now L-I12); (2) rounding-free dyadic synthesis (linear inverse over dyadic rationals, one output rounding; exact running account at quantisation time) — makes legality accounting exact and one-pass, but the re-encode lock is NOT by bijection any more: the forward analysis of round(S(c)) is c plus the analysis of a ±0.5 rounding field, whose worst case (0.5 × the low-pass analysis L1 gain ≈ 3.8 codes at LL5) exceeds the 2-code half step of the LL band, so the lock becomes probable, not provable — a codec redesign with the lock burden unmet; parked as a direction only if in-lattice repair fails; (3) predict-only (identity-preserving, "lazy") lifting on rail lineages (proposal 4): keep the even samples of a lineage whose support touches a rail as source samples (no update step), code the odd as its residual against a convex two-tap interpolant, cap the residual by the interpolation gap so the odd cannot leave the legal interval, unmarked lineages unchanged. Legality structural in one pass, in-lattice (the committed picture is the decode of the symbols), no loop, not flat (edges are preserved as subsampled source). Defects as written: the marks must be a function of committed symbols, and its proposed sources (a causal prefix of the LIVE source for intra; the previous slice's committed evens for inter) differ between generations for intra — the marks must be SIGNALLED (bits per lineage) or derived from something both generations share; the coarse band of a marked lineage becomes plain subsampled pixels (aliasing; more residual bits); the even's dequantised value at a rail can exceed it by half an LL step (lattice alignment at the rail or a cap on the LL reconstruction needed); ownership at slice boundaries. Genuinely outside the eight falsified families: it removes the update step that creates the coarse lobe instead of fighting the lobe. Queued as L-I11 (after L-I10): oracle first — marks from the source (gen-1 oracle), predict-only lifting + gap cap on marked lineages in a probe encoder/decoder pair; violations after one pass (expect 0 — verify), bits, quality per plane, marked fraction, eye renders; then signalled marks and the lock chain. Proposal 1 (balanced texture atoms + credit ledger): a representation redesign whose "non-ringing legal base" is unspecified — the whole problem; rejected. Proposal 2 (polar-rail quantisation): "sign-definite inward errors cannot produce an out-of-range sample" is false for a signed overlapping synthesis (over-cancelling at one sample overshoots at another); README agrees; rejected. Proposal 5 (pilots + static guard bands): guard bands = admission bound (falsified, S5.138); pilots assume a basin that S5.176 shows does not exist; rejected.

### S5.198 — 2026-09-14 — SA7 DESIGN2.md (edge-adaptive predictor): a decision-dependent predictor is NOT exactly invertible in a lossy codec unless the decision reads data both ends hold at that point; the reference-driven form reduces ripple but does not remove the blocker

Three exact forms: A closed loop (decision from reconstructed coarser levels; breaks the one-pass order and the ladder as the transform stands), B decision from committed data outside the slice (the T5 reference; exact, no bits, stale by one frame), C signalled (excluded by the brief). Design proposes B: members V0 normal / V1 b / V2 c vertically, H0 9/7-M / H1 5/3 two-tap / H2 one-sided horizontally; predict steps only (update and W_b untouched); decision gA = R[y−1]−R[y−3], gB = R[y+1]−R[y−1] on the reference, T = (1<<depth)>>5, seven integer ops; forced NORMAL where the reference is absent and on row sh−1. Provenance: signalled selection and decisions from the current slice's own samples left out.
Coordinator conclusion: form B is a quality lever, not the legality fix. The legality-by-construction transform is the universal PREDICT-ONLY (interpolating, "lazy") lifting: no update step at any level, convex predictors only (the 5/3 two-tap everywhere; the 9/7-M's negative taps dropped), so an odd sample's prediction lies between its evens and cannot overshoot; the residual INDEX capped per sample to the gap the evens leave to the rails (a quantiser rule both ends compute from the already-reconstructed evens — no clip, so the committed odd = pred + res exactly and generation 2 re-derives the same index); the coarsest LL clamped at both ends (idempotent, S5.191). Then every sample is legal by construction at every level, one pass, no repair, no escapes, no bits beyond the residuals, no grid. L-I11's predict-only failed only on COVERAGE (rail-based source marks); the universal form has no marks. Open risk = compression efficiency without the update's anti-aliasing (R = 2R) and the look of texture/aliasing — the oracle question. Provenance: interpolating subdivision (Deslauriers–Dubuc 1989), interpolating wavelets (Donoho 1992), lifting (Sweldens 1996): obviously clean; added to legal memo 003 as a second element for confirmation before building.

(b) Cap qhi = (U′ − P) >> s, qlo symmetric, two shifts + two compares from values both ends hold; the cap can never exclude the true value (the source odd is in range and P is convex over in-range evens); it suppresses only quantisation overshoot ≤ half a step within half a step of a rail; legality by induction (LL clamped, evens = committed coarser samples, odds convex + capped); lock simpler: at gen 2 the evens ARE the committed samples, P identical, r = dequant(q) exactly. (c) The XSL display blend still adds up to lim (8 codes) after reconstruction: row 0 exactly certified, row sh−1 at lim with the §2 per-column bound; row 0 is an even at every level, so the gen-2 un-blend must remain exact and unclamped. (d) Measured on the source: the AM/GM coding-gain proxy is neutral (−0.02…−0.07 dB) but dominated by LL5 — not believed; per-band energies: level 1 bit-identical, LL5 barely moves, coarse detail bands grow 5–36 % on the hard cells (HL3 +26.9 % dng 720p, +36.1 % cf_gfx; HL4 +17–19 %; HL2 +18–19 %) — the missing anti-aliasing compounding down five horizontal levels ≈ +0.13…+0.23 bits/coefficient where the bits are; spotrobotL neutral or better; expectation for R = 2R: neutral-to-better on smooth content, a real loss on texture and graphics; recovery within the rule: convexity is the requirement, not two taps — a four-tap positive-weight interpolating predictor (1,7,7,1)/16 keeps P inside the hull and restores most of the interpolation order at one add and one shift. (e) New artifact class: lowpass aliasing (a 4×32 subsample grid), discriminator: it does not shrink with rate (test 0.5/1.0/4.0); texture look (zeroed residual → a sample exactly the average of its neighbours); ringing on cf_gfx must visibly reduce or the six-iteration diagnosis is wrong. (f) Cheaper transform, fewer buffers, but the residual pass serialises over 7 levels; naively 7 entropy-coder entries (+6 traversals, does not fit 4K at 8 spc); mitigation settled: the cascade depends on dequantised indices, not coded bits, so it runs ahead and all seven levels are coded into one tANS stream at the end — coder entered once, critical path +≈2 traversals of quantise + reconstruct, added latency zero. (g) Provenance: Deslauriers–Dubuc 1989, Donoho 1992, Sweldens 1996; two-tap predict and LL clamp already shipped; index cap own work; left out: signalled selection, negative-weight predictors at levels 1–2. (h) Oracle: chain first with a negative control (cap disabled must still lock AND show out-of-range); oob = 0 across every depth/format/range with the repair and the whole correction engine OFF plus a counter proving the cap binds; compression at equal CBR on the whole corpus against 0.1 dB, sweeping the convex four-tap; then the eye, pipeline, A5, seam. Go/no-go: lock 2/3, oob = 0 with the cap binding, no plane worse than 0.1 dB — if the coarse-band cost survives the four-tap, the design stops (a legal-by-construction transform that costs R = 2R is not a trade the mandate allows). Coordinator: accepted as the build once legal confirms; analysis-only work meanwhile (four-tap and a derived positive-weight member across the corpus/depths/formats; aliasing signature + rendered level-5 lowpass for the owner; cap-binding statistics; the written generation-exactness proof PROOF_predictonly_lock.md).

### S5.212 — 2026-09-14 — Transform oracle gates (2) and (3) FAILED: DESIGN3 (universal predict-only transform) is falsified as the shipping transform; two root causes measured; ladder moves to 4b (L-I28) with 4c's residue mechanism shown to be structurally required
`Subagents/SA7_legality_v2/REPORT.md` §18 (gate 2), `out/PO2_gate2.txt` (63 points), `out/PO2/capstat.txt`, `out/PO2_smax.txt`, `out/PO3_gate3.txt` (gate 3, dng 720p only — stopped there by the coordinator because the result is decisive). All runs repair OFF (`--gamut-strict 0`, `OMC_GM_LATT=0`), cap armed, cap-off control beside.
**Gate (2) — oob = 0 everywhere, repair off.** Holds on natural content as written: dng 1080p 4:2:2 and 4:4:4, 8/10/12-bit, 0.5/1.0/2.0 bpp (18/18 → 0; control 19–3,194), dng limited range 10-bit 3/3 → 0 (the @2.0 point vacuous, control also 0), cf_gfx @1.0/@2.0 → 0, cut24 @2.0 → 0 (control 114,134). FAILS on rail-pressing content: cf_gfx @0.5 → 3 (all on slicerow −1, the row the boundary edit writes), cut24 @1.0 → 1,804, cut24 @0.5 rc = 1 (T5 wide-domain clamp, value 6144), synthetic rail extrema (8/10/12-bit, 4:2:2/4:4:4, full and limited) → 0…28,201 with the cap on and rc = 1 at four points. **Cause, one and measured, 100 % on every failing point:** every site the cap could not place has a quantiser step wider than the margined legal window (2^s > U − L − 2m: ext 422/12 @0.5 78,089/78,089; cut24 @1.0 5,618/5,618; cf_gfx @0.5 13/13); guard = 0 everywhere — the loops terminate, they step over the window. The reconstruction lattice {R + q·2^s} meets the window only when its spacing fits inside it; where the plan picks a step wider than the whole legal range no index exists. SA7's first counter (guard hits only) was blind to this mode and reported capfail = 0 while 78,089 sites were unreachable — fixed; recorded because a counter that cannot see the failure is worse than none. Two remedies measured and rejected: (a) bound the shift from header data (OMC_PO_SMAX, derive_shifts, no syntax) restores the precondition and breaks exact CBR — rc = 1 on every extrema point at every rate and on cf_gfx @0.5, a real cell; free where not needed, useless where needed; (b) all-intra where the cap cannot reach: cf_gfx stays 3, cut24 @1.0 goes 1,804 → 4,839, ext10 @2.0 23,300 → 18,309 — the temporal path is not the cause, the step is. Cap cost on natural content: binds on 0.019 % of coefficients, moves exactly one step; HH2 binds 4× more often than any other band (0.078 %) — the non-convex HH predictor (S5.211) showing where predicted; worst correction on convex bands 1 step, on HH1/HH2 2 steps. PROOF_predictonly_lock.md amended: legality rests on the lattice covering the line under an explicit precondition; convexity survives only as the cost bound where it holds.
**Gate (3) — compression at equal CBR vs the frozen base, dng 720p 10-bit, 8 frames, per-plane PSNR (bar 0.1 dB):** two-tap arm (w0) Y −3.67 dB @0.5 (34.51 → 30.84), −3.23 @1.0, −2.43 @2.0; Cb −2.1/−2.0/−2.3; Cr −2.2/−1.9/−1.9; four-tap arm (w1) +0.13 dB over w0 and oob = 2 @0.5 (site map not extended — the arm is not by construction and is dropped). Attribution: the cap moved 0.019 % of coefficients by one step and cannot cost 3 dB; the loss is the transform — deleting the update step leaves the lowpass as plain decimation, the aliasing compounds through five levels, and the coarse bands carry it (DESIGN3 §(d) predicted +5…36 % coarse-band growth; the measured cost is an order larger). The d[−1] debit (S5.202: −0.17…−0.46 dB) is inside this figure.
**Verdict.** DESIGN3 is falsified as the shipping transform on two independent counts: it costs ~3 dB at every rate (bar 0.1), and even its legal-by-construction claim has a precondition (step ≤ window) that rail-pressing content at low rates violates, and restoring that precondition costs exact CBR. **What the results say about the cause.** (i) Any encoder-only index cap, on any transform, shares the precondition: where the rate plan takes a step wider than the legal window, no committed index is legal — so on rail content a residue mechanism (escapes funded from the bank, S5.194; the 4c rung) is structurally required, not optional; the cap and the residue mechanism are one design. (ii) The update step is worth ~3 dB and stays. (iii) A separable predict-only HH is non-convex in 2-D; irrelevant once the update stays. **Ladder: 4b — L-I28** (today's transform, update and predicts kept; encoder-only residual-index cap; row-wise forward/backward sweep in a closed loop with the same self-check discriminator; infeasibility measured first; infeasible rows → bank-funded escapes). What carries over from ptree6: the closed-loop cascade on band order 0–9, the store-the-reconstruction-point cap (no syntax, no decoder clamp), the row-0/row-15 margins, the self-check discriminator, the steps-moved counter with the step-vs-window test, the extrema arms (notes/po_extrema.py). OMC_PO stays in the tree as a probe (default 0, PO off byte-identical to f0tree2). Issued to SA7 at 03:2x.

### S5.213 — 2026-09-14 — Rung 4b (L-I28) oracle: the row-sweep index cap on today's transform is quality-free (worst plane −0.087 dB) and halves the violations; the residue on real content is the update's coupling (chain conflicts 85–100 %), on rail/synthetic content step-wider-than-window; 4c issued on the same tree
`Subagents/SA7_legality_v2/REPORT.md` §20; tree btree1 (fresh copy of f0tree2); `diffs/sa7_li28_oracle.diff` (md5 ec287606…, 428 +/0 −, three files); `out/B1_oracle.txt`, `out/B1_quality.txt`, `out/B1/*.log`. Off path byte-identical to f0tree2; discriminator 0 mismatches armed, 270/270 broken.
**A harness defect caught and attributed (SA7's, by SA7).** The first quality run showed the capped arm −0.70/−0.85/−1.82 dB Y at 0.5/1.0/2.0 on dng 720p although the cap had moved 61 steps at 2.0; the control arm (cap off, repair off, engine off) vs the base (shipped repair and engine on) is +0.09/+0.01/+0.00 dB, so the switches carry nothing. Cause: the oracle wrote every coefficient back as its reconstruction point q<<s; the shipped coder's calm eligibility (omc_calm and the legacy |q| = 1 kill) tests coefficient amplitude, not the index, so rewriting untouched coefficients silently switched the heuristic off, more small coefficients were coded, and the back-off took a coarser plan — isolated: with OMC_CALM=0 in both arms the 2.0 gap goes −1.82 → −0.006 dB. Fixed: write back only what the cap moved; take the starting index from band_scan. **Quality after the fix, equal CBR vs the frozen base, 8 frames:** dng 720p Y −0.0003/+0.016/+0.003 dB, cf_gfx Y −0.087/−0.006/+0.014 dB; worst plane −0.087 dB, inside the 0.1 dB bar — the cap on today's transform is quality-free.

### S5.217 — 2026-09-14 — Escape bits are charged inside the slice's own coefficient budget: the bank is causal (prefix surplus only), so early slices cannot draw the surplus the frame will create; the 0.26 dB is a plan change on 31 % of slices (whole Q rungs), not a wire_cap or list limit
`Subagents/SA7_legality_v2/REPORT.md` §24. cf_gfx @0.5, per frame (28 slices × 2,048 bits = 57,344): frame 0 spent 57,288, surplus 56, escape bits 626; frame 1 surplus 4,792, escapes 456; frames 2–7 surplus 2,048–2,832, escapes 142–512 — surplus exists at 0.5 under exact CBR (4–9× the escape bill on seven of eight frames) and wire_cap is nowhere near binding. Yet cap-only vs cap+escapes: 80 of 256 slices plan differently, several by a whole quantiser rung (f0 s2 Q9→Q10, f0 s5 Q8→Q9, f0 s9 Q9→Q10; a rung doubles the step) — that is the 0.26 dB; both streams exactly 57,376 bytes, CBR intact. Cause: the shipped bank is causal — avail_prefix = (slice_idx+1)·B − spent_bits lets a slice draw only on what earlier slices underspent; frame 0's slice 2 cannot borrow from slice 25's later surplus. An early slice that needs escapes pays from its own coefficients and the ladder answers with a coarser rung. Consequences stated by SA7: a non-causal charge (pre-reserving escape bits frame-wide) is a different bank and costs latency (the reserve must be set before the residue is known); charging escapes only where prefix surplus exists keeps CBR free but denies exactly the early rail-content slices. ### S5.225 — 2026-09-14 — Owner's question "is there anything higher up?": the byte-exact lock is the parent of the legality problem; the clip-aware lock oracle (C) is issued ahead of the transform arms
Owner: earlier OMC iterations (not HVBC) did not have this problem; the only difference is byte-exactness. Coordinator's reading, from the ledger: every earlier OMC clipped at the decoder output like every codec, and the edge ringing was clipped away invisibly; the byte-exact design cannot tolerate a clipped sample (the encoder cannot see the overshoot; the plan and vector derivations are discontinuous, so one changed sample cascades — S5.176 "no basin"), so S5.105(4) made the clamp a never-firing backstop, which created the repair engine, which paints the artifacts. The legality problem and its artifacts descend from how exactness was built, not from cost or the transform. Candidate at the parent: keep the decoder clip as a normative part of decoding; both ends use the CLIPPED picture as the temporal reference and for vector derivation; the encoder's idempotence check becomes clip-aware — it verifies that re-encoding clip(recon) reproduces its own stream, a sample at the rail meaning "at or beyond the rail" — using the lock's existing candidate search (plan enumeration, verify_candidate) to pick a consistent index/plan where a coefficient straddles a bin edge after clipping. Generation 1 legal by clipping, no repair, no artifacts; exactness unconditional from g2 IF the fixed point exists — the S5.176 no-basin measurement was made for out-of-lattice mechanisms without a clip-aware lock and does not answer it. Not the rejected "resume after the clamp" two-tier idea. Provenance: decoder clipping is universal; the self-verifying encoder is our own design; nothing new to ask. Issued to SA7 as oracle (C), ahead of (A) and (B).

### S5.261 — 2026-09-19 — Owner ruling: fitting the slice period is not enough; the compute must be nowhere near the total capability of the reference FPGA part (ZU7EV-class, S5.40). Provisioning parallel units to fit the period is not a lever (S5.1xx latency bar). Applied to R1-LOCK: the latency gate is stated as operations per slice AND as a fraction of the part's logic/DSP/memory at the pipeline clock, for the whole encoder and decoder, worst case (rail plates), every format up to 8K; the recovery's added work must be a small fraction of the shipped encoder's own work, and the total must leave large headroom on the part. docs/HARDWARE.md (§7 attempt-loop budget, §2 memory budget) is the model to extend; the number goes in the same table.

The lock certifies the DISPLAYED rows, but the shipped temporal prediction reads the UN-BLENDED reference e->ref; gen 2 receives only the displayed picture, so its reference can differ from gen 1's wherever display and reference are not one-to-one — the uncertified last row of each slice, and seam samples where the outer clip fired (un-blend inexact by ≤ lim) — and any slice referenced through those rows sees a different pcoef, off-lattice residuals, and fails; the temporal cascade follows. Provenance: predicting from the decoded output picture is universal practice. ### S5.316 — 2026-09-26 — Owner direction: "look at patterns — what keeps the image legal, what works more than other solutions, what works when those don't; find the least common denominators instead of trying thousands of solutions; that is not 'not noticeably different from JPEG XS'"; and everything must fit the selected FPGA (ZU7EV-class, S5.40/S5.261, HARDWARE.md) comfortably. Patterns already in the ledger: (P1) the true plan's rank in the lattice ranking has MEDIAN 0 and is always in the top 16 (S5.245); (P2) given the plan, the codec's own quantiser snap equals q₁ on 100.000 % of on-lattice coefficients (S5.246); (P3) the off-lattice set is EXACTLY the clip-perturbed set, 0.26–0.98 % of coefficients (S5.246/247), and c₂ = c₁ − T(δ) exactly on 98–99 %, within 4 codes elsewhere (S5.247); (P4) with δ*, snap = q₁ on 99.994 % (S5.250) and the stream re-emits byte for byte (S5.255); (P5) the lattice residue of large-step affected coefficients separates δ* from other exact δ (R≥64 ≈ 0–31 vs 25–2,954, S5.312); (P6) a ≤ 113-code excursion moves a coarse coefficient by ≤ 0.16 of a step (S5.257) — so large-step residues do not wrap and r_c ≈ −Σ_s W_cs δ_s ± 4 is a LINEAR, directly solvable relation; (P7) the reuse result: one exact δ serves every plan (S5.313/314). Hypothesis (the least common denominator): rank-0 plan + DIRECT solve of δ from the large-step residues (fixed small number of simultaneous-update passes, weights from a fixed table indexed by the site's position class, since the transform is shift-invariant up to phase) + ONE whole-slice check covers nearly all site slices; the walk/search is only a bounded fallback. Before any more search work: STEP P, a pattern census (instrument only) measuring exactly that, across the suite plus 1080p 4:2:2 10-bit, 4:4:4 12-bit, cut24 and an extrema arm. 4b parked after its build and identity check (not adopted).

### S5.317 — 2026-09-26 — ADVERSARIAL DESIGN REVIEW of the cost rebuild (stages renamed C-b…C-e to avoid collision with the falsified S5.213–S5.221 legality rungs "4b–4e"; separate Opus 5.5 reviewer, read-only). Verdict: C-b/C-c buildable only with changes; C-d/C-e NOT buildable as specified; neither latency bar claimable. Findings: (1 MAJOR) §1(m) "δ is a property of the picture" holds only for δ*; a SEARCHED δ is a property of (picture, plan) — a δ found on a candidate coarser than gen 1's plan on the affected band can leave gen 1's plan inexact, losing it and breaking B5.5 (zero margin: ~1 in 100 slices sits exactly at budget_hard, LEDGER_v5_3_5 §51.29) — the 3g transfer evidence is 2 slices, both finer→coarser; changes: bounded descent from δ_w when reuse fails; keep the second source; take the source from the finest candidate on the affected bands; gate on winners identical to 3g per slice. (2 MAJOR) unsearched reuse targets never get MODERES (the s83 class) → run the flip loop under reused δ, capped. (3 MINOR) the δ cache (codec.c 6789) still seeds later candidates from failed ones → own seed per search; report the first-exact index. (4 MAJOR) local predicate ≠ whole-slice under targeted-partial re-ranking (LL index change), mode/tie flips (whole-band), lifting rounding outside the linear support (cone halo at every level incl. 9/7-M), seam rows (e->ref k−1 rows, two-step blend, outer clip, mutable xsl_buf state, pad rows) → route every non-local trigger to the whole-slice predicate; discriminator in debug mode with a negative control. (5 MAJOR) the forward is 55 % of R1's work and C-c localises only the inverse; r1_rebuild_plane runs two full forwards per plane per move, one of the constant uncorrected field → cache it; add a local forward; the "~1/100" figure is an extrapolation from level-1 supports (LL5 supports 209–749 samples, S5.196) → measure footprints first. (6 MINOR) acceptance failure after local 0 must be a loud defect counter, not a retry. (7 MAJOR) the no-wrap premise of the direct seed is falsified by the ledger: δ reaches 212 (cf_gfx, S5.288/290), RANGE 512 exists; w·δ = 159 > step/2 at step 256; coupling (113 pairs on spot s3), seam-residue baseline ~12 codes not confined to seam rows (S5.237/249), per-coefficient shifts, deadzone, partial chunks, inter-band lattices on coef−pcoef, no step ≥ 256 at 2.0 bpp / 8-bit / LL5 shift 2, coarse coefficients carry ≤ 0.16 step (S5.257), 12-bit lim 32 → constants not depth-scaled; bisection ill-posed on flat/non-monotone counts (S5.288–293/306); a bad seed can end in an exact δ with different indices (not proven impossible). (8 BLOCKER for C-e) a fixed cap can lose a lock; cluster-uniform alone does not close dense slices (S5.275/291/306); corpus reaches 99–126 sites/slice, cut24 and extrema produced 2,867–66,266 sites/frame in the legality oracles (S5.213) and R1 has never run on them; a SILENT 8192-site cap already exists (r1l_add_site, codec.c 6213/6247) → caps from the hardware budget, synthetic worst cases per format, locks lost at cap = gate failure, make 8192 loud. (9 BLOCKER for determinism) unbounded/quadratic loops outside C-b…C-e: best-first rounds O(sites²)×probes (codec.c 6897), uncapped reuse targets (each = resolve + predicate + trial + tie + resolve), uncapped MODERES re-searches (108 searches / 78 flips on gfx8 f7 s14), and the SHIPPED walk bounded only by progress (HARDWARE.md §7: W_max unbounded; shipped worst 16,289 slice-pass equivalents on d7x8 inter frames) → W_max as a closed formula of caps. (10 BLOCKER for latency) with 16 samples/clock at an ASSUMED 300 MHz (reviewer's assumption, not measured): 1080p60 4:2:2 ≈ 19 slice passes per slice period, 2160p60 ≈ 4.8, 8K ≈ 1.2 — the SHIPPED lock alone (~52 passes/slice) does not fit above 720p without parallel units (provisioning excluded, S5.261), work is serial (best-first rounds; slice k needs k−1's committed rows) → per-format W_max in cycles vs slice period, serial depth, fraction of the part, encoder latency vs JPEG XS, and with the converter vs sub-1 ms. (11 MINOR) IP: no patent risk identified (local re-evaluation, one-step linear estimate, bisection, caps, reuse are textbook/own work; not joint/trellis/DP); δ̂ = −r/w needs a reciprocal per site → shift-add or LUT, bound the count; add to the S5.264 provenance. (12 MINOR) no prior falsification of C-b…C-e as such; carry S5.257, S5.289/290, S5.275/291/306, S5.309/310, S5.312 into the spec; §1(g) still states the S5.296 design S5.297 falsified. (13 MAJOR) the suite is too narrow (no inter-frame stream equality, no ≥4 generations inter, no offset arm, spot 4×4 both rates pending, no 1080p/2160p, 4:4:4, 8/12-bit, limited range beyond 720p, 2.0 bpp, cut24, extrema, motion cells, rt=0 decode) → g2 streams byte-identical to 3g per row, stage discriminators with negative controls, gen 2 bits ≤ gen 1 per slice; the suite must assert its env (REUSE default 0 in rtree3 — the S5.304 precedent). FABLE'S READING: finding 10 is the governing one. Search-and-check — in R1 AND in the shipped generation lock — is structurally incompatible with the owner's latency bar (never noticeably longer than JPEG XS, which decides once) at 2160p and 8K on the ZU7EV-class part. Under the owner's rebuild rule (2026-09-26) the lock itself is a part "not working appropriately": the target is a FIXED-WORK, one-decision path (rank-0 plan read from the picture, direct δ from a position table, one check), with any fallback bounded by a closed formula.
