### S5.319 — 2026-09-27 — SA10 independent proposal delivered (Subagents/SA10_independent/PROPOSAL.md, FIRST_PRINCIPLES.md, numpy model notes/ + out/, hashes out/MD5SUMS_notes.txt; nothing built in any codec tree). Design "ECR" (embedded description + consistent legal reconstruction): replace plan/lock/R1/repair by an EMBEDDED description — nested (bit-plane truncation) quantisation cells coded in a fixed, data-causal order and cut at the slice budget; if the decoded picture lies inside its own cells, the next encoder reproduces the stream in one pass (no plan to re-find; both hops, unlimited generations). Required detail found by experiment: the cut is decided BEFORE the next symbol is read ("prefix-safe stop"; the naive stop broke exactness on 2 of 3 slices). Legality inside the cells at zero bits: decoder places each coefficient anywhere in its cell — K rounds of in-cell projection (clip samples, re-analyse, clamp to cells); a legal in-cell picture always exists (the source). Backstop: gen 1 checks its own output; if not a legal fixed point it re-describes the decoded picture up to J times; else a TERMINAL mode (closed-loop predict-only pyramid reconstructing each sample inside its cell and the legal range; legal and self-reproducing by construction); later encoders take the first mode in a fixed order that reproduces their input (bounded). Illegal sources: reflect out-of-range inward (hard clip made rail plates that stall the legaliser). Model results (K = 4, J = 2): full-range natural 0/1,974 slice-planes terminal; limited range 1/1,170; generations 2 = 3 on 3,416/3,416 fixed-point slices, non-fixed-point slices all differ (check valid both ways); PSNR vs plain clip 0 to +0.015 dB on natural rows; terminal mode 0 illegal, 100 % self-reproducing incl. synthetic extrema; worst-case work closed-form 43 transform-pass equivalents at gen 1, 10 at gen ≥ 2 (vs R1 632–191,973). Risks stated by SA10: no worst-case convergence proof of the in-cell projection (stalls on rail plates at 1–3 codes; five legaliser variants failed); cut24/extrema fall to terminal on 11–20 % of slice-planes at buildable K/J (0 % at K = J = 8, too costly at 8K); terminal slices lose 1.6–2.9 dB mean, 9 dB on cut24 → a visible step risk; bit-plane coding with simple static contexts costs 4–17 % more luma bits than one-shot at low rates (threat to the half-rate mandate; one-shot base layer proposed, unmeasured); gen-1 worst case ≈ 56 % of ZU7EV logic at 4320p60 (rough); not modelled: temporal prediction, 9/7-M, real tANS; mid-sequence baseband start exact only from g3 (as shipped, S5.236); the XSL seam blend removed. Section 6 checks prior falsifications (S5.55/156/226, S5.105(4), S5.171–176, coefficient-edit/escape families, plan-level and quantiser-field ideas, DESIGN3/S5.212, S5.70 on nested cells, S5.317 f10, S5.29, HVBC decoder-side interval reconstruction). Next: adversarial review of the proposal (owner rule), then decide.

FABLE — reading: (a) on NATURAL content (incl. graphics and hard-clipped limited range at the codec rails) clipping is overwhelmingly ISOLATED ringing overshoot at edges (level-1/2 details), not plates; the fixed path's natural misses (spot s2/s3) are coupled isolated sites → a SOLVE-quality problem, not a plate problem; (b) PLATES (flat content exactly at a rail: fades to black, full-range black bars, max-white graphics — real broadcast content, stressed by cut24/extrema) are a separate class with dense, structured, rate-dependent ripple; (c) the codec treats 0/1023 as the rail for limited-range formats today; if the owner's legality is the NOMINAL levels (64–940/960), plates become common on legalised broadcast content (4.5 % of luma on spotLIM) — the rail definition is decisive and is recorded as the open definitional fact to confirm from the owner's rulings (memory bit-depths-required: "full-range input required; legality on full range and graphics") before any plate design. Next: Step S — close the natural misses in the fixed path (plan class via MODERES + next verifying candidate; solve class via real-residue correction passes: how many to reach 100 %, and the work), measured; in parallel the coordinator designs the plate mechanism from (3).
S5.324 addendum (rail definition, from the record, not asked): the legality rails for limited-range formats are the SDI transportable range per depth (8-bit 1..254, 10-bit 4..1019, 12-bit 16..4079; memory bit-depths-required, ledger line "rails and headroom per depth"); the nominal levels (64..940/960 at 10-bit) are content levels, and excursions into the headroom are legitimate. So spotLIM's 35,803 "beyond the levels" samples are NOT illegal; the plate class is FULL-RANGE content at 0 / 2^n−1 (fades to black, full-range bars, max-white graphics) plus the synthetic stress arms. To verify in code (Step S3): which rails the codec clips to for limited-range streams (must be the SDI range, and codes 0–3 / 1020–1023 never emitted). Real plate overshoot is along plate EDGES (ringing; a flat plate reconstructs exactly on the rail — extrema's 8,192-sample plate), so its count scales with edge length; cut24/extrema are the maximum-edge-density stress.

### S5.325 — 2026-09-27 — Owner: "Every step has always been decisive. But that doesn't change the fact that we must solve the problem." Gen-2 exactness is unaffected in principle (the capped indices lie on the plan's lattice; gen 2's lock emits the recovered q₁ and never re-caps). Risk stated: the cap's residue is exactly the coupled set, so the combination may leave the hardest sites untouched — to be MEASURED, not assumed. ### S5.327 — 2026-09-27 — Owner: "we've made it to 'almost' hundreds of times." Two changes, effective now. (1) REPORTING: results are exact miss counts over the full test set; "done" = zero misses on every cell, format, depth, chroma and rate. (2) DESIGN SHAPE — completeness by construction (S5.70's canonical-emission principle, applied to recoverability): every attempt so far made gen 2 recover WHATEVER gen 1 emitted, which always leaves a residue. Instead, the first encoder (the one whose lock fails, i.e. a first generation) runs the SAME fixed-path recovery the next encoder will run, on its own decoded slice (it has source, indices, plan and the decoded picture), BEFORE emitting; if the slice would not recover exactly (or would recover with more bits than it spent), it re-chooses that slice's coding among quality-free alternatives (first the 4b cap, S5.213: quality-free, halves violations; then the next alternatives to be listed and measured, each checked quality- and bit-neutral per the owner's 2026-09-27 screen) and re-checks, with a fixed cap on re-choices. Every emitted slice is then recoverable by the next encoder by construction; the residue class disappears if a free re-choice always exists — THAT is the question to measure (per cell: slices needing a re-choice, re-choices used, quality and bits delta, and slices where no free re-choice made it recoverable = the true remaining problem, stated as a count). Work: first-generation encoders pay encode + one fixed-path check (+ re-choices, capped); later hops pay the fixed path only. Step T (running) is the first measurement of the cap as a re-choice; Step V will simulate the self-check loop on the full set.
S5.327 amendment (owner: 'until it does — isn't that why we have hundreds of tries?'): the self-check allows AT MOST ONE re-choice per slice, a single predetermined change (no loop, no trial-and-error); the design is accepted only if that one re-choice makes EVERY slice recoverable on the full set; any slice needing more is a failure of the design, reported as a count, never absorbed by adding tries. Work bound: first-generation encoder = encode + 1 check + ≤ 1 re-choice + 1 check.

### S5.329 — 2026-09-27 — Design candidate after S5.328 (doc check done: DESIGN2 edge-adaptive predictor S5.198 = quality lever, not legality; DESIGN3 predict-only S5.212/S5.254-line verdict −3 dB and step ≤ window precondition — local predict-only at rail edges inherits that precondition → not pursued; adaptive lifting IP §5.8 S5.199). CANDIDATE "in-cell legaliser + recovery": the DECODER (and the encoder's own reconstruction, rt = 0) moves out-of-range samples back toward the legal range using ONLY the freedom inside each transmitted quantisation cell (in-cell projection: clip samples, re-analyse, clamp coefficients to their cells; bounded K rounds, LOCAL to the violating samples' footprint), then clips the small residue. Properties on paper: zero bits (no side information); moves the picture TOWARD the source (both the legal set and the cells contain the source) → no artifact, PSNR ≥ plain clip (SA10 model +0 … +0.015 dB); in-cell values keep gen 2's lattice read intact; SA10 measured the legaliser alone stalls at a residual of 1–3 codes on rail plates (S5.321) — never combined with the fixed-path recovery, which handles small, sparse δ exactly (S5.326). ### S5.343 — 2026-09-27 — EXPERT ANSWERS to memo 010 (Communication/202600927/: start_here.md = "Memo 011" expert A; vibe.md = expert B; gemini.md = expert C; perplexity.pdf = expert D). SUMMARY PER EXPERT.
A (start_here): exactness = E(D(E(x))) = E(x); two conditions: (1) the decoded picture must lie in the set the codec can describe (the clip violates it), (2) E must be canonical from the picture. Proposal: legality INSIDE the synthesis — in an inverse predict step odd = d + P(even) the decoder knows P(even), so clamp the reconstructed d into [lo − P, hi − P]; the first encoder emits the one-step fixed point q* = Q(clamp(R(q))), r* = clamp(R(q*)) (proved per coefficient); REQUIRES a PREDICT-ONLY transform (interpolating (N,0) family, (2,0)/(4,0)/(6,0) Deslauriers–Dubuc; the update step creates the cycle that defeats capping and slows the legaliser); self-identifying reconstruction points r = sign(q)(|q| + β)Δ with β = m/2ᵏ, m odd → Δ read from any non-clamped nonzero coefficient by count-trailing-zeros (plan canonical without search; clamped coefficients excluded as "equal to interval boundary"); tie-break (coarsest step, fixed mode order) for bands with no signature, adopted inline by the first encoder; intra/inter identified from signatures of c and c − pred; sequence state by convention (frame 1 intra, bank empty, refresh phase from frame index); the first encoder emits what the canonical procedure returns on its own reconstruction; worst case decoder one inverse with a compare-clamp per sample, fresh encode one forward + one closed-loop quantise pass + ≤ 2 packs. Astray: legality as post-processing; plan as search; open-loop quantisation; the update step; bit-plane at the wrong layer. First measurement: predict-only (4,0)/(6,0) vs current, luma dB at equal bits — "decides whether the design is viable"; if it fails, no bounded proof exists for transforms with an update step. Appendix A: full lifting equations with clamps per level (horizontal-first 2-D structure, stages 1–4).
B (vibe): same principle (decode output a fixed point; one reconstruction pipeline shared by encoder and decoder; every decision computable from the decoded picture). KEEP the transform. Rate control feed-forward: budget = nominal + causal bank of ACTUAL prior-slice bits (canonical by induction); plan by LUT cost sums over nested power-of-two lattices derived by shifts from one quantisation (JPEG XS shape), decided FROM THE RECONSTRUCTION with a re-decision check; legality = our attempt-8 in-cell projection (convex: cell box ∩ legal preimage; alternating projection), K fixed + early exit, run by BOTH ends as the reconstruction; if the intersection is empty (dense rails) a deterministic ESCALATION LADDER coarsens the offending bands one power of two per rung, finite depth, invisible across hops (gen 2 recomputes the same coarse plan from the reconstruction); "the lock demands lattice points when cells suffice — replace the lattice test with an in-cell test" (the single cheapest fix); DELETE the display-side blend (a hidden contract across the hop) — handle the boundary in the transform with a cross-slice term computed from decoded rows, or self-contained slices; measure generation 3 and 10, both hop types. Astray: clip as decoder-only afterthought; plan from source then rediscovered; lattice-point lock; trial-encode rate control; blend patch; attempts 1–3 search for destroyed information; bit-plane abandoned for fixable reasons.
C (gemini): canonical plan via a bounded analysis-by-synthesis loop at gen 1 (plan → inverse + clip → rate control on the reconstruction → adopt the stable plan); legality by clipping inside the lifting steps (non-linear but invertible lifting); gen ≥ 2 one pass; flags the causal bank + 9/16 dead zone as a cascading dependency making plan reproduction impossible without search.
D (perplexity): a different codec — canonical legal-pixel coding (nested legal sample alphabets, causal reconstructed-neighbour prediction, fixed format-and-position-derived budgets and precision schedules, canonical padding); remove the cross-slice term and the reversible-undo blend from the correctness path; the syntax must admit exactly ONE representation per reachable decoded image and state; states plainly it cannot promise half-XS-rate quality; the hard part is rate allocation.
COORDINATOR SYNTHESIS against the record: CONSENSUS (A, B, C, D): legality inside the reconstruction loop, same at both ends, no pixel-domain clip after a lossy inverse; every decision canonical from the reconstruction, and the first encoder emits what the canonical procedure returns on its own reconstruction; the lattice-point lock is the wrong test (A: signatures; B: in-cell) — our Steps X/Z (cell-read, mode-aware) already confirm: roots 94–100 %; the display blend is suspect (B, D: remove; A: compatible) — our X4 measured it as the ONLY source of dng720's residual (81 samples). DISAGREEMENT on the transform: A requires predict-only — the RECORD answers it: DESIGN3 predict-only FALSIFIED at ~3 dB at every rate (S5.212 verdict; −3.67 dB), and the owner forbids any dB loss (2026-09-27) → A's structural premise is out as a whole-codec change; A's longer (4,0)/(6,0) predictors were never measured (DESIGN3 used 2-tap convex predictors), but the loss is attributed to the missing update (aliased low band), so recovery to 0 dB is implausible; A's other elements (self-identifying reconstruction points, one-step closed-loop requantisation, canonical emission order) are transform-independent and usable. B keeps the transform and turns our ICL into the core with a bounded ladder — consistent with our measurements. D is a different codec below the efficiency needed (1.33× vs 2× today). DESIGN CANDIDATE (to be written as DESIGN_CORE.md and adversarially reviewed): transform kept; ICL projection as THE reconstruction at both ends (K fixed, early exit), encoder references/statistics on it; the lock replaced by the canonical rule (mode-aware cell read + one predicate), and the first encoder runs that rule on its own reconstruction and emits its result (closed loop); bounded escalation ladder where the projection leaves residual out-of-range samples (the owner's eye decides any quality effect; bits only fall); seam handling moved into the invertible transform path (blend removed or made legal-safe) — seam visibility judged by eye; optional: self-identifying reconstruction points to make plan reading rank-free. FIRST MEASUREMENTS (before the design review): T1 canonical re-decision at gen 1 (how often the canonical rule on the gen-1 reconstruction differs from the open-loop plan; bits and quality of adopting it; then gen 2, gen 3 and gen 10 byte identity, both hops, on the suite); T2 escalation ladder on residual slices (natural spot/volley residuals and cut24/extrema): rungs used, residual → 0, bits, quality, renders.

### S5.365 — 2026-09-27 — SA14 NEST DESIGN delivered (Subagents/SA14_design/DESIGN.md, NOTES.md; notes/nests.py, enc3s.py; out/; numpy, intra). KEY IDEA — LEAF-READING LIFTING: every update step reads TRANSMITTED coefficient values (dequantised leaves), never clamped/final samples, so each predicted sample's legal interval depends only on final values → acyclic legal synthesis WITH the full symmetric 5/3 update; the separable 5/3 rewritten exactly so all four bands are coded coefficients: within ±0.5 % BD-rate of the separable 5/3 on every plane (dng, spot, floor, cf_gfx). This refutes the premise 'legality in synthesis ⇒ predict-only' (S5.349/S5.350/expert A), which assumed the update reads clamped values. Legality: per-sample windows (low-band windows shifted by the update, computed from the coefficients); a predicted sample lands strictly inside or is a RAIL± symbol exactly on the bound (fixed update value); encoder closure: synthesise; overshooting lattice samples move one step inward, index-0 ones become rails; repeat until none overshoots — terminates (monotone), measured ≤ 6 rounds (e.g. 903 → 227 → 65 → 4 → 1 changes), 0–0.06 % of samples touched on natural content; no pixel clip; 0 out-of-range. Exactness: reconstruction on qΔ (power-of-two, no offset; nested), next encoder inverts exactly, recognises rails on the bound, reads per band the coarsest step and cheapest mode that hold the values (one pass, no search); gen 1 emits that canonical description → g2 identical 21/21 (7 intra cells incl. 12-bit and limited synthetic rails × 3 rates); vectors derived at the encoder from decoded frames and TRANSMITTED; mode/refresh read from the picture. Seams: 'shifted causal slices' — each slice starts on a predicted row whose top neighbour is the slice above's final row; only the last low row's update is one-sided; no mirror/blend/lookahead; row ratio spot 1.05 (mirror 1.38), dng 1.36 with rows 0–1 +6 % (continuous 1.18, mirror 1.49); −3…−4 % bits, +0.2…0.4 dB vs mirror; parity rounding π removes a +0.6-code cast. Efficiency vs the same transform with plain clip: dng NEG 91.249 vs 91.248 identical bits; spot low rate NEG −0.04…−0.16 at +0.3…+1 % bits; synthetic rails −55…−63 % bits, PSNR +4…+7 dB. Weakest: closure has no proven small bound (≤ 6 measured).
